Pitch summary: Cook says his family's experience with the health system before his mother's death in 2024 led him to research practical ways to improve health-care efficiency and delivery. He joined CentreBC for its evidence-based policy and fiscal responsibility.
Key priorities: health-care efficiency and delivery; evidence-based policy; fiscal responsibility

Name: Brennan Day
Bio:
Brennan Day is a dedicated leader with a deep commitment to the Comox Valley, who served as the Executive Director of the Eureka Support Society. His extensive experience in business management and community service positions him as a key advocate for transformative change in the region.

A Longtime Resident and Advocate

A long-time resident of the Comox Valley, Brennan Day’s roots run deep in the community he passionately serves. His journey into leadership has been driven by a genuine desire to make a meaningful impact. Brennan’s background includes managing large-scale international projects and founding a successful industrial supply, manpower, and training firm. These experiences have provided him with unique insights into the diverse needs of the Comox Valley.

Champion of Mental Health and Community Well-Being

Brennan is a staunch advocate for addressing critical issues facing the Comox Valley. As Executive Director of the Eureka Support Society, he has led initiatives to enhance mental health support and community well-being. His dedication to these causes underscores his commitment to improving the quality of life for all residents.

A Multifaceted Career Path

Before focusing on community service, Brennan built a distinguished career in international project management and business. His work overseeing complex projects and driving organizational success has equipped him with the skills and knowledge necessary to tackle local challenges effectively.

Experience, Passion, and Vision

Brennan’s leadership is defined by a blend of experience, passion, and vision. His comprehensive background in both global and local contexts enables him to bridge gaps and drive positive change. Brennan is committed to implementing practical solutions to address homelessness, substance abuse, and mental health issues, aiming to restore stability and safety to the Courtenay-Comox community. With his proven ability to lead and transform organizations, Brennan is well-prepared to guide the Comox Valley toward a brighter and more prosperous future.
Pitch video title: Bill M233 - April 20, 2026 (Brennan Day for Courtenay-Comox)
Pitch summary: Day, first elected in 2024, rejoined the Conservatives on Sept 22 after leaving over Findlay's leadership, saying 'moderation has won out over division.' He says health care and seniors remain central (long-term care waitlists, ER closures, staffing, primary care), along with affordability, rebuilding resource industries and responding to U.S. economic threats. He is courting voters across party lines.
Key priorities: health care and seniors (long-term care waitlists, ER closures, staffing, primary care); affordability; rebuilding resource industries; economy / U.S. threats; homelessness, addiction and mental health
Quote: Regardless of how you have voted in the past, there is a place for you in this campaign. My responsibility has always been to represent the people of Courtenay–Comox, and that will not change.
Other media links: YouTube channel 'Brennan Day for Courtenay-Comox' (legislature clips)

Name: Jay Van Oostdam
Bio:
Jay Van Oostdam is a veterinarian, public health professional and longtime environmental advocate with decades of experience working on the connections between human health and the environment.

Jay was born in Yellowknife and grew up in Regina. He earned a Bachelor of Science in Biology from the University of Regina and later completed a Doctor of Veterinary Medicine at the University of Saskatchewan. He began practising veterinary medicine in Nanaimo and later worked across British Columbia and Saskatchewan.

He went on to complete post-doctoral work at the University of British Columbia’s Pulmonary Research Laboratory and a Master of Public Health in Environmental Health and Epidemiology at the University of Minnesota. That work led to a 25-year career with Health Canada and BC Environment studying environmental contaminants such as lead, mercury, PCBs and DDT and their impacts on human and environmental health.

During his time with Health Canada, Jay led the Human Health component of the federal Northern Contaminants Program, helping assess contaminant exposure in Arctic Canada and contributing to guidance for First Nations and Inuit communities on reducing exposure while safely maintaining traditional diets.

Jay also co-led the Human Health Assessment Group of the Arctic Monitoring and Assessment Program, working with scientists across the circumpolar region to better understand exposure to persistent organic pollutants. That work contributed scientific evidence used in the development of the Stockholm Convention on Persistent Organic Pollutants.

A longtime member of both the federal and provincial Green parties, Jay has been active in election campaigns and environmental advocacy for decades. He has also participated in direct actions to protect old-growth forests in Temagami, Ontario and at Fairy Creek in British Columbia.

Jay is running in Courtenay-Comox to bring his experience in public health, environmental science and advocacy into public service and to help strengthen the connection between healthy communities and a healthy environment.
Pitch summary: Van Oostdam, a veterinarian and former Health Canada environmental-health scientist, is running to bring public-health and environmental-science experience to protecting communities and the environment.
Key priorities: environmental protection; public health; link between healthy communities and healthy environment
Quote: I'm running to bring decades of experience in public health, environmental science and advocacy to the work of protecting our communities and our environment.

Name: Will Cole-Hamilton
Bio:
Will Cole-Hamilton: Standing firm for Courtenay-Comox

Will Cole-Hamilton is a strong advocate for the Comox Valley. As a former small business owner with a background in law, Will has been elected twice to Courtenay City Council and serves as Chair of the Comox Valley Regional District. He also led the creation of the Comox Valley Housing Authority which aims to build the affordable housing that people in the Comox Valley need to build good lives.

Will and his family live in Courtenay on the traditional territories of the K’ómoks First Nation. He knows that people in Courtenay-Comox need a government that is going to stand firm for them during this trade war.

Will Cole-Hamilton, David Eby and the BC NDP have a plan to stand up for BC, protect the services that families need, and build the homes, infrastructure and economy we need for a stronger province.
Pitch summary: Cole-Hamilton, Comox Valley Regional District chair and two-term Courtenay councillor who led creation of the Comox Valley Housing Authority, says the region needs protection for good jobs, stronger health care and a growing economy in a time of global uncertainty. He also lists protecting the environment.
Key priorities: protect good jobs; strengthen health care; grow the economy; affordable housing (Comox Valley Housing Authority); environment; stand up to U.S. trade war
Quote: At a time of global uncertainty, we need to protect good jobs, strengthen healthcare, grow our economy and stand up for British Columbia.

Name: James Chumsa
Pitch summary: No individual pitch found. Confirmed Communist Party of BC candidate.

Name: Bert Chen
Bio:
Bert Chen is a small business owner on Vancouver Island that is running to represent the Cowichan Valley and bring his experience with BC’s industrial sector and mill towns to Victoria.

A lifelong British Columbian, Bert grew up in a rural community where his family ran a small gas station and his first job was working behind the pump. Bert has seen the effect of our once strong resource economy diminished due to overly long permitting processes and knows that we need to grow BC’s economy by fast tracking projects to provide decent, stable jobs for hardworking British Columbians.

Throughout his career, he has worked in small remote communities across Canada, including BC and the North, including many where he was honoured to work with First Nations in developing critical infrastructure projects to support communities.

As the owner of a local Vancouver Island firm that provides project management and construction services for power plants and other large industries across Canada, he has worked to build clean power projects around the world, including those on Vancouver Island and the BC Coast.

Alongside his work, Bert has served with the Elks of Canada and the BC Elks Association as its long time finance director, helping to manage the charitable organization and its kids camps across the province.

In his leisure time, Bert and his wife enjoy sailing off Maple Bay.
Pitch summary: Chen, a Vancouver Island project-management and construction business owner, says B.C.'s resource economy has been diminished by long permitting processes and that projects should be fast-tracked to provide stable jobs. He wants to bring his industrial and mill-town experience to Victoria.
Key priorities: fast-track project permitting; resource economy and stable jobs; mill towns; infrastructure with First Nations

Name: Justin Douglas
Bio:
Justin Douglas is a small-business owner, lawyer by training, and community advocate running to represent the Cowichan Valley. Raised on Vancouver Island by a single mother, Justin proudly calls the Cowichan Valley home and is committed to making sure local communities have a strong voice in the decisions that affect their lives.

Justin is the co-founder of EMBER Studios Duncan and VIT Management. As a local entrepreneur, he understands firsthand the realities of running a small business, creating opportunities, supporting workers, and contributing to the community.

He holds a degree in Political Science from the University of Victoria and degrees in both Common Law and Civil Law from McGill University. His legal and community experience includes work in immigration and refugee law, legal information services, restorative justice, and non-profit organizations.

Justin has also worked on community development initiatives involving ecotourism, infrastructure, access to safe drinking water, and youth engagement. His writing has addressed issues including the criminalization of poverty and the importance of including Indigenous legal perspectives in Canadian legal education.

Justin is running because he believes government should be accountable to the people it serves. His priorities include strengthening public services and social programs, protecting the environment, supporting a fair economy, and ensuring people across the Cowichan Valley are represented in the decisions that shape their future.
Pitch summary: Douglas, a Duncan small-business owner trained in law, says government should be accountable to the people it serves. His priorities are stronger public services and social programs, environmental protection, a fair economy and real representation for Cowichan Valley residents.
Key priorities: public services and social programs; environment; fair economy; accountable government / local voice
Quote: I want to ensure that the people of the Cowichan Valley have a strong voice in the decisions that affect their lives.

Name: Debra Toporowski
Bio:
Debra Toporowski is on your side in Cowichan Valley.

A member of the Cowichan Tribes, Debra Toporowski (Qwulti’stunaat) is a two term elected councillor in the municipality of North Cowichan and a five time councillor of Cowichan Tribes — the first elected woman in these communities to hold both positions on two councils at the same time. Born to a First Nations mother and Chinese father, Debra is a champion for Indigenous watersheds and the services people count on in the Cowichan Valley.

She knows people in the Cowichan Valley are facing the same big challenges so many people across BC are facing: housing, healthcare, and affordability. She and David Eby’s BC NDP team are on your side so we can keep building more housing, improving healthcare services, and making life more affordable.

Debra knows this government is looking out for people in Cowichan Valley. Under David Eby and the BC NDP this government is building a new Cowichan District hospital, a new Cowichan secondary school, while lowering ICBC costs for drivers, and increasing the minimum wage. You can count on them to fight for you and your family.
Pitch summary: Toporowski (Qwulti'stunaat), first elected in 2024 and parliamentary secretary for rural health, is a Cowichan Tribes member and former North Cowichan councillor. Her page says she champions Indigenous watersheds and services, and her campaign emphasizes housing, health care, cost of living and the impact of U.S. trade tensions.
Key priorities: housing; health care / rural health; affordability; Indigenous watersheds; U.S. trade impacts; good jobs

Name: Kuldeep Rangi
Bio:
Kuldeep Rangi is deeply connected to the Delta North community and has been actively involved in local organizations, sports, and community activities. His children are active in the community through hockey and soccer, while Kuldeep regularly participates in pickleball, tennis, and other activities with local residents.

Kuldeep is a successful business owner who operates a real estate marketing brokerage. He also brings nearly a decade of banking experience with Scotiabank and First West Credit Union, giving him valuable experience in business, finance, and working with families and local businesses.

Kuldeep is stepping forward because he believes Delta North deserves a strong local voice and practical leadership focused on the needs of the community.
Pitch video title: Kuldeep Rangi, CentreBC MLA Candidate for Delta North
Pitch summary: Real estate marketing brokerage owner with nearly a decade of banking experience (Scotiabank, First West). His party bio says he is running because Delta North deserves a strong local voice and practical leadership focused on community needs. A CentreBC campaign video was posted Oct 2, 2026.
Key priorities: strong local voice for Delta North; practical community-focused leadership; business and finance experience
Quote: Kuldeep is stepping forward because he believes Delta North deserves a strong local voice and practical leadership focused on the needs of the community.

Name: Monica Mohan
Bio:
Monica Mohan is the BC Conservative Party candidate for Delta North.

Monica is a practicing lawyer in British Columbia and a resident of North Delta. Born and raised in Vancouver, Monica grew up in an immigrant family, with her parents having roots in India and Fiji. In addition to English, Monica is fluent in Punjabi and Hindi. Her family background has shaped her appreciation for diverse communities and given her an understanding of the challenges families can encounter, including the barriers they may face as they build their lives in Canada.

She graduated with honours from Pennsylvania State University (Penn State) with a degree in Administration of Justice before pursuing her law degree in the United States, where she was awarded an academic scholarship. Her professional experience in law, public service, and community organizations has shaped her perspective on issues affecting individuals, families, and communities.

Before becoming a lawyer, Monica worked in civilian roles with the Vancouver Police Department and the Guelph Police Service, gaining firsthand exposure to the criminal justice system.

Monica is committed to access to justice, meaningful community engagement, and ensuring that people feel heard and understood when navigating public institutions and systems. Her professional and community experiences have reinforced her belief in the importance of public service, accountability, and practical solutions to the challenges facing individuals and families.

As a lawyer and community-minded professional, Monica brings a perspective grounded in legal experience, service, advocacy, and a desire to contribute meaningfully to her community.

Outside of her professional and community work, Monica enjoys spending time with her family and exploring local parks and outdoor spaces together.
Pitch summary: North Delta lawyer, formerly in civilian roles with the Vancouver Police and Guelph Police, and a former victim advocate. Her party page says she is committed to access to justice, community engagement, accountability and practical solutions. She first registered as unaffiliated before being listed as the Conservative candidate.
Key priorities: access to justice; meaningful community engagement; accountability in public institutions; practical solutions for families
Quote: Monica is committed to access to justice, meaningful community engagement, and ensuring that people feel heard and understood when navigating public institutions and systems.

Name: Todd Schierling
Bio:
Building a stronger economy and province for Delta North

Todd Schierling has spent his career keeping people safe. He is President of the BC Professional Firefighters’ Association and a Suppression Fire Captain with Surrey Fire Service, where he has served since 1996.

He also spends his off hours making his community stronger. A committed community volunteer, Todd helped launch the Surrey FF Goodwill Senior Girls High School Basketball Tournament in 2001, which has provided more than $125,000 in bursaries to female student-athletes.

Todd has also served on the BC Municipal Pension Plan, BC Federation of Labour Executive Council, BC First Responders Mental Health Committee, and on national academic working groups focused on firefighter cancer research and early detection.

Todd Schierling, David Eby and the BC NDP will stand up for families, protect people and the services they count on, and build a stronger economy and province, so that everyone can build a good life.
Pitch summary: President of the BC Professional Fire Fighters' Association and a Surrey fire captain since 1996, endorsed by outgoing MLA Ravi Kahlon. He frames his run around the U.S. trade war: standing up for Canadian jobs, protecting public services and investing in the community.
Key priorities: stand up for Canadian jobs amid Trump trade war; protect public services; keep investing in communities; firefighter/first-responder health (background)
Quote: Things are tough right now, and Donald Trump’s trade war is putting more pressure on families and workers in Delta. We need to stand up for Canadian jobs, protect the services people rely on and keep investing in our communities.

Name: Ian Paton
Bio:
Ian Paton is a lifelong resident of Delta South and a dedicated public servant, currently serving as the MLA for Delta South since 2017. He lives on his family farm in Delta with his wife, Pam.

Career

Ian has over 30 years of experience running and owning a dairy farm and farm auction business, which has provided him with extensive agricultural knowledge. He was elected as a Delta Councillor in 2010, where he chaired key committees such as the Agricultural Advisory Committee and the Dikes and Drainage Committee. As an MLA, Ian has served on the Select Standing Committees on Health and Agriculture, Fish and Food, and has been the Shadow Minister for Agriculture and Food.

Community Involvement

Ian is deeply involved in his community, having served as the past president of the East Delta Community Hall Society and as a volunteer firefighter with Hall 4. He has also contributed to various local organizations, including the Delta Hospital Foundation, REACH Child and Youth Development Society, and the Delta Farmland and Wildlife Trust.
Pitch summary: Delta South MLA since 2017 and a dairy farmer. He left the Conservatives in August over the party's direction, briefly joined CentreBC, and rejoined under interim leader Lorne Doerkson when the election was called. He describes himself as fiscally conservative and socially moderate, and says the province faces serious debt and a collapsed resource sector.
Key priorities: fiscal responsibility / debt; resource sector recovery; delayed projects (incl. Massey Tunnel replacement criticism); agriculture; uniting centre-right
Quote: So, for everyone wondering where I stand, let me be clear: I am fiscally conservative. I am socially moderate. And I will stand by those principles - every single time.

Name: Skadi Green
Pitch summary: No individual pitch found. No party page, bio or news coverage was found for this candidate.

Name: Jason McCormick
Bio:
Jason McCormick: On your side in Delta South.

Jason McCormick has fought for better public and active transportation for more than a decade. A bus driver for TransLink and community leader, Jason is extremely active in the BC cycling community and the South Delta Basketball Association, growing the latter to more than 400 youth participants.

Families in Delta South and across BC are facing real challenges, and Jason McCormick and the BC NDP are ready to take them on: building homes for people, strengthening our public healthcare system, and making day-to-day life more affordable.

Jason McCormick, David Eby and the BC NDP team are on your side and ready to take on the big challenges facing your community.
Pitch summary: TransLink bus driver, union activist and transit/cycling advocate from Ladner who ran against Paton in 2024 and federally in 2025. He says working people face higher costs and uncertainty from the trade war and wants to make it easier to get to work, support local jobs and create opportunities for young people.
Key priorities: public and active transportation; good local jobs; opportunities for young people; costs amid trade war
Quote: We need to make it easier for people to get to work, support good local jobs and create more opportunities for young people. I’ve spent my career doing that work in Delta, and I’m ready to take it to the legislature.

Name: Jim McMurtry
Bio:
Jim McMurtry was born and raised in Toronto, the son of a former Chief Justice of Ontario and Order of Canada recipient.

He is an award-winning teacher who gained renown for standing against the exploitation of schoolchildren for political advantage. Fired by the Abbotsford School District in 2023 for speaking honestly about residential schools, he has become a nationally recognized voice on the failure of Indigenous policy, the defamation of the dead in Canadian history, and the defence of fundamental Canadian values.

His professional résumé is impressive. He holds a Ph.D. in Educational Theory from the University of Toronto and has served as a teacher, principal, and college lecturer over four decades. He has been committed to a life of service at school as a coach, club supervisor, and organizer of events for students with disabilities.

In addition to his love for and commitment to teaching and his country, Jim has built a thriving family, including his wife, a retired vice-principal, his three children and their spouses, all of whom are lawyers, and his seven grandchildren who live nearby.

Jim has deep ties to the South Delta riding, where he resides with his wife and family.

Nobody who has met Jim can doubt his love for this province and this country. Jim is running to reaffirm all that is positive about our province and our country, and he is running to preserve British Columbia’s beautiful and glorious heritage.
Pitch video title: B.C. Politics EXPOSED? Jim McMurtry on KLF, the Conservative Revolt & What Really Happened (Chanteh Podcast)
Pitch summary: Retired teacher and principal fired by the Abbotsford School District in 2023 over comments on residential schools; also running for Delta school trustee on Oct 17. His OneBC page says he is running to reaffirm what is positive about the province and preserve B.C.'s heritage. He hosts his own YouTube channel.
Key priorities: defence of 'fundamental Canadian values'; Indigenous policy critique; education/schools; preserving B.C. heritage
Quote: Jim is running to reaffirm all that is positive about our province and our country, and he is running to preserve British Columbia’s beautiful and glorious heritage.

Name: Sid Tobias
Bio:
Sid Tobias is a decorated Canadian Armed Forces veteran, experienced public servant, and municipal leader with deep roots in Esquimalt–Colwood.

Born in Esquimalt, Sid served nearly 25 years in the Canadian Armed Forces, much of that time based at CFB Esquimalt. His distinguished military career included receiving the Meritorious Service Medal for his role in integrating Canadian, NORAD, and U.S. forces in support of the 2010 Olympic Games. He also served as chair of a NATO working group.

Following his military service, Sid spent more than a decade working in the B.C. Public Service, bringing his experience in leadership, collaboration, and public administration to the provincial level.

In 2022, Sid was elected Mayor of View Royal and became a director with the Capital Regional District. As mayor, he has focused on practical, community-based solutions, including advancing View Royal’s first comprehensive Official Community Plan update since 2011, supporting efforts to establish a primary-care clinic for residents without a family doctor, and helping re-establish an ambulance station in the community.

At the regional level, Sid has worked to strengthen cooperation among municipalities, First Nations, regional governments, and other partners, including efforts surrounding the future of the E&N rail corridor.

Sid believes British Columbia needs stable, practical and collaborative government focused on delivering results rather than increasing political division. His priorities include housing, health care, transportation, infrastructure and affordability, with an emphasis on governments working together to address the challenges facing communities.

With decades of military, provincial and municipal public service, Sid brings extensive leadership experience and a lifelong commitment to serving the communities of Esquimalt–Colwood.

Sign up to stay informed and receive news from CentreBC:
Pitch summary: Outgoing View Royal mayor and CRD director, a 25-year Canadian Armed Forces veteran and former provincial public servant. He says Eby's snap election brought him out of planned retirement; his bio highlights a primary-care clinic effort, re-establishing an ambulance station and View Royal's OCP update.
Key priorities: primary care access; ambulance/emergency services; regional cooperation; practical community-based solutions
Quote: From my perspective, they are amazing leaders. It is literally building an airplane while it’s in flight, but the team is doing an incredible job to field some high-quality candidates that offer a good platform.

Name: Dave Johnston
Bio:
Dave Johnston is the Conservative Party of BC candidate for Esquimalt-Colwood.

The son of two public school teachers, Dave was born in Prince Rupert, raised in Campbell River, and now calls Colwood home. For the past decade, he has served in the Canadian Armed Forces as a Canadian Ranger.

After studying at Camosun College and living in Victoria for several years, Dave obtained his Red Seal as an electrician from BCIT and began working in BCs North at Mount Milligan. The Rio Tinto Alcan upgrade project then brought Dave to Kitimat, where he founded the nonprofit organization, The North Matters, to advocate for responsible resource development. For over three years, Dave worked with the Haisla Nation managing capital projects and assets.

Dave understands the issues facing both rural and urban communities in BC, and is eager to address the needs of Esquimalt-Colwood residents. An avid outdoors enthusiast, Dave enjoys hiking and camping with his three dogs: Boss, Apollo, and Loki. When not exploring the beaches and forests of the South Island, Dave can be found cooking up new recipes in his home kitchen and attending local events.
Pitch summary: Red Seal electrician and Canadian Ranger from Colwood who worked at Mount Milligan, on the Kitimat Rio Tinto upgrade and with the Haisla Nation; founded the nonprofit The North Matters for responsible resource development. His party page says he understands rural and urban issues and is eager to address residents' needs; no specific promises listed.
Key priorities: responsible resource development (background); rural and urban community needs
Quote: Dave understands the issues facing both rural and urban communities in BC, and is eager to address the needs of Esquimalt-Colwood residents.

Name: Sidney Coles
Bio:
Sidney Coles is a journalist, communications professional, researcher, and former public servant running to represent Esquimalt-Colwood. Her career has focused on environmental justice, human rights, Indigenous issues, gender equity, and building stronger, more inclusive communities.

Based in Victoria, Sidney has worked as a freelance journalist since 2021, including two years as a Local Journalism Initiative reporter with Capital Daily. Her reporting has appeared in Ricochet Media, the Watershed Sentinel, Canada’s National Observer, the Toronto Star, the Hamilton Spectator, and Women and Climate, with a particular focus on climate change, environmental justice, and Indigenous land rights in British Columbia.

Sidney has also worked closely with Indigenous leadership in British Columbia. As External Communications Manager for the Gitanyow Hereditary Chiefs, she supported communications on land governance, resource development, and Indigenous rights. Earlier in her career, she worked internationally on climate and gender equity, including evaluating environmental grant-making across sub-Saharan Africa and advising on gender and resource governance initiatives.

Her public-service experience includes senior policy and program roles with the Ontario government. At the Ministry of Education, Sidney evaluated programs supporting Indigenous children and youth and children in care. At the Ministry of the Status of Women, she helped manage an employment program designed to reduce barriers facing Indigenous, racialized, and newcomer women entering skilled trades, technology, and entrepreneurship.

Sidney has also worked in humanitarian and international development settings, including with Doctors Without Borders in the Democratic Republic of Congo and on a psychosocial support initiative for refugee mothers and young children in Türkiye.

She holds two PhDs from the University of Toronto. She completed a PhD in Comparative Literature in 2008 and a PhD in Applied Psychology and Human Development in 2024, with research focused on women’s empowerment and the gendered impacts of mining in international development. Sidney was also nominated for a Rhodes Scholarship at McMaster University and held a Junior Fellowship at Massey College.

As a reporter in the Capital Regional District, Sidney has developed a close understanding of the challenges facing local municipalities and communities. She is running to bring that experience to public life with a focus on evidence-based policy, environmental responsibility, reconciliation, accountable government, and ensuring Esquimalt-Colwood remains a place where people and families can feel welcome, safe, and able to thrive.
Pitch video title: Policy Announcement: Regulate AI (w/ Sidney Coles, David Evans, Andrew Appleton and Carolyn Howe) (BC Greens)
Pitch summary: Journalist (former Capital Daily reporter), researcher and former Ontario public servant with two PhDs. Her party page says she is running with a focus on evidence-based policy, environmental responsibility, reconciliation and accountable government. She appeared in a BC Greens policy announcement on regulating AI.
Key priorities: evidence-based policy; environmental responsibility; reconciliation; accountable government; regulating AI (party message)
Quote: I want to support Esquimalt and Colwood in continuing to be places where people and their families feel welcome, safe, and are able to thrive.

Name: Darlene Rotchford
Bio:
Darlene Rotchford: building up a stronger Esquimalt-Colwood

Darlene Rotchford has been fighting for people for her entire career. Elected as the MLA for Esquimalt-Colwood in 2024, she proudly served as the Parliamentary Secretary for Armed Forces Development and Veterans’ Affairs.

Prior to provincial politics, as an elected councillor in Esquimalt, she’s fought for homes for people. And as President of the Victoria Labour Council, she took on powerful interests on behalf of working families, fighting for good wages and working conditions. In her professional life, she took on tough challenges in mental health and addictions, working to ensure people get the treatment they need so they can get well.

Darlene Rotchford, David Eby and the BC NDP have a plan to stand up for our province, protect people and services, and build a stronger economy, so you can build a good life in the community you love.
Pitch video title: "We need stability right now:" Esquimalt-Colwood BC NDP incumbent seeking re-election #BCpoli (CFAX 1070)
Pitch summary: MLA since 2024 and parliamentary secretary for armed forces development and veterans' affairs; former Esquimalt councillor and Victoria Labour Council president. She is seeking re-election arguing for stability, and has spoken on B.C. shipbuilding capacity.
Key priorities: stability; armed forces/veterans and shipbuilding; housing; working families and wages; mental health and addictions treatment
Quote: Darlene Rotchford: building up a stronger Esquimalt-Colwood

Name: Tony Luck
Bio:
About

Tony Luck is a dedicated leader, community advocate, and the Conservative Party of British Columbia MLA for Fraser-Nicola. Born and raised in British Columbia, Tony has a deep connection to the region and a passion for serving its residents. With a diverse background spanning finance, public service, and community engagement, Tony is committed to bringing positive change to Fraser-Nicola.

Proven Experience

Tony’s extensive career includes a decade as a financial planner, 26 years with BC Hydro, and his current role as a professional realtor. He has also served as a councillor on Mission City council and held leadership positions within the Fraser Valley Regional District and the Southern Interior Local Government Association (SILGA). Tony’s wealth of experience demonstrates his commitment to effective governance and community service.

Community Involvement

Tony is actively involved in various community organizations, including the Chamber of Commerce, Community Futures Nicola Valley, and the UFV Alumni Association. He believes in the power of grassroots initiatives to drive positive change and has dedicated his time to volunteering and supporting local causes. Tony’s community involvement reflects his deep-rooted commitment to the well-being of Fraser-Nicola residents.

Key Goals

Tony’s key goals for Fraser-Nicola center around transparency, accountability, and fiscal responsibility in government. He aims to implement fair taxation policies that support economic growth and alleviate the burden on working-class families. Additionally, Tony is a passionate advocate for affordable housing and healthcare reform, seeking practical solutions to address these pressing issues. Through engagement with medical professionals and community stakeholders, Tony aims to improve access to quality healthcare services for all residents of Fraser-Nicola.

With a proven track record of leadership, community involvement, and a commitment to addressing the needs of Fraser-Nicola residents, Tony Luck is serving as a strong voice in the BC Legislature.
Pitch summary: First elected in 2024 with about 54% of the vote; former Merritt and Mission councillor, BC Hydro employee and realtor. If re-elected he wants to revive forestry, grow tourism and look after riding infrastructure, with health care and affordability as priorities. He launched his campaign Sept 30 in Merritt.
Key priorities: revive forestry; increase tourism; infrastructure care; health care; affordability; fiscal responsibility and fair taxation (party page)
Quote: I am looking forward to (continuing) to serve the people of Fraser-Nicola. I’m really excited about that.

Name: Patrick Michell
Bio:
Patrick Michell is the retired Chief of T’eqt”aqtn’mux (Kanaka Bar Indian Band) and a lifelong resident of the Fraser Canyon. His career spans law, Indigenous governance, renewable energy, economic development, community safety and climate resilience.

Patrick graduated from the Administrative Management program at Douglas College in 1989 and from the University of British Columbia’s law program in 1993. He began his professional career working on Aboriginal Fisheries Strategy agreements and later served as a Lands Officer with Indigenous and Northern Affairs Canada. After completing his legal articles, he practised law in Lytton from 1997 to 2005.

In 2005, Patrick shifted his focus toward community development and renewable energy. He became closely involved with the Kwoiek Hydro project, a renewable energy initiative first developed by Kanaka Bar Indian Band. He later served as Community Liaison, Lands and Economic Development Officer and, from 2015 to 2022, Chief of Kanaka Bar Indian Band.

During his time in leadership, Patrick also served in a number of advisory and director roles related to climate policy, clean energy, agriculture, finance, Indigenous health and economic development. These included appointments to the BC Climate Solutions Council, the BC Centre for Innovation and Clean Energy, the Fraser Basin Council, the BC Indigenous Advisory Council on Agriculture and the BC Real Estate Foundation.

His commitment to climate resilience is also deeply personal. Patrick and his family were evacuated during the 2021 Lytton fire and, like many people across the Fraser Canyon, experienced the displacement, infrastructure damage and repeated extreme weather that followed. From 2023 to 2025, he served as Rebuild Director for Lytton First Nations, focusing on rebuilding and strengthening community and regional resilience.

Today, Patrick continues to provide contracted services and speak publicly on climate change, resilience and community development. He believes the future of the Fraser-Nicola region depends on combining Indigenous knowledge, modern science and technology, strong local leadership and long-term investment in community safety.

Patrick is running to bring decades of experience in law, governance, renewable energy and climate resilience to the people of Fraser-Nicola and to help build communities that are safer, stronger and better prepared for the future.
Pitch summary: Retired Chief of Kanaka Bar Indian Band, lawyer and renewable-energy and climate-resilience leader, evacuated in the 2021 Lytton fire and later Rebuild Director for Lytton First Nations. He is running on climate resilience and community safety, combining Indigenous knowledge with science and technology.
Key priorities: climate resilience and wildfire/extreme-weather recovery; community safety; renewable energy; Indigenous knowledge and governance; strong local leadership
Quote: The future of the Fraser-Nicola region depends on combining Indigenous knowledge, modern science and technology, strong local leadership and long-term investment in community safety.

Name: Jason Leboe
Pitch summary: District of Hope utilities operator, secretary-treasurer of the Fraser Valley Labour Council and CUPE member. He argues public services and infrastructure are the foundation of good jobs, investment and strong rural economies.
Key priorities: public services in rural communities; infrastructure; supporting workers; good jobs and investment in rural B.C.
Quote: Public services are the lifeblood of rural communities. We can’t have good jobs, new investment and strong local economies without the public services and infrastructure that make them possible.

Name: Jeff Brown
Pitch summary: No individual pitch found. Listed as the Christian Heritage Party candidate in Times Colonist's final candidate list; not on the CHP BC 2026 candidates page.

Name: Mike Hicks
Bio:
Mike Hicks is the Conservative Party of BC candidate for Juan de Fuca–Malahat

Mike has called this community home for 28 years, building businesses, raising his family and serving the people of the region. A graduate of BCIT’s Hotel Management program, Mike’s career has included forestry, tourism, hospitality and the recreational fishing industry. He has managed resorts and owned and operated fishing lodges in coastal communities including Hakai Pass, Sointula, Bamfield and Port Renfrew. Today, Mike and his wife Kathy operate Arbutus Cove Guesthouse in Sooke.

Mike’s commitment to his community led him into public service. For 13 years, he served as the elected Capital Regional District Director for the Juan de Fuca Electoral Area, representing East Sooke, Otter Point, Shirley, Jordan River, Port Renfrew, Malahat and Willis Point. During his time in office, Mike worked directly with residents, businesses, First Nations, community organizations and all levels of government to deliver practical results for the communities he represented.

His record includes advocating for the East Sooke Fire Hall, replacement of the Roche Cove Bridge, Highway 14 access from Gillespie Road, Sooke’s artificial turf field, the Charters River salmon hatchery, the Sooke Regional Library and the acquisition of important regional parkland. Mike also spearheaded efforts to improve cellular and emergency communications along Highway 14, helping bring seven new cellular towers to approximately 70 kilometres of the corridor.

As the Conservative Party of BC candidate for Juan de Fuca–Malahat, Mike brings decades of business experience, 13 years of elected public service and a deep understanding of the communities he seeks to represent. He is committed to listening to residents, standing up for rural and coastal communities, and working for practical solutions that make life more affordable, strengthen public safety and ensure government is accountable to the people it serves.
Pitch video title: BC Conservatives running former long-time Juan de Fuca area director #yyj #BCpoli (CFAX 1070)
Pitch summary: Sooke guesthouse owner and former fishing lodge operator who served 13 years as CRD director for Juan de Fuca Electoral Area. His party page cites his record on local projects (East Sooke fire hall, Roche Cove bridge, Highway 14 cell towers) and pledges to stand up for rural and coastal communities.
Key priorities: rural and coastal communities; affordability; public safety; accountable government; Highway 14 safety/cell coverage (record)
Quote: He is committed to listening to residents, standing up for rural and coastal communities, and working for practical solutions that make life more affordable, strengthen public safety and ensure government is accountable to the people it serves.

Name: David Evans
Bio:
David Evans is running to serve as MLA because he believes British Columbians deserve better representation and a government focused on improving people’s lives and strengthening their communities.

Born and raised on Vancouver Island by a mill-working father and a school trustee mother, David has deep roots in the region. He graduated from high school in Victoria before attending university in Toronto and later spending several years working in Vancouver.

David’s career has taken him through broadcasting, writing, community service, and entrepreneurship. In Vancouver, he worked in radio, freelanced for magazines, and served as Distribution Supervisor at the Vancouver Food Bank.

For most of the past four decades, David has been self-employed. He founded Victoria’s first Zero Impact landscaping company and later built a successful community hub, café, and bakery that employed up to 20 people across three locations before its operations were transferred to a community co-operative in 2023.

Today, David operates a retail and wholesale coffee roasting business in Sooke, where he has lived, farmed, gardened, and raised three daughters. His experience as a parent, small business owner, employer, and community member has given him a firsthand understanding of the pressures facing families, workers, and local businesses.

David believes government should serve people rather than powerful corporate interests. He is concerned about rising inequality, the loss of good-paying jobs, and the long-term sustainability of B.C.’s resources, and he is running to advocate for an economy and government that put communities first.

David holds an Applied Arts Degree from Toronto Metropolitan University. He previously ran as a BC Green candidate in the 2024 provincial election, finishing third in a historic outcome for BC Greens.
Pitch video title: Policy Announcement: Regulate AI (w/ Sidney Coles, David Evans, Andrew Appleton and Carolyn Howe) (BC Greens)
Pitch summary: Sooke coffee roaster and former café/bakery owner who ran in 2024 and finished third. He says government should serve people rather than corporations, and is concerned about inequality, loss of good-paying jobs and the sustainability of B.C.'s resources.
Key priorities: government that serves people not corporations; inequality; good-paying jobs; sustainable resource use; small business; regulating AI (party message)
Quote: Government needs to remember that it serves real people, not corporations.

Name: Dana Lajeunesse
Bio:
Standing up for families in Juan de Fuca-Malahat

Elected MLA for Juan de Fuca-Malahat in 2024, Dana Lajeunesse has deep roots on southern Vancouver Island. He served as Parliamentary Secretary for Accessibility, he worked to advance accessibility and inclusion for people with disabilities across British Columbia.

A longtime resident of Sooke, he spent his childhood in Jordan River, expecting to grow up and work in the forestry industry, like his Dad and his Grandfather before him. Then, in 1989, a life-altering injury at work changed everything.

Unable to continue working in forestry, Dana went back to school. He earned a degree from Camosun College in Mechanical Engineering Technology, and worked in the industry for twenty four years. He built strong connections in his community, serving on the Mayor’s Advisory panel for economic development and Sooke Region Chamber’s Board of Directors. He was elected to the District of Sooke Council in 2019, and re-elected in 2022.

Dana Lajeunesse, David Eby and the BC NDP have a plan to stand up for our province, protect people and the services they count on, and build a stronger economy and province.
Pitch summary: MLA since 2024 (won by 141 votes) and parliamentary secretary for accessibility; former Sooke councillor and mechanical engineering technologist whose forestry career ended with a 1989 workplace injury. For this campaign he is highlighting health-care access, transportation, affordability and support for local businesses and workers.
Key priorities: health-care access; transportation (incl. road safety, Xavier's law); affordability; local businesses and workers; accessibility
Quote: Dana Lajeunesse, David Eby and the BC NDP have a plan to stand up for our province, protect people and the services they count on, and build a stronger economy and province.

Name: Shane Friesen
Pitch summary: No individual pitch found. Listed on Elections BC's candidate list and Times Colonist's final list; no OneBC page, bio or coverage found.

Name: Peter Milobar
Bio:
Peter Milobar is a dedicated Conservative MLA for Kamloops Centre with deep roots in the Kamloops community, where he lives with his wife Lianne and their three grown children. Together, they operate a local small business, reflecting their commitment to the local economy and community engagement. Peter’s longstanding connection to Kamloops is matched by his passion for public service and his active involvement in community life.

Career

Peter Milobar’s career in politics and public service spans over two decades, marked by significant roles and achievements. Elected MLA for Kamloops-North Thompson in 2017 and 2020, and current MLA for Kamloops Centre, elected in 2024. Most recently serving as Shadow Minister for Finance, Peter has a strong focus on fiscal responsibility and economic development. His previous roles include serving as Opposition House Leader and Shadow Minister for Indigenous Relations and Reconciliation, Environment and Climate Change. Before his provincial role, Peter was the Mayor of Kamloops for three terms, where he demonstrated leadership and commitment to local governance. He also served as chair of the Thompson Regional Hospital District for five terms and as a director for the Thompson-Nicola Regional District since 2005. His extensive experience extends to work with the BC Transit Board of Directors, PRIMECorp, and the Local Government Contract Management Committee.
Pitch summary: Three-term former Kamloops mayor and MLA since 2017, most recently Conservative finance critic. He left the party in August, briefly led CentreBC, and returned when Findlay resigned, saying the party is again a 'serious, stable alternative'. Locally he points to school capital needs, the promised Red Bridge replacement, health care, crime and street safety, and affordability.
Key priorities: school capital investment; Red Bridge replacement; health care (incl. Kamloops cancer centre); crime and safety; affordability; fiscal responsibility
Quote: A lack of investment in our school system, in terms of the capital needs of the school district. Where is that Red Bridge we were promised in the last election by David Eby? To healthcare issues that continue to challenge not just Kamloops but the surrounding area, to crime and safety on our streets, and the affordability crisis.

Name: Annelise Beach
Pitch summary: No individual pitch found. Named as the BC Green candidate in Castanet and CFJC final-list coverage; no party page or bio found.

Name: Mike Wisla
Pitch summary: Political newcomer, 64, a former Ashcroft teacher and senior labour relations officer (occupational health and safety) with the Health Sciences Association. He says he is running because he saw a need and wants Kamloops represented in government so work already started can continue.
Key priorities: Kamloops representation in government; continuing work already started; NDP majority stability
Quote: A lot of work has started, we got to keep that work going and I want to make sure Kamloops is represented in that.

Name: Rocky McAfee
Pitch summary: No individual pitch found. Confirmed as OneBC candidate in Castanet/CFJC final-list coverage; OneBC candidate page not found.

Name: Thaelo Proctor
Pitch summary: 23-year-old carpenter with no political experience running a 'service-first' campaign, offering free odd jobs to voters to show politicians should stay present in their communities. He calls his politics 'no-nonsense progressivism' and is considering higher taxes on the very wealthy and large corporations to cut taxes for lower-income people.
Key priorities: politicians present in their communities; volunteering/community service; higher taxes on the very wealthy and large corporations; lower taxes for lower-income people
Quote: It's unlikely that I will win. But I think voting for me on either side is a vote toward showing people in our community that we are tired of the status quo.

Name: Ward Stamer
Bio:
About Ward

Ward Stamer, a devoted husband to his beloved wife Carleen and a proud father of two adult children and three grandchildren, has deep roots in Barriere, where he has called home since his youth. With a career spanning many years in the forest industry, Ward’s commitment to his community is unwavering.

Leadership and Community Involvement 

Ward’s dedication to public service began long before his mayoral tenure, serving as Chairman to the Barriere Improvement District, overseeing essential services such as solid waste management, streetlights, water, and fire services. His leadership continued as he was elected to Barriere’s first Council upon incorporation, eventually earning the trust of the community to serve as Mayor in 2018 and subsequently re-elected in 2022.

As a Lions Club member for over three decades, Ward embodies the motto “We Serve,” which reflects his lifelong dedication to his community and its people. During his two terms as Mayor, Ward has confronted the challenges faced by municipalities head-on, prioritizing critical issues such as healthcare access, affordable housing, and senior care.

Under Ward’s leadership, significant infrastructure improvements have been realized, including enhanced water system capacity and the expansion of the business and industrial park sectors, providing localized employment opportunities for residents.

Commitment to Kamloops-North Thompson

Healthcare Access: Ward advocates for streamlining accreditation processes to attract and retain medical professionals, ensuring residents have access to quality healthcare services.

Affordable Housing: Recognizing the housing affordability crisis, Ward proposes fostering public-private partnerships to unlock land for sustainable housing projects, coupled with strategic infrastructure investments.

Economic Stability: Ward prioritizes fiscal responsibility by curbing excessive spending, and conducting a comprehensive review of provincial taxes to alleviate burdens on residents and businesses.

New Initiatives: Ward is committed to revitalizing the local economy by promoting resource industries such as forestry, mining, agriculture, and tourism, thereby creating jobs and opportunities for families. Additionally, he envisions a future of energy self-sufficiency through investments in renewable energy sources.

Ward’s leadership, community involvement, and forward-thinking platform embody a vision of progress and prosperity for Kamloops-North Thompson. With his proven track record and unwavering dedication, Ward is poised to lead the region towards a brighter future for all its residents.
Pitch summary: Former two-term Barriere mayor and forestry worker, MLA since 2024. He says affordability is the number one issue, along with jobs and a 'disastrous' health-care system, and that after 10 years of NDP government it's time for a change. His party page also lists faster accreditation of medical professionals, public-private partnerships for housing land, a provincial tax review and promoting resource industries.
Key priorities: affordability; jobs; health care / medical professional accreditation; housing via public-private partnerships; fiscal responsibility and tax review; forestry, mining, agriculture, tourism
Quote: It’s the bread and butter. It’s affordability, number one. People are trying to make ends meet. We are talking about people trying to keep their jobs. We are talking about our disastrous healthcare system that we have. The list goes on and on.

Name: John Kidder
Pitch summary: No individual pitch found. Ashcroft resident and husband of federal Green leader Elizabeth May, reported to be seeking the BC Green nomination; he has run before provincially and federally as a Green and as a federal Liberal in 2011.

Name: Kory Clark
Pitch summary: 24-year-old health-care worker (community support worker, USW Local 1-417) who grew up in Cache Creek. He says he believes in the NDP's vision and names cost of living, housing and health care as key issues.
Key priorities: cost of living; housing; health care
Quote: I've always been interested in politics, and I just decided now's the time to represent Kamloops.

Name: Deborah Friesen
Pitch summary: No individual pitch found. Confirmed OneBC candidate in final-list coverage; a LinkedIn profile under this name lists a Kamloops strata property manager (not confirmed as the same person).

Name: Kristina Loewen
Bio:
Professional Experience

Kristina is a seasoned real estate professional, known for her exceptional ability to prioritize her clients’ needs while maintaining a level-headed approach under pressure. Her career has not only honed her skills in negotiation and client relations but has also given her a deep understanding of the local housing market.

Community Involvement

In addition to her work in real estate, Kristina has been actively involved in various aspects of the healthcare system. Starting as a care-aide, she later became a doula, supporting families during childbirth. Her commitment to empowering individuals extends to her role as a youth and young adult leader in her community, where she inspires others to achieve their goals.

Advocacy and Values

Kristina is a passionate advocate for affordable housing, recognizing the importance of stable and accessible housing for all. She is also committed to extensive tax reform and fiscal responsibility, believing that a balanced budget and a profitable economy are crucial for the prosperity of British Columbians.

Personal Life

Kristina Loewen has been an integral part of the Kelowna community for 25 years. She is happily married to Andrew, and together they have four children. Their enduring marriage of 26 years this spring is a testament to their commitment to family values.

Vision for the Future

Kristina envisions a future where individuals and families are empowered in all aspects of their lives, including health, finances, and relationships. She believes that a strong, safe, and united community, coupled with a thriving economy, are essential for achieving this vision. Kristina’s strong conservative values drive her commitment to forging a better future for Kelowna, the province, and all its residents.

Kristina Loewen’s blend of professional expertise, community engagement, and strong conservative values make her a strong MLA for Kelowna Centre. Her dedication to empowering individuals and families, coupled with her commitment to affordable housing and fiscal responsibility, positions her as an MLA who is ready to lead Kelowna into a prosperous future.
Pitch summary: Realtor and former care aide/doula who won the seat in 2024 by 40 votes. She has made addiction treatment central to her time in office and campaign, calling for detox, treatment, counselling and compassionate secure care, and says the NDP has not prioritized healing people. Her party page also stresses affordable housing, tax reform and fiscal responsibility.
Key priorities: addiction treatment, detox and recovery; compassionate secure care; street disorder; seniors; affordable housing; tax reform and fiscal responsibility
Quote: What I've been advocating for has been treatment, detox, counselling, all of the services that really heal people and get them off the streets and restore them to some sort of family and health and whatever's possible for them.

Name: Loyal Wooldridge
Bio:
Loyal Wooldridge: Building up Kelowna Centre

A successful entrepreneur, social equity advocate, Regional District of Central Okanagan Director and Former Chair, Loyal Wooldridge was elected as a Kelowna city councillor in 2018 and 2022. During the 2023 Grouse Complex fires, Loyal’s communication efforts kept thousands of evacuees and families informed during a devastating crisis, while helping secure vital disaster relief funding so communities can rebuild. Loyal is an active community volunteer with the YMCA, BC SPCA and KGH Foundation, among other organisations.

Loyal knows that housing, healthcare and affordability are big challenges across BC, and Kelowna Centre is no different. People here need a representative who will fight hard for them — building more housing that’s affordable, improving healthcare services and strengthening our resilience to climate-fueled fires and drought.

Loyal Wooldridge, David Eby and the BC NDP have a plan to stand up for British Columbians against external threats, protect the services people count on, and build for the future.

The plan is working. And we can’t stop now.
Pitch video title: Loyal Wooldridge 2026 | STAND UP. PROTECT. BUILD. (own channel)
Pitch summary: Two-term Kelowna councillor and former RDCO chair who lost to Loewen by 40 votes in 2024. His campaign puts addiction treatment at the centre: restoring bed-based withdrawal management delivered directly by Interior Health, recovery housing, and compassionate involuntary care for a small group. His campaign page also names housing, health care, affordability and resilience to fires and drought.
Key priorities: bed-based withdrawal management by Interior Health; recovery-based housing; compassionate involuntary care (Interior-based); affordable housing; health care; affordability; wildfire and drought resilience
Quote: Right now, people have to wait weeks. When people need help today, they're unable to receive it.

Name: Bill Desrosiers
Pitch summary: No individual pitch found. Listed as OneBC candidate in Kelowna Capital News final list; no OneBC page or coverage found.

Name: Pavneet Singh
Bio:
Pavneet Singh is a successful entrepreneur, community advocate, and political leader who has called the Okanagan home for more than 25 years. Through his business ventures and community involvement, he has built strong relationships with residents, local businesses, first responders, and community organizations.

Pavneet currently serves as Vice-President of the Conservative Party of B.C., following his previous role as Director-at-Large. His leadership is rooted in entrepreneurship, community service, and a commitment to bringing people together.

During the 2024 provincial election, Pavneet chose not to run as an independent and instead supported the Conservative Party of B.C., putting the broader conservative movement ahead of his own political ambitions and helping avoid a split in the conservative vote.

As an entrepreneur, Pavneet has built and operated multiple businesses throughout the region. He has created employment opportunities and remains actively involved in the local business community.

Pavneet is also a strong supporter of firefighters, first responders, and community organizations, and continues to contribute his time and resources to causes that strengthen the community he has called home for more than two decades.
Pitch summary: Okanagan entrepreneur and Conservative Party of B.C. vice-president, chosen over former MP Tracy Gray. He ran for BC United in 2024 but stepped aside to avoid splitting the vote. He pledges to work hard, listen to residents and earn the chance to represent the riding.
Key priorities: listening to residents; local business and jobs; support for firefighters and first responders; conservative unity
Quote: I am proud to stand with the Conservative Party of BC and look forward to working hard, listening to residents, and earning the opportunity to represent our community.

Name: Carter Mochinski
Bio:
Carter Mochinski is a youth advocate, climate organizer and community member who grew up in Lake Country and has a strong connection to the Okanagan. He is passionate about climate action, reducing inequality, improving education and making sure young people have a meaningful voice in public life.

Carter represented Canada as a delegate at the United Nations Climate Change Conference COP30 in Brazil, where he advocated for climate education and spoke about the impacts of climate change on young people. He has also worked with the BC Parks Foundation and independently to support stronger connections between nature, climate education and the provincial curriculum.

He is also a TEDx speaker and has spoken publicly about inequality in the education system, including the experiences of neurodivergent learners and the need for more inclusive approaches to learning.

Carter currently serves as Director of Research and Publications with the BC Youth Council, a non-partisan, youth-led organization focused on connecting young people with politics through educational resources, advocacy and opportunities to engage with elected representatives.

His community involvement also includes serving as a youth representative with the BC Parks Foundation and previously as a Youth Councillor with the District of Lake Country, where he advocated for young people in his community.

Having grown up in the Okanagan, Carter has a deep appreciation for the balance of natural beauty, urban communities and rural life that defines Kelowna-Lake Country-Coldstream. He is running to bring his experience in youth advocacy, climate action and education into public service and to be an accessible and engaged representative for the community.
Pitch summary: Youth advocate and climate organizer from Lake Country, COP30 delegate, TEDx speaker and BC Youth Council research director. He is running on climate action, reducing inequality, improving education (including for neurodivergent learners) and giving young people a voice.
Key priorities: climate action; reducing inequality; education and inclusive learning; youth voice in politics; accessible representation
Quote: I will represent our community with the love, passion, and integrity it deserves.

Name: Binny Boparai
Pitch summary: No individual pitch found for 2026. A 2023 video shows a fruit-beverage entrepreneur named Binny Boparai seeking the BC United nomination (same person not confirmed).

Name: Alexandra Wright
Bio:
Candidate — Kelowna – Lake Country – Coldstream

Alexandra is a first-generation Canadian who was raised with a deep appreciation for the freedoms and opportunities that Canada provides, but also with the understanding that democracy can never be taken for granted. Good government depends on elected representatives who are accountable to the people they serve, and more importantly, upon the citizens who hold those representatives accountable.

Alexandra earned her BA in Anthropology from the University of Calgary before briefly moving to California, where she obtained her Juris Doctor degree from UCLA School of Law. After practising law for several years, Alexandra returned home to Canada and built a career as a legal advisor in the energy sector. In 2013, Alexandra and her husband, John, incorporated a full-service supply chain consulting firm. Over the years, they have grown their business while raising their daughter and running their family farm in Ellison, gaining firsthand experience of the challenges faced by farmers, parents and small business owners in our province.

Alexandra believes strongly in standing up for her community and in leading by example, and over the past years she has led rallies and campaigns within her region to oppose unlawful dumping, protect waterways and take a stand against irresponsible development that threatens to harm the future of the Okanagan Valley. Her favourite part of living in Ellison is listening to the owls hooting at night.

Alexandra believes British Columbians deserve leaders who approach public service with humility, make decisions openly and transparently, and never lose sight of the fact that a government only exists to serve its citizens. If elected, Alexandra will bring to the legislature the same approach that has guided her throughout her career: read the fine print, think critically, ask difficult questions, and never be afraid to challenge the status quo. Most importantly, she intends to remain true to the principles that brought her there in the first place.
Pitch video title: Alexandra Wright: Why I Chose OneBC Over the BC Conservatives (The Really Big Show)
Pitch summary: UCLA-trained lawyer and energy-sector legal advisor who runs a supply-chain consulting firm and family farm in Ellison, and has led local campaigns against unlawful dumping and irresponsible development. Her OneBC page promises humble, transparent public service and challenging the status quo; she explained choosing OneBC over the Conservatives in an Oct 4 interview.
Key priorities: accountable, transparent government; protecting waterways and opposing irresponsible development; farmers and families; challenging the status quo
Quote: If elected, Alexandra will bring to the legislature the same approach that has guided her throughout her career: read the fine print, think critically, ask difficult questions, and never be afraid to challenge the status quo.

Name: Gavin Dew
Bio:
Gavin Dew is a business leader, entrepreneur, and executive with extensive experience in governance and public policy. As the MLA in Kelowna-Mission and the Conservative Critic for Jobs, Economic Development, and Innovation (JEDI) & AI, Gavin is driven by a passion to renew and rebuild BC’s economic potential.

Personal Life

Born and raised in British Columbia, Gavin lives in Kelowna with his wife, Erin, and their two children, Abby and Evan. The Dew family is committed to building community through both volunteerism and small business. Erin, a UBC Forestry graduate, has a diverse background that includes working with children on the autism spectrum and running a small business. Together, they recently launched Play Area, Kelowna’s newest indoor playground, to serve the growing number of young families in the Okanagan.

Professional Background

Gavin’s career spans two decades at the intersection of business, public policy, and technology. He has played a key role in building public understanding and support for complex policies and projects across Canada, including affordable housing, energy infrastructure, and tech clusters. Most recently, Gavin served as Chief Strategy Officer for a $5 billion agricultural innovation and food security project in BC. He also has a strong academic background, with a BA from UBC and an MBA from the University of Oxford, where he focused on corporate social responsibility.

Community Involvement

Gavin is deeply committed to his community. Prior to being elected, he served on the boards of the Business Council of British Columbia and Resource Works, an organization promoting responsible resource development. He has also served in governance roles with organizations like UBC, Kwantlen Polytechnic University and Community Futures, a rural small business lender. Gavin continues to volunteer as chair of the Veterans Transition Network, a national mental health charity that played a crucial role in evacuating Afghan interpreters at risk from the Taliban. His community efforts have earned him recognition, including being named a “Forty Under 40” by Business in Vancouver for his leadership.
Pitch summary: MLA since 2024 and Conservative critic for jobs, economic development, innovation and AI; former business-policy executive. His campaign message is affordability through a stronger economy and lower taxes, attacking Eby's record and calling the NDP grocery 'price guard' 'the arsonist offering to put out the fire.'
Key priorities: affordability via stronger economy; lower taxes; small business confidence; economic rebuilding; distrust of Eby's promises
Quote: The best thing we can do to make sure that food is more affordable is strengthen the economy and make sure that people actually have more money in their pockets and in their wallets.

Name: Saoirse MacKinnon
Pitch summary: No individual pitch found. Listed as BC Green candidate in Kelowna Capital News final list; no party page or coverage found.

Name: Miriam Rycroft
Pitch summary: No individual pitch found. Listed as BC NDP candidate in final-list coverage; no campaign page or news profile found.

Name: Abraham Nordine
Pitch summary: No individual pitch found. Listed as OneBC candidate in Kelowna Capital News final list.

Name: Gordon Skulnec
Bio:
Gordon Skulnec is the Conservative Party of BC Candidate for Kootenay Central

Gordon is a husband, father, volunteer and small business owner. He and his wife were both born and raised in the West Kootenays and have been married for 19 years.

Gordon began his career as a medical radiographer at Kootenay Boundary Regional Hospital in Trail before joining the RCMP. He served 17 years as a general duty police officer in the East Kootenays, beginning in Cranbrook, and retired from the Kimberley detachment in May 2023. For the past 20 years, he has also run a small business as a rental housing provider and property manager, working with landlords and tenants alike, and for the past decade he has operated a business in Salmo.

Serving his community, especially its young people, has always been important to Gordon. He started as a youth group leader in Trail and coached Cranbrook Minor Baseball house and all-star teams for four years. Today he serves as Director of Baseball for the Cranbrook Minor Ball Association and drives the team bus for the Cranbrook Bandits. Faith matters deeply to his family. They attend Connect Church, where he helps lead the men’s group. 

Gordon brings a humble heart and a willingness to listen, and he is committed to working alongside the people of Kootenay Central to build real progress for their communities.
Pitch summary: Former RCMP general-duty officer (17 years in the East Kootenay, retired from Kimberley in 2023), former medical radiographer, and rental-housing provider with a business in Salmo. His party page says he brings a willingness to listen and wants to work with residents to build progress; no specific promises listed.
Key priorities: listening to residents; community and youth (background); public safety (policing background); rental housing (business background)
Quote: Gordon brings a humble heart and a willingness to listen, and he is committed to working alongside the people of Kootenay Central to build real progress for their communities.

Name: Nicole Charlwood
Pitch summary: Nelson city councillor and economist who placed second with 31% for the Greens in 2020 and ran again in 2024. No 2026-specific pitch found; in 2024 she listed political representation, rural health care, affordability, water security and housing for workers and young families as her focus.
Key priorities: (2024) political representation; rural health care; affordability; water security; housing for workers and young families
Quote: (2024) political representation, rural healthcare, affordability, water security and housing for workers and young families — issues that are at the forefront of our shared priorities.

Name: Brittny Anderson
Bio:
Protecting the things that matter in Kootenay Central

Brittny Anderson is a lifelong resident of the Kootenays and former small-business owner. Elected as MLA for Nelson-Creston in 2020, and re-elected in 2024, Brittny has served as Minister of State for Local Governments and Rural Communities, Parliamentary Secretary for Tourism, as well as the Premier’s Special Advisor on Youth.

Brittny previously served her community as a Nelson city councillor and board member for the Regional District of Central Kootenay, where her work covered environmental services, resource recovery and water systems. Like so many people in the Kootenays, Brittny is passionate about spending time outdoors, and can often be found hiking with her family and her dogs Stella and Boreal.

Brittny Anderson, David Eby and the BC NDP are standing up for BC with a plan to fight for our province and country, protect people and services, and build a stronger economy.

The plan is working. We can’t stop now.
Pitch summary: MLA since 2020 (Nelson-Creston, then Kootenay Central) and former Minister of State for Local Governments and Rural Communities; former Nelson councillor. She is running on public health care, the environment, reconciliation and stable government that stands up to Trump's tariffs, and on building a B.C. economy less dependent on the U.S.
Key priorities: public health care; clean environment/climate; reconciliation; affordable housing; good jobs and thriving businesses; standing up to U.S. tariffs
Quote: At this critical moment for our province and country, I will never stop fighting for my Kootenay community to continue building a stronger, more affordable future for everyone. For public health care. For our planet. For reconciliation.

Name: Hunter Corrigal
Bio:
Hunter spent twenty years doing the jobs that keep B.C. running: fighting wildfires, securing our courts, working our mines and supporting kids in our classrooms.

He runs a small business and is raising two daughters. He has also engaged with our healthcare system through his cancer journey. Hunter knows where this province works and where it is letting people down, and he is running to be a part of the solution in making life better.

Hunter holds a Diploma in Tourism & Recreation Management from the College of the Rockies and a Sheriff Training Certificate from the Justice Institute of BC.

He is the owner-operator of an exploration logistics and hardscape company. In his community, he has served as past president of the Wildhorse Cycling Club and as a Special Olympics ski coach.

Hunter is running to fight for safer communities, resource jobs, strong schools, better healthcare and lower taxes.
Pitch summary: Cranbrook-based former BC Sheriff officer, Teck Elkview operator, wildfire crew leader and small-business owner, and OneBC's Kootenay coordinator. Tax relief is his number-one focus, along with rural health care (informed by his own 2024 cancer diagnosis), safer communities, resource jobs and strong schools.
Key priorities: tax relief (personal and business); rural health care access; safer communities; resource jobs; strong schools; local-government autonomy
Quote: Number one is absolutely tax relief.

Name: Warren Mirko
Bio:
Warren Mirko is the Conservative Party of BC candidate for Kootenay-Monashee

Warren has more than 15 years of experience in public relations, crisis response, and risk management, having supported public protection mandates at BC Financial Services Authority, Engineers and Geoscientists BC, Transport Canada, and other regulatory authorities. His work has included regulatory reform, public safety issues, stakeholder disputes, and high-profile matters requiring coordination between government, industry, professionals, and affected communities. He holds a BA in Political Science from the University of British Columbia.

Warren’s work spans both the public and private sectors, where clear communication and public disclosure are critical to maintaining public trust. He is a Councillor in the Village of Warfield and a public affairs consultant who helps clients navigate government relations and align with regulatory and community expectations.

Warren contributes to media on issues of economics, governance, and accountability, bringing a candid perspective to land use and public policy in BC. He enjoys travelling throughout BC with his family and spending time outdoors. He also speaks Japanese and has practised Okinawan karate for more than 15 years.
Pitch summary: Warfield councillor and public-affairs consultant who founded the Public Land Use Society. He says Victoria's decisions hit rural B.C. disproportionately and is campaigning on land and resource access, clear rules, democratic voice in land-use decisions, and tighter management of public finances.
Key priorities: rural voice in Victoria; public land use and resource access; clear, predictable rules; fiscal accountability / deficit
Quote: Living in a small community, spending much of my free time on public land, and working closely on land-use and governance issues has given me a direct appreciation for how decisions made in Victoria can have a disproportionate impact on rural B.C.

Name: Connie Larochelle
Bio:
