Maureen is running to advocate for stronger public services, affordable housing, support for families and small businesses, environmental stewardship, and investments that build resilient communities for the next generation. A vote for Maureen and the BC Greens is a vote for better for the people of New Westminster and Coquitlam.
Pitch summary: Coquitlam science and math teacher of 25 years, physicist and climate organizer (co-founder of the Climate Safe Cities Coalition). She is the 2024 Green candidate here. She is running for stronger public services, affordable housing, support for families and small business, environmental stewardship, and evidence-based decisions.
Key priorities: stronger public services;affordable housing;support for families and small businesses;good jobs for young people;environmental stewardship/climate action;evidence-based decision-making
Quote: It is time for governments that want to collaborate, plan for the future, and make decisions based on facts and evidence.

Name: Jennifer Whiteside
Bio:
Protecting the things that people value in New Westminster-Coquitlam

Jennifer Whiteside has dedicated her career to fighting for the rights of working people. She has fought for better public healthcare and making sure people are treated fairly -- including leading BC’s first living wage campaign.

A former labour leader and community advocate, Whiteside was elected as the MLA for New Westminster in October 2020, and re-elected in 2024. She is the Minister of Labour and previously served as the Minister of Mental Health and Addictions and Minister of Education and Child Care. She was born and raised in New Westminster.

Where the BC Conservatives would roll over for Trump, Jennifer Whiteside, David Eby and the BC NDP have a plan to stand up for British Columbia, protect the services that families need, and build the homes and good jobs we need for a stronger province.
Pitch summary: Incumbent MLA since 2020, Minister of Labour, and former Education and Mental Health minister. She is a former labour leader who led BC's first living wage campaign. Her campaign page frames her as protecting public healthcare and fair treatment for workers, and contrasts the NDP with Conservatives who would 'roll over for Trump.'
Key priorities: workers' rights and fair treatment;public healthcare;protecting services for families (party message);building homes and good jobs (party message)
Quote: Jennifer Whiteside has dedicated her career to fighting for the rights of working people.

Name: Gerry Lenoski
Pitch summary: No individual pitch found.

Name: Rodney Proskiw
Bio:
Rodney Proskiw is the Conservative Party of BC candidate for North Coast-Haida Gwaii.

Rodney has lived in Prince Rupert for 20 years, and he and his wife Sheryl are proud to have raised their family on the North Coast.

Rodney brings a perspective few candidates can offer. As a small business owner, he knows what it takes to meet a payroll and keep the doors open. As a longtime union member with UFCW 1518, UFCW 247 and the Teamsters, he understands that families on the North Coast need good, stable jobs. That experience on both sides gives him the insight to listen to every point of view and find the solutions that work best for local residents.

Rodney has spent years serving his community. He is a past President of the Prince Rupert Lions Club and a past Zone Chairman of Lions International, and he retired as the longest-serving director on the board of Tourism Prince Rupert.

Rodney believes the North Coast has a vibrant future, with real opportunities ahead. But many of the issues facing the region are complex, and too many local voices are not being heard. He is running to change that.
Pitch summary: Prince Rupert small business owner of 20 years, longtime union member (UFCW, Teamsters), and past Lions Club president. His party profile says the North Coast has real opportunities but too many local voices aren't heard, and he's running to change that and support stable jobs.
Key priorities: good, stable jobs;small business;giving local voices a hearing;North Coast economic opportunity
Quote: Rodney believes the North Coast has a vibrant future, with real opportunities ahead. But many of the issues facing the region are complex, and too many local voices are not being heard. He is running to change that.

Name: Francis Racy
Bio:
Francis Racy was born and raised in northern B.C. and called Prince Rupert home for close to half her life. Her grandfather was Tsimshian from Lax Kw’alaams and her grandmother was Gitxsan. She carries that lineage as Ganeda, Frog Clan, of Wilp Luuxhon, and holds the hereditary name En nuu Ann Gaiwh. For Francis, the North is not simply where she lives. It is part of her identity, her responsibility, and a central reason she is running to represent North Coast-Haida Gwaii.

Since February 2026, Francis has led mental health education programming and supported regional educators across Prince Rupert, Terrace, the Bulkley Valley, and Haida Gwaii. Her work has given her a firsthand view of the pressures facing rural and northern communities, particularly gaps in healthcare, mental health supports, and social services.

Francis also brings direct front-line experience as a Health Care Assistant and Early Childhood Educator. Those roles gave her close insight into the needs of families, elders, children, and people navigating systems that are often stretched thin.

Land and water stewardship are central to Francis’s community work. She has built relationships with Indigenous leaders across Canada and internationally and is a founding board member of the Wilp Sustainability Forum, where she helps support governance rooted in Wilp member voice, Gitanyow law, and stewardship of the land and water.

Francis is also involved in local food sovereignty work and has supported poultry raising and livestock processing shared with family and community. Her broader record of community leadership includes serving as Chairperson of the Powell River BCSPCA Community Council and decades of involvement with the SPCA.

While continuing her community and professional work, Francis is completing a Bachelor of General Studies through Thompson Rivers University’s Open Learning program, with plans to pursue a Master of Education in Indigenous Education at UBC.

Francis is running because she believes North Coast-Haida Gwaii deserves representation grounded in lived experience of the region, its communities, and the challenges people face every day. She is ready to bring that experience to Victoria.
Pitch summary: Tsimshian/Gitxsan mental health educator, former health care assistant and early childhood educator, and founding board member of the Wilp Sustainability Forum. She says she is running for representation grounded in lived northern experience, focusing on gaps in rural healthcare, mental health and social services, plus land and water stewardship and food sovereignty.
Key priorities: rural and northern healthcare gaps;mental health supports;social services;land and water stewardship;food sovereignty;Indigenous governance
Quote: This land isn’t a backdrop to my politics – it’s my lineage, my responsibility, and the reason I’m running.

Name: Tamara Davidson
Pitch summary: Incumbent MLA (Laanas), an elected Council of the Haida Nation representative from Skidegate with 25+ years in public service. Her page stresses Indigenous rights, housing and healthcare. Eby opened her Prince Rupert campaign office on Sep 28 with pledges to keep the North Coast tanker ban, support the North Coast Transmission Line, and focus on rural health care and jobs.
Key priorities: Indigenous rights;housing;healthcare (rural);North Coast tanker ban (party message);jobs and economic development/port (party message)
Quote: I know I wouldn’t be here without our volunteers, staff, and people like you willing to come forward, ask tough questions, and be here for us the same way we want to be there for you.

Name: Anna Kindy
Bio:
A Physician and Advocate for the North Island

Dr. Anna Kindy is a physician, addiction specialist and dedicated advocate, and the MLA for North Island. With a career spanning 35 years in medicine and a commitment to her community, Anna is poised to make a significant impact on the North Island’s well-being.

Championing the Marginalised and Stigmatised

Throughout her career, Anna has been a tireless advocate for the marginalised and stigmatised populations of the North Island. Her compassionate approach to healthcare and her ability to objectively analyse issues have allowed her to collaborate effectively to address root problems and work towards positive solutions.

A Physician’s Journey of Service

Anna’s journey in medicine began with her graduation from the University of Alberta Medical School in 1986. Early in her career, she worked in remote Quebec, gaining valuable experience and contributing to underserved communities. In a unique twist, from 1989-1992, she balanced a career as a family doctor in Port Hardy with her husband, who was also a GP, while simultaneously competing on the World Cup circuit in mogul skiing. Her dedication and perseverance led her to represent Canada in mogul skiing at the Albertville Olympics in 1992.

In 1998, Anna and her husband, Dr. Peter Olesen, a surgeon, made the pivotal decision to move to Campbell River to both work and raise their three children. Anna’s commitment to healthcare extended to international missions in Guatemala. She specialised in addiction medicine and embraced principles such as informed consent, doing no harm, and upholding bodily autonomy as core tenets of her practice.

A Vision for Positive Change

Anna’s vision for the North Island is one of positive change and empowerment. She is excited to help break away from politics as usual. Her mission is to provide the North Island’s population with a strong voice, driving improvements in their standard of living, work environments, and access to healthcare.

As the MLA, Dr. Anna Kindy’s represents a unique blend of medical expertise, community advocacy, and a deep commitment to fostering well-being in the North Island.
Pitch summary: Incumbent MLA (2024), physician and addiction specialist, and former Olympic mogul skier. She says the campaign spotlights a health care crisis in the riding: Port Hardy ER closed after 5 p.m. for about three years, an overcapacity Campbell River Hospital, a cancelled long-term care project, and a slow Carihi Secondary rebuild. She also criticizes NDP fiscal management.
Key priorities: health care crisis (Port Hardy ER hours, Campbell River Hospital capacity);long-term care beds;Carihi Secondary rebuild;fiscal management/deficit;standard of living and access to healthcare
Quote: I’m a physician, so (there is a) health care crisis on our hands across B.C. but also in our riding. For example the Port Hardy Hospital emergency department is now closed after 5 p.m. for almost over three years.

Name: Benjamin Olsson
Bio:
Benjamin Olsson is a Registered Social Worker, healthcare professional and longtime North Island resident who has called Campbell River home since 2010. He moved to Vancouver Island because of his love for the coast and has developed a deep connection to the communities and natural environment of the North Island.

Benjamin holds a Diploma in Social Work from Red Deer College and a Bachelor of Social Work from the University of Regina. He later completed a Post-Degree Diploma in Interprofessional Mental Health and Addiction at Camosun College. His career has included work in social services, healthcare, mental health and community wellness.

Community involvement has been a constant throughout Benjamin’s life. He has more than two decades of union activism, has participated in election campaigns and has supported a wide range of local causes including Pride events, the Terry Fox Run, Cops for Cancer, Habitat for Humanity, the Campbell River Hospice Society and harm reduction initiatives.

Benjamin has also been active in advocating for the protection of green spaces and critical salmon habitat. He believes the North Island’s communities, forests, coastlines and ecosystems are worth protecting for the people who live there today and for future generations.

His political involvement began early and has included organizing, union work and serving as Leader of the Green Party of Saskatchewan in 2003. He brings that experience together with decades of frontline work supporting individuals, families and communities.

Benjamin is running in North Island to bring his experience in social work, healthcare, community organizing and environmental advocacy into public service, with a focus on listening to local residents and acting in the best interests of the communities he calls home.
Pitch summary: Registered social worker and healthcare professional in Campbell River since 2010, a union activist, and a former Saskatchewan Green leader (2003). He is running to listen to residents and protect North Island green spaces, forests and salmon habitat, drawing on his social work and mental health experience.
Key priorities: listening to local residents;protecting green spaces and salmon habitat;mental health and addiction/social services;healthcare;community wellness
Quote: I want to support the people and places I love by listening, leading, and acting in the best interests of the North Island.

Name: Sara Lopez
Bio:
Building a stronger North Island.

Sara Lopez has called Campbell River home for more than a decade, choosing to raise her children close to their Kwakwaka’wakw and Nuu-chah-nulth community, culture and family.

Her career in nonprofits, arts and culture, social justice and community service has always been about standing up for people who too often don’t have a voice.

As Executive Director of the Campbell River Art Gallery, Sara stood her ground when the City Council moved to remove the Gallery’s tax-exempt status, fighting back with broad community support and winning that fight.

Today, through her work with Habitat for Humanity Vancouver Island North, she continues to advocate for affordable housing and stronger communities.

Sara Lopez, David Eby and the BC NDP have a plan to build BC strong: to create jobs, to strengthen healthcare, and to make life more affordable.
Pitch summary: Campbell River nonprofit leader (former Campbell River Art Gallery executive director, now with Habitat for Humanity Vancouver Island North), raising her children close to their Kwakwaka'wakw and Nuu-chah-nulth community. She is running on good jobs, strong health care and affordable housing and life.
Key priorities: good jobs;strong health care;affordability;affordable housing;standing up for people without a voice
Quote: North Island families deserve good jobs, strong health care and a fair shot at an affordable life and a future in the communities they love.

Name: Richard Lambert
Pitch summary: Port McNeill-raised Army veteran (PPCLI, 15 years), electrician and retail building-centre worker in Campbell River. He says North Island communities are dwindling in jobs, people and health care while social problems and the cost of living rise, and he wants to bring solutions and relief.
Key priorities: jobs;health care;cost of living;social problems;population decline in North Island communities
Quote: I have lived on the North Island for three decades. I have seen too many communities dwindling down.

Name: Karen Fraser
Bio:
Karen Fraser is a North Vancouver resident and active member of her community who believes British Columbians deserve a practical, balanced alternative in provincial politics.

Karen believes good government should focus on solving problems, listening to communities and finding workable solutions rather than engaging in ideological divisions.

As the CentreBC candidate in North Vancouver Lonsdale, Karen is proud to give voters the opportunity to support a new political choice and to help build a stronger centrist movement in British Columbia.

Sign up to stay informed and receive news from CentreBC:
Pitch summary: North Vancouver resident, community volunteer (Family Services of the North Shore) and early CentreBC supporter. Her profile offers a practical, centrist alternative focused on solving problems and listening rather than ideological division. It lists no specific policy items.
Key priorities: practical, centrist government;listening to communities;problem-solving over ideology
Quote: Karen believes good government should focus on solving problems, listening to communities and finding workable solutions rather than engaging in ideological divisions.

Name: Trevor Withers
Bio:
Trevor Withers is the Conservative Party of BC candidate for North Vancouver-Lonsdale.

Trevor Withers is a North Shore local whose commitment to North Vancouver has been shaped by years of living, working and participating in the community.

A graduate of Queen’s University, Trevor works as a Data Visualization Engineer at Aritzia, turning complex information into clear insights that support better decisions. He wants to bring that same analytical approach to public service, with an emphasis on fiscal responsibility and ensuring taxpayers receive value for their money.

Trevor’s community connections include years working at Tap & Barrel in North Vancouver, playing junior hockey with the North Vancouver Wolfpack and refereeing local minor hockey. These experiences have shaped his appreciation for teamwork, hard work and the people who make the North Shore home.
Pitch summary: North Shore local, Queen's graduate and data visualization engineer at Aritzia. His profile pitches an analytical approach to public service, with an emphasis on fiscal responsibility and value for taxpayers.
Key priorities: fiscal responsibility;value for taxpayers' money;analytical, evidence-based decisions
Quote: He wants to bring that same analytical approach to public service, with an emphasis on fiscal responsibility and ensuring taxpayers receive value for their money.

Name: Joshua A Singer Johnson
Pitch summary: No individual pitch found.

Name: Bowinn Ma
Bio:
Bowinn Ma: Standing up for families in North Vancouver-Lonsdale

Elected in 2017, 2020 and 2024, Bowinn has served as Minister of Emergency Management and Climate Readiness and Minister of Infrastructure. A professional engineer and working mother, she welcomed her daughter in 2023, becoming the third B.C. cabinet minister to give birth while in office, and welcomed her son in 2026.

As a member of David Eby’s BC NDP team, Bowinn has delivered real action for people across the North Shore, helping secure provincial funding for housing, schools, health-care facilities, child care spaces, and transit and active transportation infrastructure. Her collaborative work on a regional transportation strategy helped pave the way for a rapid transit concept to the North Shore, which the TransLink Mayors’ Council has since identified as a regional priority.

Bowinn Ma, David Eby and the BC NDP have a plan to stand up for British Columbians, protect what families depend on, and build an economy free from the United States.
Pitch summary: Incumbent MLA since 2017, former Minister of Infrastructure and of Emergency Management, and a professional engineer and mother of two. Her campaign page credits her with provincial funding for North Shore housing, schools, health facilities, child care and transit, and with work that led to a North Shore rapid transit concept. She says voters deserve a stable government to face US economic threats.
Key priorities: North Shore rapid transit;housing;schools and child care;health-care facilities;stable government in face of US tariffs;economy free from the US (party message)
Quote: British Columbians deserve to have a choice in deciding how the province moves forward in the face of that threat.

Name: Lori Climenhaga
Bio:
Lori Climenhaga brings seasoned leadership and deep community roots to her candidacy. A Deep Cove resident for more than 16 years, she has had the privilege of raising her family in the community she loves. Lori is running because she believes British Columbians deserve a government that works with people, not around them. In the Legislature, she will bring a balanced, common-sense approach, a focus on affordability and economic opportunity, and a commitment to respectful dialogue and collaboration.

Lori brings more than 25 years of results-driven leadership across government, business and the community sector, with a career built on bringing people together to solve complex challenges. She began at WCG International, where she built and led strategic partnerships with more than 40 chambers of commerce, community agencies and business associations to connect employers with talent across the province.

Following, as Director of Member Relations at the BC Chamber of Commerce, Lori championed a provincial network of more than 75 local chambers, ensuring the priorities of businesses in every region were heard.

In 2020, Lori was hired as a Director with the BC government, where she led province-wide engagement with industry associations and Crown corporations. Working across multiple ministries, she ensured employer and community insights informed policy and program design. She co-chaired a national task team under the Forum of Labour Market Ministers and supported a ministerial advisory committee of business leaders advancing accessible and inclusive workplaces.

Committed to creating opportunity for those too often left behind, Lori has led special projects and initiatives that help job seekers succeed and advance diversity and inclusion in BC’s priority sectors. She is especially passionate about building a better future for young people in our province and supporting a healthy economy that creates jobs of the future.

Today Lori leads her own consulting practice, advising organizations on community engagement, workforce development, strategic partnerships and securing funding for community initiatives. A dedicated community builder, she has served on the boards of the North Vancouver Chamber and the BC Chamber Executives Society.
Pitch summary: Deep Cove resident, consultant, former BC Chamber of Commerce director of member relations, and former BC government director for industry engagement. She is running for a government that 'works with people, not around them,' with a balanced, common-sense approach focused on affordability, economic opportunity, jobs for young people and respectful collaboration.
Key priorities: affordability;economic opportunity and jobs of the future;better future for young people;respectful dialogue and collaboration;inclusive workplaces
Quote: Lori is running because she believes British Columbians deserve a government that works with people, not around them.

Name: Lynne Block
Bio:
Lynne Block is the Conservative candidate for North Vancouver-Seymour. She is an educator, former school trustee and community leader who has dedicated her life to serving the North Shore. Having immigrated to Canada from England as a child, she grew up in British Columbia and went on to earn a Bachelor’s degree and a Master of Education from the University of British Columbia.

Lynne’s career in education spans elementary, secondary and post-secondary classrooms, as well as leadership in professional training and development. She has designed and delivered innovative programs for students and educators, including founding and facilitating the Youth Engaged in Social Responsibility Forums, which encouraged young people to take an active role in their communities. Her work in education earned her the Prime Minister’s Award for Teaching Excellence. She also co-founded a business and education consulting company dedicated to research-based learning, corporate social responsibility and collaborative leadership.

As an elected trustee in the West Vancouver School District, Lynne focused on improving student achievement while ensuring careful stewardship of public resources, balancing educational excellence with fiscal responsibility. In 2024, she was elected as a Conservative MLA, carrying the concerns of North Shore parents, seniors, educators, business owners and volunteers to Victoria.

Lynne has long given her time to her community. She has served on the North Shore Youth Justice and Family Court Committee and as British Columbia’s United Nations Representative for Women Educators International, and has volunteered with the Canadian Cancer Society, the BC Paraplegic Society and Violence Against Women in Relationships.
Pitch summary: Sitting Conservative MLA (elected 2024 in West Vancouver-Capilano) who moved to this riding so Caroline Elliott could run in her old seat. She is a former educator and West Vancouver school trustee (Prime Minister's Award for Teaching Excellence). Her profile stresses student achievement with fiscal responsibility. She called the snap election a 'power grab' and blamed Eby rather than Trump for BC's economic problems.
Key priorities: education/student achievement;fiscal responsibility;carrying North Shore parents', seniors' and business concerns to Victoria;criticism of NDP economic record
Quote: He’s blaming the boogeyman, Trump. But the reality is a lot of this [economic challenge] happened way before, all under his auspices.

Name: Ben Holt
Pitch video title: Benjamin Holt Green Party: why vote for him? North Vancouver Seymour (Boxing Beaver Media)
Pitch summary: In an Oct 3 street interview, Holt said he is running mainly over the climate crisis and accused the NDP of doing the opposite of its climate promises. He linked climate action to cost of living, housing, child care and transit. Locally he named traffic and unaffordability in North Vancouver, and he opposes new pipeline tanker traffic and dredging off North Van. He also defends DRIPA.
Key priorities: climate action;opposing pipeline/tanker expansion and Burrard Inlet dredging;cost of living;housing;child care;transit and traffic in North Vancouver;DRIPA/Indigenous rights;opposition to AI data centres

Name: Susie Chant
Bio: MLA for North Vancouver-Seymour
Pitch summary: Two-term incumbent MLA, registered nurse and naval reservist from Lynn Valley. Her campaign page commits to investing in healthcare, education and climate readiness. She says voters should decide who governs during the US trade war.
Key priorities: healthcare;education;climate readiness;standing up for services (party message)
Quote: I feel it’s important that the people of British Columbia have the opportunity at this time to determine who is going to be governing on their behalf and who has got their best interests in hand.

Name: Frederick Thiele
Pitch summary: No individual pitch found.

Name: Andrew Weaver
Bio:
Dr. Andrew J. Weaver is a Professor in the School of Earth and Ocean Sciences at the University of Victoria. He was also the Canada Research Chair in Climate Modelling and Analysis until he was elected as a BC Green Party MLA in the 2013 BC Provincial Election representing the riding of Oak Bay-Gordon Head. In 2015 Dr. Weaver assumed leadership of the BC Green Party, leading them to an historic election result in the 2017 provincial election with three elected MLAs holding the balance of power in an NDP minority government. He returned to UVic after completing two terms as an MLA.

Dr. Weaver received his B.Sc. (Mathematics and Physics) from the University of Victoria in 1983, a Master of Advanced Studies in Mathematics from Cambridge University in 1984, and a PhD in Applied Mathematics from the University of British Columbia in 1987. He has authored or coauthored over 200 peer-reviewed papers in climate, meteorology, oceanography, earth science, policy, education and anthropology journals. He was a Lead Author in the United Nations Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change 2nd, 3rd, 4th and 5th scientific assessments. He was the Chief Editor of the Journal of Climate from 2005-2009.

Dr. Weaver is a Fellow of the Royal Society of Canada, Canadian Meteorological and Oceanographic Society, American Meteorological Society, American Geophysical Union and the American Association for the Advancement of Science. Over the years he has received a number of awards including the NSERC-Steacie, Killam and Guggenheim Fellowships and the CMOS President’s Prize, the Royal Society of Canada Miroslaw Romanowski Medal and the A.G. Huntsman Award for Excellence in Marine Science. In 2008 he was appointed to the Order of British Columbia and in 2014 he received an honourary D.Sc. degree from McMaster University.

His book, Keeping our Cool: Canada in a Warming World was published by Viking Canada in September 2008. His second book, Generation Us: The Challenge of Global Warming was published by Raven books in 2011.
Pitch summary: Former BC Green leader and MLA for this riding (2013–2020) and UVic climate scientist, now running for CentreBC. On his blog he says he's running because the snap election was opportunistic and the legislature has become dysfunctional, and to support leader Elenore Sturko. He promises civility, evidence-based decision-making and constituent service.
Key priorities: civility and less partisan politics;evidence-based decision-making;constituent service in Oak Bay-Gordon Head;supporting CentreBC/Elenore Sturko;preventing an NDP majority;fiscal responsibility
Quote: Let’s return to evidence-based decision-making. Let’s put people’s interests front and centre and govern for our collective wellbeing, with responsibility to the generations who follow.

Name: Stan Sipos
Bio:
Stan Sipos is the Conservative Party of BC candidate for Oak Bay-Gordon Head.

Stan came to Canada as a refugee. Born in communist Yugoslavia, he lost his mother before his second birthday and spent three years in an Italian refugee camp with his father before Canada welcomed them. His early Canadian years were spent working on the family’s mink ranch in northern Alberta. His family cherished the freedom and opportunity Canada offered. 

At 16, Stan left home with $7.50 and a red CCM bicycle and went to work as a construction labourer. He spent the next decade in the trades, including time in the Carpenters Union, before building a career of more than 50 years in business and real estate development. He has delivered dozens of major projects across British Columbia. 

Stan remains active in award-winning developments built on a simple principle: a project has to earn community support, respect its surroundings, meet residents’ needs and make fiscal sense. He is proudest of the Customs House heritage revitalization in Victoria’s Inner Harbour. He also co-founded Cielo Carbon Solutions, a carbon capture company that reduces emissions at the source while protecting the strength of Canada’s natural gas industry.

A lifelong drag racer, Stan has won races across North America as the underdog against far better-funded teams and was inducted into the inaugural class of the Canadian Drag Racing Hall of Fame. Stan lives in Oak Bay with his wife, Dr. Anna Sylwestrowicz, and their combined family of six.
Pitch summary: Former refugee from Yugoslavia, construction labourer turned developer (Customs House revitalization), and co-founder of Cielo Carbon Solutions. His profile describes his development principle that projects must earn community support and make fiscal sense. It lists no explicit policy priorities.
Key priorities: (implied) housing/development that earns community support;fiscal sense;emissions reduction while supporting natural gas industry
Quote: Stan remains active in award-winning developments built on a simple principle: a project has to earn community support, respect its surroundings, meet residents’ needs and make fiscal sense.

Name: Andrew Appleton
Bio:
Andrew Appleton is a two-term municipal councillor for the District of Oak Bay, a community advocate, environmental professional, and longtime champion of climate action, housing diversity, active transportation, and sustainability. He has also chaired the District’s Community Climate Action Working Group, which launched the Coolkit community climate initiative.

He is running to represent Oak Bay-Gordon Head and bring local priorities directly into the provincial conversation.

Andrew has also represented Oak Bay as a Trustee on the Greater Victoria Library Board and served as Board Chair in 2023-24. During his time with the board, he worked with the Vancouver Island Regional Library to advance a Special Resolution to the Union of BC Municipalities calling for expanded provincial funding for libraries. He helped guide the renovation and upgrade of the Oak Bay library branch and the development of temporary facilities for the Nellie McClung branch during its replacement.

Andrew’s commitment to environmental stewardship began early, shaped by a childhood spent exploring creeks and the Kootenay backcountry. He holds professional training in Renewable Resource and Recreation Management and has spent his career working to protect natural spaces while helping communities plan for a more sustainable future.

Andrew is running to keep the priorities of Oak Bay-Gordon Head front and centre, bringing the same approach he has taken in local government: forward thinking, practical action, creativity, and a willingness to speak up on the issues that matter.
Pitch summary: Two-term Oak Bay councillor, former Greater Victoria Library Board chair, and environmental professional of 25+ years. He is running to bring local priorities into provincial decisions, with a record on climate action, housing diversity, active transportation, library funding and sustainability.
Key priorities: local priorities in provincial decisions;climate action;housing diversity;active transportation;library funding;sustainability/environmental protection
Quote: I will keep Oak Bay-Gordon Head priorities front and centre, with a willingness to speak up on issues that matter to this community.

Name: Diana Gibson
Bio:
Action for you in Oak Bay-Gordon Head.

Diana Gibson has devoted her career to making life better for people. An award-winning community leader and entrepreneur, she led Greater Victoria’s Community Social Planning Council, and co-founded the Firelight Group — now Canada’s largest Indigenous-owned consulting firm.

During the pandemic, when many people across Greater Victoria faced financial challenges that threatened their housing, Diana’s team at the Community Social Planning Council launched a Rent Bank for the region. They helped more than 2,000 households keep their homes.

On building more housing, investing in healthcare, and tackling climate change, you can count on Diana Gibson and David Eby to fight for you.
Pitch summary: Incumbent MLA (2024) and former Minister of Citizens' Services and of Jobs, Economic Development and Innovation. She previously led the Community Social Planning Council, whose Rent Bank helped more than 2,000 households keep their homes, and co-founded the Firelight Group. Her campaign page uses the party lines on jobs, healthcare and lowering costs.
Key priorities: housing security (Rent Bank record);good jobs (party message);protecting healthcare (party message);bringing down costs (party message);energy and economic future
Quote: During the pandemic, when many people across Greater Victoria faced financial challenges that threatened their housing, Diana’s team at the Community Social Planning Council launched a Rent Bank for the region.

Name: Curtis Whitford
Bio:
Curtis is the Conservative Party of BC candidate for Fort St. John. He will bring to Victoria his 36 years of energy-sector experience and decades of involvement in Northeast B.C.

Curtis has called Fort St. John and Northeast British Columbia home throughout a career and community life deeply connected to the region. With 36 years of experience in the oil and gas industry, Curtis brings extensive firsthand knowledge of the energy sector and the communities and people who support it. He began his career in oilfield construction and maintenance before completing his Fourth Class Power Engineering training at SAIT in Calgary.

Over the following decades, Curtis worked across a wide range of operational and supervisory roles. His experience includes working as a field operator in multiple oil and gas fields throughout Northeast B.C., as well as in gas plant operations and the control room of a producing facility. He subsequently spent approximately a decade in oilfield waste management and later worked as a regional manager with an oilfield engineering firm. His career has also included experience in oilfield transportation and fluid hauling, regional field safety, and community engagement.

Curtis has also maintained a longstanding commitment to his community. He recently joined the Board of Directors of a local co-operative serving the Fort St. John area, continuing his involvement in organizations that support the region and its residents. He has volunteered with minor hockey as a coach and board member and served as Transportation Director for the Regional Trackers hockey program. 

A proud father and part of a blended family, Curtis believes strongly in family, community involvement and contributing to the region he calls home.
Pitch video title: Why I am running to be the MLA for Peace River North
Pitch summary: Fort St. John energy-sector veteran (36 years in oil and gas operations, safety and management) and minor hockey volunteer. In his Sep 29 campaign video he says decisions are too often made without understanding life in the Peace, and he wants to be a strong voice for the region in Victoria.
Key priorities: strong voice for the Peace in Victoria;energy sector/oil and gas;decisions informed by regional realities;community and family
Quote: Together, let's make sure the voice of Peace River North is heard loud and clear in Victoria.

Name: Jordan Kealy
Bio: MLA for Peace River North
Pitch summary: Incumbent MLA, elected as a Conservative in 2024 and an Independent since 2025. He calls himself an 'Independent conservative' and says independents can represent their ridings without party constraints. He calls the snap election a 'power grab' and blames NDP policies for economic and resource-sector problems. His 2026 videos focus on agriculture and the Old Fort landslide.
Key priorities: independent representation without party constraints;opposing NDP 'power grab';resource-sector and fiscal issues;BC agriculture first;Old Fort landslide response
Quote: This region matters to me, and I’m determined to get it the attention that it deserves.

Name: Larry Neufeld
Bio:
A Dedicated Engineer and Business Leader Running for Peace River South

Larry Neufeld, a seasoned Professional Engineer and accomplished business leader, is committed to the betterment of his local community and society as a whole. As the Conservative Party of BC MLA in Peace River South, Larry brings a wealth of experience, strong values, and a passion for serving his constituents.

Rooted in the Peace River South Community

Larry’s deep commitment to the Peace River South electoral district is evident in the long period he and his family have called this area home. Growing up as the eldest son of a first-generation farmer, Larry inherited a strong work ethic and a “make do with what we have” attitude. His journey led him to pursue higher education, earning a Bachelor of Applied Science in Engineering and pursuing Graduate Studies in the same discipline. His dedication and hard work paid off when he was appointed Vice President of Western Canada’s largest environmental remediation contractor at just 29 years old.

Entrepreneurial Spirit and Fiscal Responsibility

Larry’s entrepreneurial journey began in 2006 when he founded and managed his own successful companies, giving him a profound understanding of fiscal requirements and responsibilities. His approach to managing finances is guided by the principle of not borrowing money for things that cannot be afforded. With a keen understanding of compound interest, Larry believes in responsible financial management and looks forward to bringing this perspective to government.

A Commitment to Strong Values and Community

As a former Reserve Infantry Platoon Commander, Larry instilled strong values in the troops under his command. He has also dedicated countless volunteer hours to his local community, embodying his commitment to service and making a positive impact.

Exploring Diverse Cultures and Engaging with People

Larry’s personal interests extend beyond business and politics. He is an avid traveler who seeks to connect with local people and understand their cultures and ways of life. Engaging with and forming meaningful connections with others is a core value he brings to every aspect of his life.

A Voice for a Better Community

Larry does not support the current political structure and is determined to make the South Peace Region community a better place by providing a strong voice and unwavering support for its residents.

Fiscal Conservatism and Law and Order

Larry’s political views align with fiscal conservatism, rooted in the belief that one should not borrow money for things beyond their means. His deep understanding of compound interest informs his commitment to responsible financial management. Moreover, Larry advocates for the strengthening and re-establishment of law and order in the province, emphasizing personal responsibility for one’s actions and their consequences.

As the MLA for Peace River South, Larry Neufeld represents a unique blend of engineering expertise, business acumen, strong values, and a commitment to community service. With his dedication to fiscal responsibility and law and order, Larry is ready to be a powerful advocate for the constituents of Peace River South, working tirelessly to create a safer, more prosperous, and better future for all.
Pitch summary: Incumbent MLA (2024), professional engineer, business owner and former reserve infantry officer, raised on a farm. His party profile stresses fiscal conservatism (not borrowing for what you can't afford), restoring law and order and personal responsibility, and being a strong voice for the South Peace.
Key priorities: fiscal conservatism/no borrowing beyond means;law and order and personal responsibility;strong voice for South Peace;opposition to current political structure
Quote: Larry’s political views align with fiscal conservatism, rooted in the belief that one should not borrow money for things beyond their means.

Name: Tracy St Claire
Bio:
Tracy St. Claire is a long-time Penticton resident, healthcare leader and former school trustee with a track record of bringing people together to solve complex problems and deliver results.

Improving access to care has been at the heart of Tracy’s work with the South Okanagan Similkameen Division of Family Practice, where she has spent the past 14 years, including nine years as Executive Director. In that role, she leads a regional organization representing family physicians and nurse practitioners and works with healthcare providers, community partners and all levels of government to strengthen primary care.

Under Tracy’s leadership, the Division led family physician and nurse practitioner recruitment and retention and established four family medicine clinics, the Penticton hospital inpatient program and the South Okanagan Maternity Centre. This work has given Tracy firsthand experience with the challenges facing B.C.’s healthcare system and where investments in frontline patient care can make a difference.

Most recently, during the 2026 Bald Range wildfire, Tracy served as Incident Commander for the Division’s emergency response, coordinating primary care services during the evacuation of Summerland and the disruption of healthcare and long-term care services.

She believes the region must now focus on recovery, support those affected and use what was learned to better prepare for future emergencies.

Earlier in her career, Tracy worked in negotiation and mediation, including with the BC Treaty Commission. She later served as Director of the United Way of the South Okanagan Similkameen and was elected to the Okanagan Skaha School Board, where she served as Vice-Chair and Finance Chair.

Tracy holds a Master of Arts from Simon Fraser University and a Bachelor of Arts from the University of British Columbia, with additional training in negotiation, financial management, quality improvement and organizational coaching.

Fiscally conservative, Tracy believes government has a responsibility to live within its means, use taxpayers’ money carefully and ensure public spending delivers results. She believes effective government starts with listening to communities, making sound decisions and staying focused on the services and priorities that matter most to British Columbians. She would be honoured to represent the people and communities of Penticton-Summerland in the B.C. Legislature.
Pitch summary: Executive director of the South Okanagan Similkameen Division of Family Practice, where she led physician recruitment and new clinics. She was incident commander for primary care during the 2026 Bald Range wildfire and is a former school trustee. She ran unaffiliated in 2024. Her profile pitches better access to primary care, wildfire recovery and preparedness, and fiscally careful government.
Key priorities: access to primary care/doctor recruitment;wildfire recovery and emergency preparedness;fiscal responsibility (live within means);listening to communities
Quote: Fiscally conservative, Tracy believes government has a responsibility to live within its means, use taxpayers’ money carefully and ensure public spending delivers results.

Name: Bradley Sean Bartsch
Bio:
Bradley Bartsch is a community advocate with experience across the nonprofit, education, social services, international development, financial services, arts and athletics sectors. He and his wife of 40 years moved to Penticton in 2021 and have enjoyed becoming part of the South Okanagan community.

Throughout his career, Bradley has worked with organizations including Ronald McDonald House BC & Yukon, Co:Here Housing Society, World Vision Canada, Simon Fraser University, RBC Financial Group and the Abbotsford Heat Hockey Club. His work has included fundraising for healthcare and social housing initiatives and supporting international maternal and child health programs.

Raised on Canada’s west coast, Bradley holds a Bachelor of Arts in Political Science and Business Administration from Simon Fraser University. A former multi-sport athlete, he continues to enjoy the outdoors and values the natural environment that makes the South Okanagan a special place to live.

Bradley is running in Penticton-Summerland to advocate for community-driven development and to help realize the region’s potential for both economic and environmental prosperity. He wants to bring the needs, ideas and priorities of local residents to the Legislature while working toward a sustainable future for the region.
Pitch summary: Nonprofit fundraiser and community advocate (Ronald McDonald House, World Vision, Co:Here Housing) who moved to Penticton in 2021. He ran in 2024. He is running for community-driven development and economic and environmental prosperity, bringing residents' priorities to the Legislature.
Key priorities: community-driven development;economic and environmental prosperity;sustainable future;representing local residents' ideas
Quote: I am committed to serving and being the voice in Victoria of the residents of Penticton-Summerland.

Name: Tina Lee
Bio:
Building BC strong in Penticton-Summerland

Tina Lee has worked across six continents, but Penticton is always home. It’s where she’s raising her two children, and where she wants them to grow up.

Tina works hard for people every day, and has a proven record of making their lives better. As a member of the Okanagan College’s Board of Governors she helped deliver real action on housing, leading the charge towards 101 units of affordable student housing announced this spring for the Penticton campus.

Tina Lee, David Eby and the BC NDP have a plan to create jobs, protect healthcare, and make life more affordable.
Pitch summary: Okanagan College board member who pushed for 101 affordable student housing units in Penticton. She was the 2024 NDP candidate (about 300 votes behind) and stepped in after incumbent Amelia Boultbee withdrew. She is running on affordable housing, mental health supports, strong public services and dignity for seniors.
Key priorities: affordable housing;mental health supports;strong public services;seniors aging with dignity;care when people need it;standing up for working people
Quote: People in Penticton-Summerland deserve a representative that will stand up for affordable housing, mental health supports and strong public services.

Name: Warren Hamm
Bio:
Warren Hamm has spent his life building things, fixing problems, and getting the job done, not building a political career.

A contractor, licensed aircraft maintenance engineer, and small-business owner, Warren has more than 30 years of hands-on experience in aviation, construction, resources, and emergency response. His work has taken him across British Columbia, from Dawson Creek and Prince Rupert to Campbell River and the West Kootenay, including helicopter maintenance supporting firefighting operations.

Born in Vancouver and raised in the Cariboo, Warren has lived the realities of communities across this province. After more than 25 years in the West Kootenay, he and his family now call the South Okanagan home.

He knows what it takes to start a business, meet a payroll, work with your hands, solve problems under pressure and deliver when people are counting on you.

Warren is a husband and father of two daughters, both trained as nurses. He believes British Columbia needs to get back to building more homes, stronger communities, thriving small businesses and a resource economy that creates opportunity and prosperity.

His message is simple: cut the red tape, get government out of the way, and put “builders – not bureaucrats” in charge of getting British Columbia moving again.

Warren was the first candidate to declare for the 2026 BC Conservative leadership race. Now, he is proud to be a OneBC candidate for Penticton–Summerland.

He’s spent 30 years building British Columbia. Now he’s ready to fight for its future.
Pitch summary: Contractor, aircraft maintenance engineer and small business owner with 30 years in aviation, construction, resources and wildfire support. He was the first declared candidate in the 2026 Conservative leadership race. His message: cut red tape, get government out of the way, and put 'builders – not bureaucrats' in charge of more homes, small business and a resource economy.
Key priorities: cut red tape;build more homes;small business;resource economy;'builders not bureaucrats'
Quote: His message is simple: cut the red tape, get government out of the way, and put “builders – not bureaucrats” in charge of getting British Columbia moving again.

Name: Keenan Adams
Bio:
Keenan Adams has called Port Coquitlam home since 2010, where he lives with his wife, Florence.

That same year, Keenan graduated from the Railway Conductor program at the British Columbia Institute of Technology and began a career in the local railroad industry. Through hard work and dedication, he advanced from conductor to locomotive engineer, and today he helps train the next generation of railway workers. His career has given him a firsthand understanding of the industry that keeps goods, jobs, and the Lower Mainland moving.

Alongside his work on the railway, Keenan pursued further education in public relations. He also serves as Local President of Teamsters Canada Rail Conference Local 320, where he represents his fellow workers and advocates for safe, fair and well-paying jobs. His leadership in the labour movement reflects a simple belief: working people deserve a strong voice, both on the job and in government.

Keenan is deeply invested in his community. He volunteers frequently with the PoCo Lions Club, takes part in the City of Port Coquitlam’s Adopt-A-Spot program and joins local river cleanups to help keep the city’s natural spaces clean and healthy for families to enjoy.
Pitch summary: Railway locomotive engineer and Teamsters Canada Rail Conference Local 320 president, running again after his 2024 Conservative campaign. His party bio stresses that working people deserve a strong voice in government. In his 2024 campaign video he pledged to move the MLA office downtown and focus on a diverse economy, seniors and the cost of living and housing (2024).
Key priorities: cost of living and housing (2024);strong diverse economy with the environment in mind (2024);care for elders and vulnerable (2024);move MLA office to downtown PoCo (2024);voice for working people/labour
Quote: His leadership in the labour movement reflects a simple belief: working people deserve a strong voice, both on the job and in government.

Name: Stephanie Hendy
Pitch summary: no individual pitch found. Confirmed BC Green candidate on the Elections BC list; no bio, website or social posts located.

Name: Lewis Dahlby
Pitch summary: Party bio (best available): Lewis Dahlby, 70, runs a trucking and excavating business. The Libertarian page says he believes greater personal and economic freedom increases overall prosperity. He also ran federally in 2025.
Key priorities: personal and economic freedom (party bio)
Quote: Lewis believes greater personal and economic freedom increases overall prosperity.

Name: Mike Farnworth
Bio:
Mike Farnworth: Protecting what families rely on in Port Coquitlam

Mike Farnworth has proudly called Port Coquitlam home for more than 50 years. Raised in our community, he has spent decades serving British Columbians in a variety of leadership roles, including several senior cabinet positions, and most recently as Minister of Transportation.

A strong advocate for Port Coquitlam, Mike served three terms as a City Councillor before being elected MLA in 1991. Since then, voters have re-elected him six times.

Throughout his career, Mike has remained committed to the community he calls home. He understands local priorities and has always put Port Coquitlam first.

Whether championing strong public healthcare and education, improving transportation, protecting the environment, or advancing justice reforms, Mike has a proven record of delivering results for local residents.

The BC Conservatives may want to cozy up to Trump and cut the things British Columbians value, but Mike Farnworth, David Eby and the BC NDP have a plan: to stand up for BC and for Canada, to protect the services that people need, and to build the infrastructure and economy we need for a stronger future.

The plan is working. We can’t stop now.
Pitch summary: Long-time MLA (since 1991) and most recently Minister of Transportation, seeking re-election in his home community of 50+ years. His campaign page cites his record on health care, education, transportation, environment and justice reform, and frames the race as protecting services against Conservative cuts (party message).
Key priorities: protect public health care and education;transportation/infrastructure;environment;justice reform;stand up to Trump/tariffs (party message)
Quote: Mike Farnworth: Protecting what families rely on in Port Coquitlam

Name: Lee-Ann Bates
Pitch summary: no individual pitch found. Listed as unaffiliated candidate by Elections BC; no bio or campaign material located.

Name: Freddy Rawji
Bio:
Freddy Rawji was born and raised in Port Moody and graduated from Port Moody Secondary School as the 2010 valedictorian. After earning a BSc in Economics from the University of Victoria, he built a career in recruitment focused on the engineering and construction management sectors.

In 2018, Freddy joined RAM Consulting and helped the company scale from 15 to 100 people as it delivered one of Metro Vancouver’s largest industrial projects, supplying aviation fuel to YVR. He also launched RAM’s electric vehicle charging infrastructure design service.

In December 2020, Freddy founded Torus Talent, a recruitment and leadership consulting firm that specializes in technical talent. In under six years, he has grown it to 20 headcount and $5 million in annual revenue, working with some of BC’s largest companies as well as start-ups.

Freddy is passionate about making BC a better place to do business. His own path has convinced him that small businesses are best placed to innovate and create high-paying jobs, and that a stronger economy is what pays for the social services British Columbians rely on.

He is running with CentreBC because he believes the other parties are rowing in opposite directions, while most British Columbians are in the middle. Freddy believes in progress, but in progress that is thought through and guided by science and data, not political ideology.
Pitch summary: Port Moody-raised recruitment entrepreneur (founder of Torus Talent) running for CentreBC. He argues small businesses create high-paying jobs and a stronger economy pays for social services, and says he wants evidence-based progress rather than ideology.
Key priorities: support small business and economy;fund social services through growth;science- and data-guided policy;centrist alternative
Quote: Freddy believes in progress, but in progress that is thought through and guided by science and data, not political ideology.

Name: John McEwen
Bio:
John McEwen is the Conservative Party fo BC Candidate for Port Moody-Burquitlam

John has called Anmore home for more than 20 years and has spent much of that time serving the community and the broader region. John served 18 years on Anmore Council, including 12 years as Mayor. When he was first elected 18 years ago, the Village faced an infrastructure deficit of approximately $10 million and had limited revenue sources. John worked with Council and staff to develop a long-term financial plan focused on responsible fiscal management and building sustainable reserves. Today, Anmore’s infrastructure has been brought up to municipal standards and the Village has more than $10 million in reserve. 

John has also held significant regional leadership positions. For the past four years, he has been elected by his peers on the Metro Vancouver Board to serve as Vice Chair. For the past eight years, he has chaired the Metro Vancouver Parks Committee, where he helped oversee an unprecedented expansion of the regional parks land inventory. He has also served as a member of the Mayor’s Council on TransLink and is a Trustee with the Municipal Finance Authority of British Columbia.

John created and owned two small businesses, both of which he subsequently sold. This experience has given him a practical understanding of business, investment, employment and the challenges facing small-business owners.

After 18 years in municipal government, John has decided to step forward at the provincial level because he believes British Columbia needs practical solutions, responsible fiscal management and leadership grounded in real-world experience.

John is running to bring his municipal, regional and business experience to the Legislature and to be a strong, independent voice for the residents of Port Moody-Burquitlam.
Pitch summary: Former Anmore mayor (12 years) and Metro Vancouver Board vice-chair. He points to bringing Anmore's infrastructure up to standard while building over $10 million in reserves, and says he is running for practical solutions and responsible fiscal management.
Key priorities: responsible fiscal management;practical solutions;regional parks/infrastructure experience;small business;independent voice for riding
Quote: John is running to bring his municipal, regional and business experience to the Legislature and to be a strong, independent voice for the residents of Port Moody-Burquitlam.

Name: Wei Chou
Pitch summary: no individual pitch found. Confirmed BC Green candidate on the Elections BC list; no bio or campaign material located.

Name: Rick Glumac
Bio:
Rick Glumac: Standing up for people in Port Moody-Burquitlam

Rick Glumac is a three-term MLA with a long record of standing up for people and local businesses. His work in government has focused on economic development, technology and trade, serving as Minister of State for AI and New Technologies, Minister of State for Trade, and Parliamentary Secretary for Technology.

Rick also served as President of the Pacific NorthWest Economic Region, championing stronger cross-border cooperation and Canadian interests. Before public service, he worked in the tech sector in computer animation and video games, including on films like Shrek 2 and Madagascar.

As a Port Moody City Councillor and MLA, Rick has worked to improve healthcare and childcare, helped establish Port Moody’s Urgent and Primary Care Centre, and helped stop the sale of lands around Eagle Ridge Hospital, preserving them for future hospital expansion.

A Port Moody resident for more than 20 years, Rick raised his family here and is proud to keep working hard for Port Moody–Burquitlam.

Rick Glumac will never stop fighting for Port Moody-Burquitlam, and he's ready to keep building BC strong with David Eby.
Pitch summary: Three-term MLA and Minister of State for AI and New Technologies, formerly a tech/animation worker. His page highlights helping set up Port Moody's Urgent and Primary Care Centre and stopping the sale of land around Eagle Ridge Hospital to keep it for expansion.
Key priorities: health care (Eagle Ridge Hospital expansion lands, urgent care);childcare;economic development, technology and trade;stand with Eby (party message)
Quote: Rick Glumac will never stop fighting for Port Moody-Burquitlam, and he's ready to keep building BC strong with David Eby.

Name: John Henderson
Bio:
John Henderson is the Conservative Party of BC candidate for Powell River-Sunshine Coast.

John is currently finishing his second term as Mayor of the District of Sechelt. During his first term, he led the team that designed, funded and built the award winning SecheltWater Resource Centre, which treats wastewater to amongst the highest standards in Canada. Re-elected in 2022, John has advocated strongly for the needs of rural communities across Canada.

His service to the Coast extends beyond municipal government. He was chair of the Sunshine Coast Community Forest, and served on the board of BC Ferries for 2004 to 2008. He also chaired the Sechelt Sewage Facilities Commission in partnership with the Sechelt Indian Government District. He has served as a director of the Sunshine Coast Golf & Country Club, and coached Sunshine Coast youth soccer. In 2012, John’s service to his community was recognized with the Queen’s Diamond Jubilee Medal. John believes the Sunshine Coast can lead the province, not follow it.

John pairs his passion for community service with nearly 50 years of business experience, including 20 years based in Hong Kong. John earned a Bachelor of Commerce degree from UBC in 1977 and his Chartered Accountant designation in 1979. In 1997, he was awarded the prestigious Fellow of the Institute of Chartered Accountants designation.
Pitch video title: Sechelt Mayor & Conservative Candidate John Henderson on Indigenous Relations & Politics (The New Westminster Times)
Pitch summary: Outgoing two-term Sechelt mayor and chartered accountant, recruited after the snap election was called. He told local papers he will focus on community safety and support for municipalities, ferry reliability (including buying used vessels), and transparency about provincial debt.
Key priorities: community safety and neighbours near supportive housing;end downloading onto municipalities;BC Ferries: new/used vessels, backup capacity;provincial debt and transparency
Quote: We’ve got to get real about what it takes to run a ferry system,

Name: Griffin Leonard Lea

Name: Randene Neill
Bio:
Randene Neill: Protecting the services families count on in Powell River-Sunshine Coast

Randene Neill was elected as the MLA for Powell River-Sunshine Coast in 2024. In government, she served as BC’s Minister of Water, Land and Resource Stewardship.

Prior to public life, Randene worked as a journalist at Global BC for nearly two decades, reporting and anchoring for the Noon Newshour, Weekend Newshour, and Newshour Final. She also worked as a communications consultant for organizations that include te BC Parks Foundation and the new St. Paul’s Hospital.

She lives on the beautiful Sunshine Coast with her partner and two (mostly) good dogs.

Where the Conservatives would cut services and cozy up to Trump, Randene Neill, David Eby and the BC NDP have a plan to stand up for families, protect the services that matter, and build our economy so we are strong in the face of threats.

The plan is working. And we can’t stop now.
Pitch summary: First-term MLA (2024) and Minister of Water, Land and Resource Stewardship, a former Global BC journalist living in Pender Harbour. Her launch statement focuses on standing up for B.C. against Trump's economic threats while protecting the environment; her campaign page frames the race as protecting services from Conservative cuts (party message).
Key priorities: stand up to Trump/tariffs (party message);protect environment and stewardship;protect public services (party message)
Quote: We’re fighting for a more resilient B.C. where we are good stewards of the place we call home,

Name: Kiel Giddens
Bio:
Kiel Giddens is a dad to two young boys, Thomas and Charlie. He and his wife Elyse have chosen to make Prince George their home to work, raise their children, and provide every opportunity they possibly can for their kids’ futures.

Career and Community Involvement 

Kiel has spent over a decade building Northern opportunities as part of the largest private sector investment in Canadian history in bringing a brand-new LNG industry to British Columbia and Canada. He has spent time in communities across the North building partnerships, engaging stakeholders, and connecting economic opportunities for job-seekers and businesses.

As a Past-President of the Prince George Chamber of Commerce, he has been an advocate for small businesses and jobs in Prince George and the region. Kiel currently serves on the Board of Directors for Spirit of the North Healthcare Foundation. He has also served as a representative on the Premier’s LNG Labour Working Group, the College of New Caledonia President’s Industry Council, and the Regional District of Bulkley-Nechako Strategic Workforce Opportunities Team.

Aside from his time in the private sector, Kiel has held senior roles in previous governments. As Chief of Staff to the Minister of Environment, he supported the
former government’s mandate to reduce red tape in environmental assessments, and to enhance environmental stewardship. Immediately prior to the 2013 election, Kiel was Chief of Staff to the Minister of Transportation & Infrastructure and negotiated with federal government representatives to fast-track spending on projects like the Cariboo Connector and South Taylor Hill in the Peace. He also held roles in the Ministry of Forests, Lands, and Natural Resource Operations, and the Ministry of Labour, and has experience in topics such as wildlife management policy, forest policy, climate policy, WorkSafe BC policy, and construction labour relations policy.

Vision 

Kiel is a strong voice for Northern British Columbia, and wants Prince George, Mackenzie, and the Northern region to grow and prosper. As a Father, he is driven to find ways to make life more affordable for families. He believes in respect for taxpayers, enhancing community safety, tackling pressing healthcare issues, strengthening mental health and addiction support systems, championing our resource sectors, and building job opportunities for people to get ahead.
Pitch summary: First-term Conservative MLA and the party's election readiness chair, formerly in the LNG sector and Prince George Chamber past-president. At his Oct 2 launch he said resource-sector jobs, especially forestry, will be central, along with cardiac care for the north and continued University Hospital of Northern B.C. expansion.
Key priorities: protect forestry and resource-sector jobs;long-term forestry stabilization plan;cardiac care in northern BC;UHNBC hospital expansion;affordability for families;community safety;mental health and addictions
Quote: We need to fight tooth and nail for resource-sector jobs in this part of the province,

Name: Teri Young
Bio:
Teri holds a Bachelor of Education in Industrial Education from the University of British Columbia. Early in her career, she taught in Gitlax̱t’aamiks Village (New Aiyansh) in Nisga’a territory on the Nass River, before returning to Victoria and continuing to work as a substitute teacher.

She later founded and operated Paxar Technologies Corp, a national software distribution company that she successfully ran for more than 30 years before retiring in 2018. Her experience as a small-business owner gave her firsthand experience with managing employees, adapting to change and building a business over the long term.

Teri now lives on a small hobby farm in Cowichan Bay, where she raises chickens and supports local agriculture. She is passionate about food security, local farming and protecting the natural systems communities depend on.

As a mother of three adult children and a grandmother, Teri is focused on the kind of future younger generations will inherit. She is running in Prince George-Mackenzie to advocate for clean energy, good jobs, strong social supports and safe, resilient communities.
Pitch summary: Retired software-company founder and former teacher who lives on a hobby farm in Cowichan Bay (per her bio). Her bio says she is running to advocate for clean energy, good jobs, strong social supports and safe, resilient communities, with a focus on food security.
Key priorities: clean energy;good jobs;strong social supports;safe, resilient communities;food security and local farming
Quote: She is running in Prince George-Mackenzie to advocate for clean energy, good jobs, strong social supports and safe, resilient communities.

Name: Sheldon Clare
Bio:
Born and bred in the heart of Prince George, British Columbia, Sheldon Clare’s deep roots in the community have shaped his unwavering commitment to the betterment of Prince George-North Cariboo. A loving father to two daughters, Elise and Danielle, Sheldon’s life is dedicated to both his family and the community he proudly calls home.

A Scholarly Journey with a Passion for Education

Sheldon’s academic journey is marked by excellence. He holds a Bachelor of Arts degree in International Relations from the esteemed University of British Columbia. Furthermore, his passion for military history led him to achieve cum laude honors for his Master of Arts degree from Norwich University.

Dedicated to the Classroom

Since 1993, Sheldon has been an integral part of the College of New Caledonia (CNC), where he has played a pivotal role in shaping young minds. As an educator, his dedication goes beyond teaching, as he served as a contract negotiator for 12 years. His leadership qualities shone through with six terms as the chair of the provincial Bargaining Co-ordination Committee, ensuring the welfare of educators across the province. Sheldon’s commitment extended to serving on the CNC Board of Governors, where his insights and vision contributed to the institution’s growth and development.

A Defender of Canadian Values

Sheldon’s service to the nation extends beyond the classroom. As a reserve army officer, he dedicated over seven years to instructing cadets, instilling discipline and leadership in the next generation of Canadian citizens. His advocacy successfully led to the establishment of a reserve infantry unit in Prince George, bolstering the region’s contribution to national security.

A Musician and Sports Enthusiast

Sheldon’s passion for music has found expression as a piper, playing with the local pipe band since his teenage years. His love for the outdoors is evident through his interests in hunting, shooting, and both downhill and cross-country skiing. Sheldon’s dedication to sports goes beyond participation; he is a certified Biathlon Canada Technical Delegate and trained coach. His commitment to the sport is reflected in his service on the board of Biathlon BC.

A Community Leader with a Heart of Gold

Sheldon’s leadership extends to various community organizations. He served two terms as the president of Royal Canadian Legion Branch 43 in Prince George and continues to hold the esteemed position of Legion Chair. Additionally, he played a pivotal role as the national president of Canada’s National Firearms Association from 2010 to 2021, advocating for responsible firearms ownership.

As a past multi-term president and current director at large of the PG Rod and Gun Club, Sheldon contributes significantly to the outdoor and recreational community in Prince George. He is a seasoned adventurer, having enjoyed caving, ice climbing, and mountaineering. His commitment to outdoor pursuits is exemplified by his three-term chairmanship of the Prince George Section of the Alpine Club of Canada.

Sheldon Clare’s involvement as a key organizer for the rejuvenated Northern Hardware Canoe Race from 2015 to 2019 demonstrates his dedication to preserving local traditions and fostering community connections. His multifaceted leadership and unwavering commitment make him an exceptional MLA for the Conservative Party of BC in Prince George-North Cariboo. Sheldon Clare brings his rich experience and passion for community service to the forefront, ensuring a brighter future for the people of Prince George-North Cariboo.
Pitch summary: First-term Conservative MLA, longtime College of New Caledonia instructor, former reserve army officer and past president of the National Firearms Association. He entered the Conservative leadership race in January 2026. His party page is biographical and highlights community leadership; his MLA channel covers forestry and his 2025 throne speech response.
Key priorities: forestry (MLA video);outdoor/firearms community advocacy;education;veterans/Legion
Quote: Sheldon Clare brings his rich experience and passion for community service to the forefront, ensuring a brighter future for the people of Prince George-North Cariboo.

Name: Rosalyn Bird
Bio:
Rosalyn Bird was elected as the Member of the Legislative Assembly for Prince George-Valemount in November 2024, bringing more than two decades of Canadian Armed Forces service and a lifelong commitment to leadership, accountability and public service to the Legislature.

Since her election, Rosalyn has worked to be a strong and accessible voice for Prince George, Valemount, McBride and communities throughout the Robson Valley, while ensuring the priorities of Northern and rural British Columbia are heard in Victoria.

During her first term, Rosalyn served as Official Opposition Whip and held critic responsibilities for Citizens’ Services, Children and Family Development, Community Safety and Integrated Services, and Armed Forces Development and Veteran Affairs. She has also served on several legislative committees, where she developed a strong appreciation for detailed legislative review, government accountability and constructive collaboration across party lines.

One of Rosalyn’s proudest accomplishments was successfully sponsoring the Veterans and First Responders Act in 2026. The Private Member’s Bill received unanimous support in the Legislative Assembly and formally recognizes the service and sacrifice of British Columbia’s veterans, Canadian Armed Forces members and first responders.

Rosalyn has also advanced a long-term economic vision for Prince George and Northern British Columbia through her proposal for an Integrated Northern Defence, Training and Trade Hub. The initiative builds upon the region’s strategic location, transportation infrastructure and skilled workforce, with the goal of attracting investment, diversifying the Northern economy and creating stable, family-supporting careers for generations to come.

Before entering provincial politics, Rosalyn served for more than twenty years in the Canadian Armed Forces. She began her career as a Boatswain, later became a Resource Management Clerk, and in 2005 was commissioned from the ranks as a Naval Logistics Officer. Her career included service at CFS Alert, deployments aboard Royal Canadian Navy ships and support for NATO operations.

Her military service helped shape the values she continues to bring to public life: duty, loyalty, integrity and courage.

Rosalyn’s work as MLA has been grounded in listening to constituents, advocating for communities that too often feel overlooked, and pursuing practical solutions. Her priorities have included safer communities, veterans and first responders, stronger public services, government accountability, economic development, and resource and infrastructure investment.

Rosalyn is seeking re-election with a desire to continue serving the people of Prince George-Valemount and strengthening the voice of Northern British Columbia. She believes public service is both a privilege and a responsibility and that the decisions made today must create opportunity, stability and stronger communities for the generations that follow.
Pitch summary: First-term MLA and 20-year Canadian Armed Forces veteran who left the Conservatives for CentreBC in August 2026 and has since returned to run as a Conservative. Her party page highlights her unanimously passed Veterans and First Responders Act and a proposed Integrated Northern Defence, Training and Trade Hub to diversify the northern economy.
Key priorities: safer communities;veterans and first responders;stronger public services;government accountability;Northern Defence, Training and Trade Hub/economic development;resource and infrastructure investment
Quote: Her priorities have included safer communities, veterans and first responders, stronger public services, government accountability, economic development, and resource and infrastructure investment.
