Quote: I’ve spent my career inside the system, now I’m ready to help fix it.

Name: Mitchell Lukoni
Bio:
Born and raised in Prince George, Mitchell has spent his working life in Northern British Columbia.

He holds a Bachelor of General Studies from Athabasca University, with concentrations in psychology and political philosophy. He has volunteered in his community as a UNBC Faculty of Science and Engineering student senator and in child and family grief support with the Prince George Hospice Palliative Care Society.

Mitchell has deep ties working and volunteering with federal Conservative and grassroots conservative movements in British Columbia through years of campaign work, organizing, and volunteering. He currently works as a business, communications, and policy strategist.

A father, Mitchell believes in small government, accountability, tax cuts, cutting red tape, reviving the resource economy, backing small business, defending families, and putting Northern communities — not Victoria bureaucracy — first.

Mitchell Lukoni is now the proud OneBC candidate for Prince George–Valemount.
Pitch summary: Prince George-born business, communications and policy strategist with years of conservative campaign work. His OneBC page lists small government, tax cuts, cutting red tape, reviving the resource economy and putting Northern communities first.
Key priorities: small government and accountability;tax cuts;cut red tape;revive resource economy;back small business;defend families;Northern communities first
Quote: A father, Mitchell believes in small government, accountability, tax cuts, cutting red tape, reviving the resource economy, backing small business, defending families, and putting Northern communities — not Victoria bureaucracy — first.

Name: Sacha Peter
Bio:
Sacha is a Chartered Professional Accountant specializing in corporate taxation. Born and raised in Richmond, where he still lives, he graduated from the University of British Columbia with a Bachelor of Science in Physics and is the father of two teenage sons. Peter will be a strong advocate for Richmond. 

Since 2009, Sacha has written about Canadian finance, economics, politics and the ups and downs of investing in the capital markets at Divestor.com. He also hosts the Late Night Finance show.

Sacha’s record of public service reflects a deep commitment to accountability. He has served on many boards and committees, most notably the Cultus Lake Park Board. Elected twice, he served for six years, including three as Chair, and led the board in eliminating its budget deficit.

As the MLA for Richmond Centre, Sacha will scrutinize the provincial budget the way he has scrutinized publicly traded companies for nearly two decades: following the numbers, demanding accountability and exposing waste wherever he finds it.
Pitch summary: Richmond-born chartered professional accountant specializing in corporate tax, finance writer (Divestor.com) and former Cultus Lake Park Board chair who says he eliminated that board's deficit. His pitch is budget scrutiny, accountability and exposing waste.
Key priorities: scrutinize provincial budget;accountability;expose government waste;strong advocate for Richmond
Quote: As the MLA for Richmond Centre, Sacha will scrutinize the provincial budget the way he has scrutinized publicly traded companies for nearly two decades: following the numbers, demanding accountability and exposing waste wherever he finds it.

Name: Teresa Wat
Bio:
Teresa Wat has served as the Member of the Legislative Assembly (MLA) for Richmond Centre since 2013, winning re-election in 2017 and 2020. She ran and won re-election in the Richmond-Bridgeport district in 2024.

Wat has held several key roles, including Shadow Minister for Tourism, Arts and Culture, and Multiculturalism. Since 2017, she has been the Shadow Minister for Multiculturalism and a member of the Select Standing Committee on Children and Youth.

Between 2013 and 2017, Wat was the Minister of International Trade and the Minister Responsible for the Asia Pacific Strategy and Multiculturalism. She also contributed to the Cabinet Committee on Strong Economy and the Priorities and Planning Committee.

Before entering politics, Wat was the News Director at Channel M Television (now OMNI TV), where she helped launch the first live Cantonese, Mandarin, and Punjabi daily news programs in British Columbia. She also served as the News Editor for Ming Pao Daily News and as President and CEO of Mainstream Broadcasting Corporation, a multicultural broadcasting station. Prior to immigrating to Canada in 1989, she had a distinguished career in the communications industry in Hong Kong and Singapore.

Wat’s achievements have been recognized with the Grand Officer of the Order of the Crown, one of the highest honours from the Kingdom of Belgium, and the Queen’s Diamond Jubilee Award for her community service. She has also been named one of BC’s top 100 most influential women by the Vancouver Sun and one of Greater Vancouver’s top 33 most outstanding Chinese Canadians by Sing Tao Daily Vancouver.
Pitch summary: Longtime Richmond MLA (since 2013) and former International Trade minister, previously a multicultural broadcasting executive. She left the Conservative caucus in August over Kerry-Lynne Findlay's leadership but is running for re-election in Richmond-Bridgeport as a Conservative. No 2026 pitch found; her party page is biographical.
Key priorities: multiculturalism;experience/record serving Richmond
Quote: I'm humbled to serve the people of Richmond

Name: Steve Kooner
Bio:
Professional Background:

Steve Kooner is a well known successful lawyer who has owned his own law firm, Steve Kooner Law Corporation, for over 17 years. Steve prides himself with being a solution oriented problem solving lawyer in the litigation area. Steve has a Bachelor of Arts degree with a Major in Political Science from Simon Fraser University and a Juris Doctor law degree from the University of Calgary. Steve and his law firm have received legal service awards such as Three Best Rated Award and Consumer Choice Award in recent years. Steve has also given back to the legal profession by providing mentorship to countless number of aspiring lawyers in the community and by formally taking on many articled students through the Law Society of British Columbia Admissions Program.

Community Involvement:

In addition to being a practicing lawyer, Steve is known for his significant community involvement. Steve has helped countless community organizations with community connecting and spreading awareness. Steve regularly engages in public speaking at events held by community organizations. Steve has spoken at community events of various sizes, which includes anywhere from a few people in a conference room to massive crowds in an arena.  In 2023, Steve was awarded the Queen’s Platinum Jubilee Award by the Government of Canada for his significant community contribution. Also in 2023, Steve was named an Ambassador to a BCHL Junior Hockey Club.

Personal Background:

Steve was born in Vancouver and grew up in the lower mainland of British Columbia. Steve was born into an iconic music family, as Steve’s father is a former superstar Punjabi recording artist, who recorded with EMI and who had many hit songs in the 1980s. As a child, Steve’s parents taught him the value of hard work and generous giving. In line with this thinking, Steve was enrolled in the martial art of Taekwondo as a young child and he achieved a black belt at the age of 11. Steve was also always seen with his dad as a child learning about the music industry within the community.

Passion to Serve:

Steve has a passion to continue serving the community to make a difference.
Pitch summary: First-term Conservative MLA and litigation lawyer who owns his own law firm. No 2026 campaign pitch found; his party page is biographical. As MLA he has spoken out in 2026 about property rights after the Cowichan title case and about extortion threats against lawyers (video titles).
Key priorities: property rights / Cowichan title case concerns;extortion and public safety;community service
Quote: Steve has a passion to continue serving the community to make a difference.

Name: Barry Wosk
Bio:
Barry Wosk is a lifelong Richmond resident who calls the Steveston area home.

Raised in Westwind, he is a proud Steveston High School graduate – GO PACKERS! His mother still lives in his childhood home after more than 50 years and his roots in the community continue today, living and working in the riding with his wife and two teenage children.

A graduate of the University of British Columbia with a Bachelor of Commerce degree, Barry has spent more than three decades building and operating a successful Richmond-based small business. As an entrepreneur, he has developed expertise in strategic planning, finance, sales, marketing, operations, and manufacturing. He has also provided consulting for foreign organizations looking to grow their footprint in Canada.

Having travelled extensively throughout Canada, the United States, and internationally, Barry has gained a broad appreciation for different perspectives, cultures, and communities. Those experiences have reinforced his belief that Richmond is the best place in the world to live, work, and to raise a family. He values the city’s diversity, natural beauty, enterprising spirit, and unique role as Canada’s gateway to the Pacific.

Barry is seeking public office because he believes British Columbians deserve better governance that focuses on results rather than division. He believes government should be financially responsible, socially inclusive, and environmentally sustainable. He is committed to strengthening the economy, improving access to healthcare, building safer communities, addressing housing affordability, and working collaboratively with local governments to deliver better outcomes for residents and is committed to building a stronger future for Richmond and British Columbia.

The political status quo is over. It’s time for civility, strong leadership, and practical solutions to complex problems. It’s time for something new.

Sign up to stay informed and receive news from CentreBC:
Pitch summary: Lifelong Steveston-area resident, Richmond small-business owner for over 30 years and former Richmond Chamber of Commerce director. He says he is running for results-focused, civil governance that is financially responsible, socially inclusive and environmentally sustainable.
Key priorities: strengthen the economy;improve access to health care;safer communities;housing affordability;collaboration with local governments
Quote: The political status quo is over. It’s time for civility, strong leadership, and practical solutions to complex problems. It’s time for something new.

Name: Gordon Zhang
Bio:
Gordon Zhang is the Conservative Party of BC candidate for Richmond-Steveston.

Zhang is a community leader with deep roots in Richmond and across the Lower Mainland’s Chinese-Canadian community. For more than seventeen years, he has taught business at Kwantlen Polytechnic University’s Richmond campus, helping prepare students for careers in B.C.’s economy.

Alongside his teaching, Gordon is an entrepreneur who has co-founded several Canadian companies. When the COVID-19 pandemic exposed Canada’s dependence on imported protective equipment, he helped establish one of the country’s first domestic N95 respirator production lines, supplying certified respiratory protection to the Canadian Olympic Team at the 2021 Tokyo Games. He also built one of only three laboratories in Canada accredited to test respirators and medical masks, strengthening the country’s ability to verify the safety of equipment frontline workers rely on.

That experience gave Gordon a firsthand understanding of what it takes to build in British Columbia: the value of domestic manufacturing, the importance of secure supply chains, and the challenges businesses face in getting new ventures off the ground.

Gordon has given back to the community he calls home. Through the local Lions Club, he has raised funds for the Richmond Hospital Foundation and other local causes, and he has lent his organizing experience to community and technology events across Metro Vancouver.

Gordon will bring an educator’s perspective, an entrepreneur’s drive and a deep commitment to community service to Victoria. He will be a strong voice for Richmond families and businesses, and for an economy that makes things here at home.
Pitch summary: Kwantlen Polytechnic business instructor and entrepreneur who helped set up a domestic N95 respirator production line and testing lab in Richmond. His party page pitches domestic manufacturing, secure supply chains and help for businesses getting started.
Key priorities: domestic manufacturing (make things at home);secure supply chains;support for new businesses;voice for Richmond families and businesses
Quote: He will be a strong voice for Richmond families and businesses, and for an economy that makes things here at home.

Name: Richard Smith
Bio:
Dr. Richard Smith is research scientist and project manager. His field of expertise is in Immunology/Microbiology. He received his PhD from the University of British Columbia and was awarded a Post-doctoral fellowship from the National Institutes of Health (Bethesda MD) for further studies at the Scripps Medical Research Laboratories (La Jolla CA). From there he worked for a biotechnology company developing patented, ground-breaking technology for in vitro diagnostic tests detecting human pathogens.

This early work led to the publication of over 20 peer reviewed scientific articles and a family of more than 21 international patents.

More recently Dr. Smith managed large multi-national life science projects for Defence R&D Canada and the Canadian Forces Health Services Group. These projects led to the development of vaccines and broad spectrum anti-viral drugs. During his tenure with the DRDC, he led a NATO study group examining new technologies for use in medical countermeasures. In preparation for the 2010 Olympic Games, Richard led a risk assessment team examining possible bio-chem threats and their mitigation.

Dr. Smith was recently part of a nation-wide group developing a framework for reducing the price of biologic drugs. Working with the BC Ministry of Health and representatives from all provinces and territories, a new strategy was developed to reduce the cost of biologics by 80%. He also served as a contract tracer and case manager with Island Health during the COVID epidemic.

Richard is married and has 5 beautiful daughters. He enjoys sailing, gardening, cycling and spending time with four grandchildren.

Richard chose to be a candidate with Centre BC because he agrees with their pragmatic and accountable philosophy of governing. He hopes that his scientific training will bring logic and rigour to the development and implementation of policies that are positive and provide opportunities for every British Colombian.
Pitch summary: Immunology/microbiology research scientist who managed vaccine and antiviral projects for Defence R&D Canada and worked on a national framework to cut biologic drug prices. He says he chose CentreBC for its pragmatic, accountable approach and wants to bring scientific rigour to policymaking.
Key priorities: pragmatic and accountable government;evidence-based/scientific policymaking;health/drug costs (background)
Quote: He hopes that his scientific training will bring logic and rigour to the development and implementation of policies that are positive and provide opportunities for every British Colombian.

Name: Ryan Windsor
Bio:
Mayor Ryan Windsor is the BC Conservative candidate for Saanich North and the Islands.

Ryan brings more than a decade of local leadership to the Conservative team. First elected to Central Saanich council in a 2013 by-election, he was elected Mayor in 2014 and returned by acclamation in 2018 and 2022. Over 12 years at the helm, Ryan championed fair governance and fiscally responsible management of infrastructure and services, building long-term funding for the essential water and sewer systems that residents count on every day.

Ryan also served as a director on the Capital Regional District board, working with neighbouring municipalities on the issues that matter most to the South Island. He has been a strong supporter of local food production and the farms that define the Saanich Peninsula, and led work to make roads and trails safer for families getting around the community.

Before entering public life, Ryan worked in the private sector and in his family’s business.
Pitch summary: Central Saanich mayor since 2014 and former Capital Regional District director. The party pitch highlights fiscally responsible management of infrastructure, long-term water and sewer funding, support for Peninsula farms and local food, and safer roads and trails.
Key priorities: fiscally responsible infrastructure management;water and sewer funding;local food production and farms;safer roads and trails;regional cooperation
Quote: Over 12 years at the helm, Ryan championed fair governance and fiscally responsible management of infrastructure and services, building long-term funding for the essential water and sewer systems that residents count on every day.

Name: Emily Lowan
Bio:
Hi, I’m Emily Lowan and I’m running to be your MLA for Saanich North and the Islands.

I feel so lucky to have spent my youth crabbing with my dad off the Sidney pier, camping with my family in Ruckle Park, and snorkelling at Ardmore Beach. I grew up with a reverence for this coastline and the people who’ve built their lives around it. I’ve watched this community do what the government wouldn’t. When the Peninsula was staring down a lost generation of family doctors, neighbours built Shoreline Medical Society from nothing and turned five doctors into twenty-five. It’s an incredible achievement, and a beautiful example of what we can get done when people work together.

Loving this place also means seeing clearly what’s happening to it. Healthcare and housing keep drifting further out of reach, as people work harder than ever just to make ends meet. Ferries break down and get cancelled with no real fix in sight. Wildfire smoke settles over these islands more summers than not. Oil tankers keep moving through the Salish Sea while the Southern Resident orca population—down to just 74 whales—barely hangs on.

I’m running because I see the same challenges you do, and I have the experience, grit, and determination to fight alongside you. I’m running to make sure you can afford to build a life, you get care when you need it, and that the people you love and the planet you stand on are protected, this generation and the next.

I’ve spent my entire life fighting for better—for people, our planet, and our province. I’m a coalition builder, bringing groups together, from rural to urban, labour to environmental, to build a future where everyone, not just the fortunate few, gets to thrive. I’ve worked across the country, leading coalitions with labour, Indigenous nations, and environmental groups to advocate for federal pollution regulations as the fossil fuel supply campaigns lead for Climate Action Network Canada. I’ve worked as an investigative researcher with the Canadian Centre for Policy Alternatives’ Corporate Mapping Project, exposing corporate influence in our government and training researchers nationwide. Right here in B.C., I’ve been standing up for affordable housing, accessible healthcare, a fair economy, and a liveable planet as the leader of the BC Greens.

I feel incredibly honoured to step into the legacy of Adam Olsen and Rob Botterell, passionate advocates for their communities who proved what Green representation delivers, election after election. I’m honoured to work to carry that legacy forward.

I’m a renter, an organizer, a Saanich Fair enthusiast (I’ve been every single year!), and I’m the leader of the BC Greens. The status quo is failing all of us. I want to be in your corner.

Believe in Better. Vote Green. Vote Emily Lowan.

Join Team Lowan for a morning sign wave in Brentwood Bay! We’ll be meeting at the corner of Wallace Drive and West Saanich Road to make a green splash and

Join Team Lowan for a sign wave in Sidney! We’ll be meeting at the Sidney Information Centre to make a green splash and show support in the community. 📅 When:

Join us on Pender Island for a meet and greet with Emily Lowan, Leader of the BC Greens! This is a great opportunity to meet Emily, hear from her directly,
Pitch video title: Rights for Renters.
Pitch summary: BC Green leader, raised on the Saanich Peninsula, running to succeed retiring Green MLA Adam Olsen. Her pitch centres on affordability, health care access, reliable ferries, renters' rights, free child care, and protecting the coast and Southern Resident orcas from tankers and climate impacts; she frames herself as a coalition builder.
Key priorities: cost of living/affordability;health care access;housing and renters' rights;ferry reliability;universal free child care;protect Salish Sea, orcas and climate;fight corporate/oligarch influence
Quote: I’m running to make sure you can afford to build a life, you get care when you need it, and that the people you love and the planet you stand on are protected, this generation and the next.

Name: Kala Bryson
Pitch summary: Lawyer and community advocate raised in co-op housing and a UVic graduate, named Oct 2. Her launch statement focuses on strengthening public institutions and access to justice, plus good jobs, public health care and help with rising costs (party message).
Key priorities: strengthen public institutions;access to justice;good jobs (party message);public health care (party message);support for families facing rising costs (party message)
Quote: People deserve to know that the institutions they rely on will be there when they need them,

Name: Cathie Ounsted
Bio:
Cathie Ounsted is the Conservative Party candidate for Saanich South with a proven track record of getting things done for her community. 

Cathie brings a breadth of community-building, business and financial oversight experience. She has served as an appointed member of the Central Saanich Police Board, elected to the Peninsula Co-Op Board of Directors, elected to Central Saanich Council, and most recently served 9 years on the Victoria Airport Authority Board of Directors with the last two years being the Chairperson. 

Cathie and her husband Chris also operate Ounsted and Company, a local accounting firm.

Cathie’s other past experience includes owning the Red Barn Market, a Director of Operations for Thrifty Foods and a short stint as a Reserve Constable for the Victoria Police Department.

Cathie’s “strength by example” motto has led her to reach many goals and achievements that have brought her to politics.

Cathie also has extensive volunteer activities for various youth sports activities including Program Co-ordinators for Saanich Peninsula Minor Football and Mt Douglas Rams High School Football. It’s with these programs she has connected with many of the Saanich South’s youth and families. Cathie has lived and worked in Saanich South for over 35 years, where she and her husband raised their two young men, Jake (26) and Matthew (23).
Pitch summary: Former Central Saanich councillor and Victoria Airport Authority board chair running on her local governance, business and financial-oversight experience. In her campaign launch statement she said she is dedicated to improved access to health care, safer communities and a stronger economy.
Key priorities: improved access to health care; safer communities; stronger economy
Quote: Cathie’s “strength by example” motto has led her to reach many goals and achievements that have brought her to politics.

Name: Lisa Lapointe
Bio:
Lisa Lapointe is a lawyer, longtime public servant, and former Chief Coroner of British Columbia who has spent three decades working to support healthier and safer communities across the province.

From 2011 until her retirement in 2024, Lisa served as B.C.’s Chief Coroner, overseeing the independent and objective investigation of unnatural and unexpected deaths across the province. During her tenure, she became known as an advocate for evidence and public-health data informing government decision-making. In 2018, the BC Coroners Service received the inaugural Premier’s Award for Evidence-Based Design for its analysis and timely reporting of illicit drug overdose deaths during the ongoing public-health emergency.

In her tenure, she worked proactively to strengthen relationships with Indigenous communities. In 2017, in partnership with the First Nations Health Authority, she committed the Coroners Service to Cultural Safety and Humility in services for First Nations and Indigenous people in British Columbia. The Coroners Service was the first provincial government agency to make that public commitment.

A graduate of the University of British Columbia Law School, Lisa joined the BC Public Service in 1995 and served in a range of roles before joining the Coroners Service, including the province’s Civil Forfeiture Office. She also served as chair of the Canadian Forum of Chief Coroners and Chief Medical Examiners and of the British Columbia Institute of Technology’s Forensic Science and Technology Program Advisory Committee.

Now a grandmother of five, she is deeply concerned about the future facing younger generations, particularly the growing impacts of climate change and persistent gaps in housing, healthcare, mental-health supports, and other essential public services. She is running to bring her decades of public-service experience, evidence-based approach, and commitment to public health and environmental responsibility to the Legislature.
Pitch video title: Policy Announcement: Addressing the Toxic Drugs Crisis (w/Lisa Lapointe)
Pitch summary: Former BC Chief Coroner (2011-2024) running on public health and evidence-based policy. She launched her candidacy alongside the BC Greens' toxic drugs policy, calling for regulated alternatives, voluntary treatment on demand, and better housing, health care and mental-health supports.
Key priorities: toxic drug crisis (regulated alternatives, voluntary treatment on demand); housing; health care and surgeries; mental-health supports; climate change
Quote: I want to do what I can to ensure my grandchildren grow up in a province that recognizes the health and well-being of people as our most critical priority.

Name: Richard Zussman
Bio:
Richard Zussman: Protecting the services that people rely on in Saanich South

Richard Zussman is an award-winning journalist who has spent his career covering every corner of this province, telling the stories of British Columbians and leading discussions on issues that matter most to people.

As a legislative reporter for Global BC and CBC, and President of the B.C. Legislative Press Gallery, he became a trusted voice during major events like the COVID-19 pandemic, wildfires, and provincial elections.

Deeply committed to his community, Richard serves on the boards of the Lakehill Baseball and Fastball Association and the Victoria Curling Club. He has also served as Lieutenant Governor of the B.C. Youth Parliament, promoting youth civic engagement. Richard, his wife, and their two children have proudly called the South Island home for more than a decade.

The BC Conservatives might want to cozy up to Trump, but Richard Zussman, David Eby and the BC NDP have a plan to stand up for BC, protect the services that people count on, and build a strong economy.

The plan is working. And we can’t stop now.
Pitch video title: Richard Zussman: BC Conservatives' "chaos" and shift in values were "hard to watch"
Pitch summary: Former Global BC/CBC legislative reporter running to replace retiring NDP MLA Lana Popham. He echoes the party's trade-war message and says he will advance the NDP plan to protect and create jobs, build homes, support farmers and recruit health-care workers.
Key priorities: protect and create good jobs amid U.S. trade war; build more homes; support farmers and agriculture; recruit more health-care workers; protect public services
Quote: The BC Conservatives might want to cozy up to Trump, but Richard Zussman, David Eby and the BC NDP have a plan to stand up for BC, protect the services that people count on, and build a strong economy.

Name: Denise Reimer
Bio:
Denise Reimer has spent more than 30 years serving British Columbians through emergency health services, local government and community leadership.

Her career with BC Emergency Health Services has included working as a Primary Care Paramedic, Emergency Medical Dispatcher and Critical Care Coordinator, as well as operational leadership roles. Her work in emergency services has given her firsthand experience of the importance of accessible healthcare, strong public services, teamwork and making thoughtful decisions when circumstances are changing quickly. In 2025, Denise was awarded the Governor General of Canada’s Emergency Medical Services Exemplary Service Medal.

Denise’s commitment to public service also includes elected municipal government. She served as a City Councillor for the City of Salmon Arm and as Deputy Mayor, with responsibilities involving planning, economic development and community engagement. She worked closely with residents, city staff, regional partners, community organizations and other levels of government.

Through her work with Implicit Career Services, Denise has also supported individuals and organizations through leadership development, career development, organizational change, conflict resolution and group facilitation. She brings a strong belief in listening, understanding different perspectives and finding practical ways forward.

Denise believes effective representation starts with being present and accessible. Her healthcare background has given her a particular appreciation for the importance of local access to healthcare, including the role of an urgent care centre within the electoral boundary. She believes an MLA should be visible in the community — boots on the ground, accessible to residents, listening to their concerns and bringing local perspectives to the Legislature and government.

With an Advanced Certificate in Local Government Leadership and decades of experience working with people, public services and community organizations, Denise brings a practical, collaborative approach to public service.
Pitch summary: Paramedic and BC Emergency Health Services veteran of 30+ years and former Salmon Arm councillor/deputy mayor. Her bio stresses local health-care access, including an urgent care centre in the riding, and an MLA who is visible and accessible in the community.
Key priorities: local health-care access (urgent care centre); accessible, present MLA; practical collaborative governance
Quote: She believes an MLA should be visible in the community — boots on the ground, accessible to residents, listening to their concerns and bringing local perspectives to the Legislature and government.
Quote source: https://www.centrebc.ca/our-team/ (bio text as captured in input CSV)

Name: David Williams
Bio:
Passion for the Community

David, a dedicated resident of the Shuswap region, is deeply committed to making the Shuswap-North Okanagan the ideal place for families to grow, retirees to relax, and businesses to thrive. His connection to the area drives his desire to represent its people and enhance their quality of life.

Professional Background

With a strong work ethic, David has a diverse and rich professional history. He began his career in the HVAC industry, taking on roles that ranged from commercial project management to small business ownership. His career path later shifted to the fields of residential and commercial real estate. David’s extensive experience and education led him to roles with the B.C. Assessment Authority and as a regional appraiser with the Saskatchewan Assessment Management Authority. Currently, he serves as a Loss Control Specialist/Residential Appraiser in the insurance industry, covering the Shuswap-Okanagan region, which gives him unique insights into the community’s needs.

Community Involvement and Leadership

Believing strongly in the power of volunteerism and sharing knowledge, David has been an active community advocate. He has coached minor soccer and baseball and has been involved in administrative roles with local sports associations. His dedication extends to serving as a board director for the Kelowna Metis Community Services Society, chairing the CSRD Board of Variance, and holding a government-appointed position on the Salmon Arm Property Assessment Review Panel.

Vision for the Future

With the support of his spouse, children, and grandchildren, David is focused on representing the wishes and interests of his constituents with integrity and commitment. He advocates for common-sense policies that resonate with the core values of British Columbians, including government transparency, fair taxation, reduced wasteful spending, easing burdens on businesses, and justice reform. David believes in the importance of action and foresight, striving for policies that promote a positive future for all.

Being your MLA is about more than just words; it’s about effective, thoughtful leadership that brings about tangible, positive changes for the residents of Salmon Arm-Shuswap.
Pitch summary: First-term Conservative MLA seeking re-election. He says land rights are top of mind and pledges the Conservatives will repeal DRIPA, alongside affordability, housing and hiring/training more doctors; his MLA priorities also include healthcare upgrades and protecting private land rights and public access.
Key priorities: repeal DRIPA / land-rights certainty; affordability for families and small businesses; build housing; hire and train more doctors, hospital upgrades; protect private land rights and public access; government transparency, fair taxation, less waste
Quote: Rest assured, we’re going to repeal DRIPA. The business community, the resource community, our economy, depends on having certainty when it comes to having land rights.

Name: Jed Wiebe
Bio:
Jed Wiebe is a lifelong Shuswap resident, organic farmer and community advocate with a strong focus on sustainable agriculture, local economic resilience and environmental stewardship.

Jed co-owns and operates Elderberry Grove, an organic elderberry farm and small-scale processing business in Salmon Arm. Through his work in agriculture, he has seen firsthand how extreme heat, wildfire smoke and changing environmental conditions affect farms, forests and rural communities.

With a background in sociology and anthropology, as well as experience in the silviculture industry, Jed brings a broad perspective on the social, economic and environmental challenges facing rural British Columbia.

Jed currently represents the agricultural community on the City of Salmon Arm’s Environmental Advisory Committee, where he contributes an agricultural perspective to local environmental and planning discussions.

His community and political involvement also includes helping establish the BC Greens’ Okanagan-Columbia-Shuswap Regional Riding Association, where he serves as Campaign Coordinator. He has also canvassed with Neighbours United in support of the proposed Biodiversity and Ecosystem Health Law and participated in the Vernon Climate Engagement Centre project.

Jed previously ran as the BC Greens candidate in Salmon Arm-Shuswap in the 2024 provincial election. He is running again to advocate for stronger local economies, affordable communities, responsible resource management and a government that listens to the people it serves.

He believes the BC Greens can build a British Columbia where people can afford housing, put food on the table and thrive in healthy communities while protecting the land and natural resources that sustain them.
Pitch summary: Organic elderberry farmer and lifelong Shuswap resident running a second time for the Greens. He says government should serve people rather than the ultra-wealthy and campaigns on local economies, affordability and responsible resource management.
Key priorities: stronger local economies; affordable communities (housing, food); responsible resource management; sustainable agriculture; climate impacts on farms and forests
Quote: I’m running because I believe government should serve people – not just the ultra-wealthy.

Name: Gloria Morgan
Pitch summary: No individual pitch found. Former Kukpi7 (chief) of Splatsin; ran federally for the Liberals in Similkameen-South Okanagan-West Kootenay in 2025 (2nd).

Name: Barbara Presch
Pitch summary: No individual pitch found. Described by local press as new to the local political scene.

Name: Claire Rattée
Bio:
Claire Rattée is a dedicated public servant with a remarkable 13-year track record as a successful business owner, embodying the values that resonate with British Columbians. Born and raised in Delta, B.C., Claire moved to Kitimat in 2011, establishing deep roots in the community and developing a profound understanding of the issues that matter most to its residents.

Professional Experience and Business Ownership

As a seasoned business owner, Claire has navigated the challenges of entrepreneurship, gaining valuable insights into the needs and concerns of local businesses. Her entrepreneurial journey has not only emphasized the importance of fiscal responsibility but has also provided her with ample opportunities for high levels of community engagement.

Public Service and City Council Experience

In addition to her private sector experience, Claire Rattée has devoted four years of service to the Kitimat City Council. In this role, she played a pivotal part in advocating for policies supporting economic growth, community development, healthcare services, and affordable housing. Claire’s focus during her time on City Council was to represent struggling business owners, provide younger voters with representation, and enhance the quality of life for Northern B.C. residents. Notably, Claire made history as the youngest female ever elected to a council position in Kitimat.

Political Engagement and Federal Elections

No stranger to the political arena, Claire transitioned from City Council to run in the 2019 and 2021 federal elections. Despite an unsuccessful bid, she garnered considerable momentum within the Conservative Party. Under her leadership, the Conservative vote share increased from 24% to 36%, highlighting her ability to resonate with voters and fortify support for conservative principles in challenging territories.

Passions and Advocacy

Claire Rattée’s passions lie in economic development, addressing the housing crisis, and advocating for healthcare and addiction recovery support for her region. Her commitment to these crucial issues stems from a genuine desire to improve the lives of Skeena residents. Notably, during her tenure on City Council, Claire played a pivotal role in collaborative efforts leading to a positive final investment decision for the LNG Canada project, the largest private sector investment in Canadian history. This accomplishment underscores her ability to work collaboratively to achieve meaningful and lasting outcomes.

Conservative Vision for Skeena

As an MLA, Claire Rattée seeks to represent Skeena with conviction, aiming to preserve the principles that make the region strong and vibrant. She pledges to be a tireless advocate for cherished values and a steadfast voice for the community. Claire is dedicated to bringing common-sense conservatism to Skeena, making her an ideal to serve as a representative in the Legislature with an unwavering commitment to shared values.
Pitch summary: First-term Skeena MLA (Conservative critic for mental health and addictions) seeking re-election after briefly being expelled from and then rejoining the Conservative caucus. She frames her campaign around well-paying jobs, affordable housing, reliable health care and a government that listens, and argues unclear rules and permitting delays are stalling investment in the Northwest.
Key priorities: well-paying jobs / resource investment (LNG, industry); affordable housing; reliable health care; mental health and addiction recovery; permitting certainty
Quote: I will run in the next election as a BC Conservative. Every action I have taken, and every action I take going forward, will be guided by one purpose: fighting for the people of Skeena and their right to a well-paying job, an affordable place to live, reliable health care and a government that listens to them.

Name: Nick Gottlieb
Bio:
Nick Gottlieb is a writer, researcher, community organizer, and PhD candidate at Simon Fraser University. His priorities for the change we need are shaped by his research into corporate power and his experience organizing in communities across British Columbia. He is running to advocate for greater investment in healthcare, housing, affordability, workers, and a liveable future, while challenging what he sees as excessive corporate influence over public policy.

For Nick, research and community organizing go hand in hand. While living in Squamish, he helped found the Squamish Resilience Network and co-led a campaign supporting the community’s “Just Recovery” initiative. Since moving to Terrace, where he has lived for the past five years, he has helped establish the Skeena Local Action Network and has been involved in campaigns focused on housing affordability, environmental protection, international solidarity, and proposed data centre development in the region.

His research focuses on the political economy of Canada’s liquefied natural gas (LNG) industry, including corporate influence on government, regional economic development, and the role of LNG in a changing global economy. In 2025, he was awarded a Vanier Canada Graduate Scholarship.

Nick’s writing and journalism have appeared in Canada’s National Observer, the Vancouver Sun, Business in Vancouver, and other publications, and he is a regular columnist with Canadian Dimension. He has also published reports based on his research and presented his work to universities, community groups, and grassroots organizers.

He has also contributed his technical expertise to environmental and community initiatives, including the UBC Big Tree Registry and forestry advocacy projects. He serves on the board of BC Whitewater, a non-profit organization advocating for public access to free-flowing rivers.

Outside of his research and organizing work, Nick is an outdoorsman and award-winning photographer who spends much of his free time exploring the mountains and rivers of British Columbia. He is running to bring his experience as a researcher, writer, and grassroots organizer to be a committed champion for the people of the Skeena region, who deserve to believe in better.
Pitch summary: Terrace-based writer, organizer and SFU PhD candidate researching the political economy of LNG. He is running to push for more investment in health care, housing, affordability and workers while challenging corporate influence over public policy.
Key priorities: health care; housing; affordability; workers; challenge corporate influence / budget cuts and deregulation; liveable future
Quote: I’ve lived in Terrace for the last 5 years, and people on the ground can see that we’re facing a five-alarm fire. But instead of responding to it, our politicians are doubling down on business as usual: budget cuts, deregulation, and selling off our industries to foreign investors at bargain-basement prices.

Name: Sarah Zimmerman
Bio:
Sarah Zimmerman: Standing firm for people and families in Skeena

Sarah Zimmerman is an elected Terrace City Councillor, former journalist, senior communications leader, and fierce advocate for people and communities in the Skeena region.

She has spent more than two decades bringing the Skeena region’s residents together to work collaboratively on the issues that matter to them. Outside her professional commitments, Sarah volunteers her time to numerous organizations, such as the Terrace Rotary Club and My Mountain Co-op.

She will bring a unique understanding of the Northwest to Victoria. You can count on her to fight to protect the services that matter to people in the Skeena region, and build for the future.

Where the BC Conservatives would cut the services you count on and surrender to Trump, Sarah Zimmerman, David Eby and the BC NDP have a plan to stand up for people in British Columbia, protect the services that people count on, and build a stronger economy.

The plan is working. And we can’t stop now.
Pitch summary: Terrace city councillor and former journalist/communications executive making a second run after losing to Rattée by 824 votes in 2024. She pitches collaboration and relationship-building to get projects done; the NDP release says her focus is protecting local jobs, lowering costs and strengthening health care.
Key priorities: protect local jobs; lower costs; strengthen health care; collaboration to get projects done
Quote: Good representation starts with building relationships across sectors to bring people together and get important projects done. I know firsthand the powerful impact of working together, and I will bring that strong, effective approach to Victoria to represent Skeena.

Name: Larry Eugene Taylor
Pitch summary: No individual pitch found.

Name: Raman Sharma
Bio:
Raman Sharma is a long-time Surrey resident, entrepreneur, and community leader with more than 28 years of experience in Canada. Since arriving in Canada in 1998, he has built strong relationships throughout Surrey and British Columbia through business, construction, community service, cultural organizations, and civic engagement.

In 2016, Raman founded the Tradesman Association of BC and continues to serve as its President. Through the organization, he has created educational and professional opportunities for builders and tradespeople, including builder licensing preparation, energy advisor education, safety training, professional development, and networking.

Raman also founded and leads the Annual Construction Expo, bringing together thousands of builders, tradespeople, businesses, and community members. He is the founder of the South Asian Construction Excellence (SACE) Awards, recognizing achievement, professionalism, and excellence within the construction industry.

Through his education and community initiatives, Raman has helped hundreds of aspiring and working construction professionals strengthen their qualifications, expand their knowledge, and advance their careers in British Columbia. His work has also created opportunities for small businesses, tradespeople, and community members to connect, learn, and grow.

Raman believes that public leadership is about listening to people, understanding community needs, bringing people together, and turning ideas into practical action.
Pitch summary: Surrey entrepreneur and founder/president of the Tradesman Association of BC and the Annual Construction Expo. His bio frames leadership as listening, bringing people together and turning ideas into practical action; no specific policy platform found.
Key priorities: construction/trades training and small business (from bio); practical, listening-based leadership
Quote: Raman believes that public leadership is about listening to people, understanding community needs, bringing people together, and turning ideas into practical action.
Quote source: https://www.centrebc.ca/our-team/ (bio text as captured in input CSV)

Name: Zeeshan Wahla
Bio:
Zeeshan Wahla is the Conservative Party of BC candidate for Surrey City Centre. 

Zeeshan is a Professional Engineer and small business owner who runs his own engineering consulting firm. Registered as a P.Eng. in four provinces, he brings extensive experience in engineering and planning, along with a professional commitment to honesty, integrity and protecting public safety and the environment.

Zeeshan arrived in British Columbia as an immigrant in 2007 and has proudly called Surrey home ever since. Raised in a family that valued hard work and perseverance, he pursued higher education and built a business of his own. That journey has given him a firsthand understanding of the pressures facing working families, from the rising cost of living to the challenge of getting ahead in today’s economy.

Zeeshan and his wife are raising their four daughters in Surrey, where they share their home with his mother. Providing his daughters with a good education and the opportunity for a bright future is at the heart of everything he does, and he wants every family in Surrey to have that same opportunity.
Pitch summary: Professional engineer and small-business owner in a rematch with Amna Shah, whom he lost to by under 100 votes in 2024. Indo-Canadian Voice reports he wants political bias and ideology removed from the school curriculum and prioritizes support for small and medium businesses; he has campaigned on rising property taxes and the cost of living.
Key priorities: cost of living / property-tax relief; remove ideology from school curriculum; support small and medium-sized businesses; education and opportunity for families
Quote: From 2023 to 2026, property taxes on this home jumped from $4,333 to $5,957. That’s a 37% increase in just three years. How are families supposed to keep up when everything else is going up too?

Name: Amna Shah
Bio:
Committed to Surrey City Centre.

Amna Shah has called Surrey home for nearly 20 years. Growing up, her family taught her about the importance of compassion, public service, and standing up for your community — values that guide her every day.

Like so many people in Surrey, Amna is concerned about housing. It’s what drove her to work with BC’s Ministry of Housing, where she helped move forward affordable housing policies and projects — many of which have become law and are in effect today.

Because she believes that no family should be left behind without enough to eat, she became a dedicated volunteer at the Surrey Food Bank, where she now serves on the Board of Directors. In this role, she’s helped expand distribution services across Surrey, helping to make sure that people and families using the food bank can get the nutritious food they need in a supportive, dignified environment.

Amna is focused on the issues that matter to people and families in Surrey, like expanded transit, strengthening education, building more healthcare facilities and keeping communities safe. Even better — she knows how to get things done.

You can count on her and David Eby to always have your best interests at heart.
Pitch summary: First-term MLA (former parliamentary secretary for anti-racism and for mental health and addictions) seeking re-election. She points to her affordable-housing policy work and Surrey Food Bank board role and warns against Conservative cuts; her candidate site lists transit, education, health-care facilities and community safety.
Key priorities: affordable housing; expanded transit; strengthening education; more health-care facilities; safe communities; food security
Quote: From my work on affordable housing to my time with the Surrey Food Bank, I’ve seen how important it is to make sure people have the support and opportunities they need to get ahead.

Name: Oliver Wildfong
Pitch summary: No individual pitch found.

Name: Bhandol Parm
Bio:
Bhandol Parm has been a resident of Surrey North for more than 10 years, and is proud to serve the community as a HandyDART operator.

Bhandol holds a BSc and MSc in Mathematics, bringing a practical, analytical, and evidence-based approach to the issues facing Surrey North.

Every day, Bhandol works alongside seniors, people with disabilities, families, and residents from all walks of life. Through local sports and community involvement, he also connects with young people and understands how important it is to give youth meaningful opportunities to learn, grow, and succeed.

Living and working in Surrey North for more than a decade has given Bhandol firsthand insight into the challenges Surrey North faces. He brings a genuine commitment to listening to people and finding practical solutions that work.

Bhandol’s priorities are clear: better public transit, stronger local infrastructure, more opportunities for youth, and accessible representation for everyone in Surrey North.

Bhandol’s goal is to be a strong voice for our community in Victoria—bringing the concerns, ideas, and priorities of Surrey North directly to the provincial government.
Pitch summary: HandyDART operator with BSc/MSc in mathematics and 10+ years in Surrey North. His stated priorities are better transit, stronger local infrastructure, youth opportunities and accessible representation.
Key priorities: better public transit; stronger local infrastructure; more opportunities for youth; accessible representation
Quote: Bhandol’s priorities are clear: better public transit, stronger local infrastructure, more opportunities for youth, and accessible representation for everyone in Surrey North.
Quote source: https://www.centrebc.ca/our-team/ (bio text as captured in input CSV)

Name: Mandeep Dhaliwal
Bio:
Mandeep Dhaliwal’s journey to becoming the Conservative Party of BC MLA for Surrey North is a testament to his diverse experiences and unwavering commitment to community service. Migrating to Canada in his 20s with his family, Mandeep embarked on a path that blends his love for social services, entrepreneurial spirit, and passion for public engagement.

Family and Background

Raised in Surrey, Mandeep is a devoted family man, nurturing his small family, which includes his wife Pawan, a dedicated Registered Nurse, and their son Diltaj. His roots in social service sprouted in India, where he completed his Bachelor of Arts degree in group humanity and excelled in the folk game of Punjab, Kabaddi (wrestling). As a national-level player, he secured a gold medal in an inter-college tournament, reflecting his dedication and prowess in sports.

Entrepreneurship in Canada

Transitioning to Canada, Mandeep became a small business owner, establishing Fixman Auto Glass Repair and Fixman Auto Glass Supplier in Surrey. Through hard work and determination, he transformed his ventures into trusted brands within the industry. As a successful entrepreneur, Mandeep is attuned to the challenges faced by small businesses and is committed to advocating for policies fostering growth and supporting startups.

Community Engagement

Beyond business, Mandeep is deeply immersed in his local community. Actively participating in various events and initiatives, he supports local charities and organizations, embodying his belief in giving back to the community that supported his business.

Sikh Motorcycle Club and Philanthropy

Mandeep’s commitment to social services continues through his membership in the BC Sikh Motorcycle Club, engaging in rides that contribute to the community. Notable among these is the 2016 motorcycle ride from BC to Ontario, where he played a pivotal role in raising $100,000 for the BC Cancer Society. Another remarkable feat is his participation in a fundraising bike ride from Canada to India, setting a world record and generating $100,000 for the Khalsa Aid organization.

Advocacy and Vision for BC

Throughout his life, Mandeep has displayed a passion for public service, social justice, equality, and sustainability. His vision for BC focuses on critical areas such as affordable housing, education, healthcare, and environmental sustainability. Mandeep believes that by investing in these areas, a stronger, more inclusive community can be forged.

Community-Centric Representation

As an MLA, Mandeep is dedicated to listening to the concerns and ideas of community members, ensuring their voices shape the decision-making process. With experience, passion, and dedication, he envisions progress, opportunity, and a better future for all residents. Mandeep Dhaliwal is poised to be a dynamic representative, committed to transparency, accountability, and integrity in his role as a public servant.
Pitch summary: First-term Conservative MLA seeking re-election. He has focused on extortion and threats against Surrey businesses and Sikh community leaders, accusing the NDP government of failing to provide protection; his party bio lists affordable housing, education, health care and small-business support.
Key priorities: public safety / extortion and violence in Surrey; affordable housing; education; health care; small-business support; parental rights (critic role)

Building a stronger Surrey.

Sahib Thind is the founder and president of the Professor Mohan Singh Memorial Foundation, which has advocated for recognition of the Komagata Maru tragedy and organizes the annual Mela Gadri Babiyan Da at Bear Creek Park. He is a fearless advocate for human and civil rights.

He received B.C.’s Medal of Good Citizenship in 2017. A Surrey North resident for more than 40 years, he is semi-retired and worked in the construction industry.

Bio:
Tanya Gupta is a business owner and Notary Public in British Columbia, bringing years of experience working directly with individuals, families, professionals, financial institutions, and businesses.

Since 2019, Tanya has owned and operated Tanya Gupta Notary Corporation, while also managing and operating SSTG Gas Station. Through her businesses, she has gained firsthand experience with the responsibilities and challenges of running a business, including managing employees, finances, customers, regulatory requirements, and day-to-day operations.

Tanya holds a Master of Applied Legal Studies from Simon Fraser University and a Bachelor of Computer Applications. Her professional and business experience has developed strong skills in leadership, communication, problem-solving, decision-making, organization, and working with people from diverse backgrounds.

Tanya is passionate about bringing her practical experience and community-focused perspective to public service. She believes that years of working directly with people, operating businesses, and serving clients have given her valuable insight into the responsibilities that come with serving the public.

Tanya Gupta is proud to be the OneBC candidate for Surrey North.

Name: Megan Knight
Bio:
Megan Knight has called the White Rock area home for more than 46 years. She graduated from Semiahmoo Secondary, went on to study at the University of British Columbia, and in 1998 was commissioned as a British Columbia Notary Public, establishing a practice she ran for 25 years, serving local families and businesses with integrity and dedication.

Megan’s commitment to her community led her into public service. She was first elected to White Rock City Council in 2014, serving as a Councillor until 2018, and was elected Mayor of White Rock in 2022. As Mayor, she has worked to keep White Rock safe, support local businesses, protect its natural spaces and ensure the city’s public spaces remain vibrant and welcoming for residents and visitors alike.

Her leadership extends well beyond city hall. Megan has served on the Metro Vancouver Board of Directors and the TransLink Mayors’ Council, giving her firsthand experience with the regional decisions that shape transportation, growth and costs for South Surrey and White Rock families. She has also served on the boards of the Sources Foundation, the Society of Notaries Public of BC, the Notary Foundation, the Fraser Valley Regional Library and Tour de White Rock. 

In 2022, Megan was honoured with the Queen Elizabeth II Platinum Jubilee Medallion in recognition of her contributions to community service.

As MLA for Surrey South, Megan will be a strong voice for safer communities and lower costs, and will deliver a provincial government that listens to the people it serves.
Pitch video title: White Rock Mayor Megan Knight Enters Surrey South Race
Pitch summary: White Rock mayor (since 2022), former councillor and 25-year notary public, withdrew from the civic race to run provincially. Her party bio says she will be a strong voice for safer communities and lower costs and a government that listens.
Key priorities: safer communities; lower costs; a government that listens; regional transportation/growth (Metro Vancouver, TransLink experience)
Quote: As MLA for Surrey South, Megan will be a strong voice for safer communities and lower costs, and will deliver a provincial government that listens to the people it serves.

Name: Nicholas Cartmell
Bio:
Nicholas Cartmell is the Conservative Party of BC candidate for Surrey-Cloverdale.

Nicholas is a brand strategist and community sport builder who has spent his career creating moments that matter to people. He and his wife, Leslie, have made Surrey home since 2012. They are raising a young son who plays competitive minor hockey, and two adult sons now building careers in engineering and the Canadian Armed Forces Reserves.

Community work has been the constant. As CEO of the BC Sports Hall of Fame and Museum, Nicholas led a non-profit accountable to a 23-member board and expanded a youth education program that reaches classrooms across British Columbia. He raised the funding for the Hall’s Indigenous Sport Gallery and led the effort to bring it online, so the stories of 40 First Nations and Métis athletes, coaches and builders could reach every corner of the province. He chaired business and community engagement for the 102nd Grey Cup Festival in Vancouver, and from 2016 to 2018 served on Capilano University’s Board of Governors, where he chaired the Investment Committee. Today he is Vice President of the Surrey 2027 55+ BC Games Host Society, preparing to welcome thousands of participants and visitors to Surrey next September.

Nicholas brings two decades of business leadership. Over 14 years at TELUS, most recently as Senior Director, Strategic Initiatives, Partnerships and Government Relations, he led national teams and budgets and negotiated $51 million in partnerships and investments. He went on to run the Western Canadian division of Canada’s largest event rental company, employing more than 100 British Columbians through peak seasons.
Pitch summary: Brand strategist, former BC Sports Hall of Fame CEO and ex-TELUS senior director, Surrey resident since 2012. His party bio highlights business leadership and community sport; no riding-specific policy pitch found beyond the party's Surrey slate message on affordability, safety and health care.

Name: Pat McCutcheon
Bio:
Pat McCutcheon is a retired professional engineer, small-business owner and longtime Cloverdale resident who raised his two sons in the community with his wife. He has seen firsthand how pressures on healthcare, public education, housing affordability and the environment affect local families.

Pat graduated from the University of British Columbia with a Bachelor of Applied Science and went on to build a long career in engineering. In 1995, he founded his own engineering consulting firm, providing services to heavy equipment manufacturers across the Lower Mainland. He operated the business for 28 years.

His professional background has given him experience in problem-solving, long-term planning and working with businesses across the region. Pat is also an active member of the Cloverdale District Chamber of Commerce.

He joined the BC Greens in 2019, motivated by a belief in evidence-based policy and the need for environmental, economic, social and fiscal sustainability.

Pat is running in Surrey-Cloverdale to advocate for stronger public services, more affordable housing, climate action and a more proactive approach to the challenges facing the community.
Pitch summary: Retired professional engineer and 28-year engineering-firm owner, long-time Cloverdale resident. He is running to advocate for stronger public services, more affordable housing, climate action and a more proactive approach to local challenges.
Key priorities: stronger public services (health care, education); affordable housing; climate action; evidence-based, fiscally sustainable policy
Quote: Pat is running in Surrey-Cloverdale to advocate for stronger public services, more affordable housing, climate action and a more proactive approach to the challenges facing the community.

Name: Stephen Dooley
Bio:
Building a stronger Surrey-Cloverdale

Stephen Dooley is the BC NDP Candidate in Surrey Cloverdale. He is the recently retired Executive Director of the Surrey Simon Fraser University campus, and the former Director and Chair of the Surrey Board of Trade, as well as the Co-Chair of the Surrey Poverty Reduction Coalition. He also served as the co-chair of the Surrey Social Innovation Summit. In his various roles, Stephen has worked extensively with First Nations communities south of the Fraser River.

Prior to joining SFU Stephen taught criminology and sociology at Kwantlen Polytechnic University and he was the first Director of Community Engagement. He is known for his ability to build trust, bring diverse interests together, and turn shared priorities into action. He has extensive experience in public accountability, strategic planning, financial stewardship, and a longstanding commitment to accessible education, poverty reduction, youth opportunity, public safety, economic development, reconciliation, and community well-being.

Steve holds a Master’s degree in Sociology and a Bachelor’s degree in Sociology and History. He and his wife Preet have lived in the region for over 25 years. Their son Dave, daughter-in-law Jasmine and grandson Wilson are proud residents of Surrey Cloverdale.

Stephen Dooley, David Eby and the BC NDP have a plan to build BC strong: to create jobs, to strengthen healthcare, and to bring down the cost of living.
Pitch summary: Recently retired executive director of SFU's Surrey campus, former Surrey Board of Trade chair and co-chair of the Surrey Poverty Reduction Coalition. His candidate page emphasizes education, poverty reduction, youth opportunity, public safety and reconciliation, plus the NDP jobs/health/cost-of-living message.
Key priorities: create jobs; strengthen health care; bring down cost of living; accessible education; poverty reduction; youth opportunity; public safety; reconciliation
Quote: Stephen Dooley, David Eby and the BC NDP have a plan to build BC strong: to create jobs, to strengthen healthcare, and to bring down the cost of living.

Name: Garry Purewal
Bio:
Garry Purewal is the Conservative Party of BC candidate for Surrey-Fleetwood.

Garry’s commitment to service began in uniform. As a Military Police member with the Canadian Armed Forces, he learned the discipline, integrity and sense of duty that have guided him ever since. That experience gave him a firsthand understanding of public safety and of what it takes to keep communities secure.x

After his military service, Garry built a career in business, owning and managing companies including a property restoration business. Running his own business has taught him what every small business owner in British Columbia knows: how hard it is to meet a payroll, keep costs down and grow when government makes it more expensive to do business every year.

Garry has also given his time to the next generation as a leader in youth sports, and has been active in community advocacy and political engagement, working with neighbours and local organizations on the issues that matter most to families.

That experience has given Garry a clear view of the challenges facing families, business owners and communities, and a strong commitment to public safety, responsible government, economic opportunity and effective public policy.
Pitch summary: Former Canadian Armed Forces military police member and small-business owner (property restoration). His party bio stresses public safety, responsible government, economic opportunity and the cost of doing business.

Quote: Running his own business has taught him what every small business owner in British Columbia knows: how hard it is to meet a payroll, keep costs down and grow when government makes it more expensive to do business every year.

Jagrup Brar has represented people in Surrey for decades. As the past Executive Director of the Surrey Self Employment and Entrepreneur Development Society (SEEDS), Jagrup trained new entrepreneurs to develop and launch successful small businesses — strengthening the community in which he, his wife and his two children live.

Jagrup is committed to building up Surrey, whether that’s a new hospital, or a SkyTrain extension, or a stronger economy with good-paying jobs, or homes - all the things people need to build a good life in the place they love.

The conservative parties would cozy up to Trump, cut healthcare, and hike costs on working people.

Jagrup Brar, David Eby and the BC NDP have a plan to lower costs, hire more healthcare workers, and build a stronger economy.

The plan is working. And we can’t stop now.

Name: Carolyn Hofbauer
Bio:
Carolyn Hofbauer grew up in Surrey’s Newton neighbourhood and attended Frank Hurt Secondary School. Surrey is where she went to school, built her career, and is raising her family.

Carolyn began working at 15 while continuing her education. After high school, she attended what is now Kwantlen Polytechnic University, where she studied music, English, and history. During her college years, she also worked as a substitute teacher.

Much of Carolyn’s early career was spent in the restaurant industry. She worked as a chef at Fresgo Inn before becoming head chef at The Vault Restaurant in Cloverdale, where she spent nearly a decade. The work demanded responsibility, teamwork, and the ability to listen to people.

Carolyn later joined her family business. Today, she manages BC Firearms Academy alongside her husband. Running a small business has given her firsthand experience with the challenges facing employers, employees, and families in British Columbia.

Carolyn and her husband are raising their son, Blake. Family is at the centre of her life and shapes how she thinks about the future of her community.

Carolyn’s involvement in politics began during college. Since then, she has volunteered on campaigns, knocked on doors, made calls, worked in campaign offices, and spoken with voters about the issues that matter to them.

Carolyn is running for OneBC to bring her experience as a mother, small business owner, and lifelong Surrey resident to provincial politics. She wants to represent the community she has always called home.
Pitch summary: Lifelong Surrey resident, former head chef and now manager of the family business BC Firearms Academy. Her bio says she is running to bring her experience as a mother, small-business owner and lifelong Surrey resident to provincial politics.
Key priorities: small business; family; representing her home community (bio only)
Quote: Carolyn is running for OneBC to bring her experience as a mother, small business owner, and lifelong Surrey resident to provincial politics.

Name: Garry Thind
Bio:
Garry Thind is the Conservative Party of BC candidate for Surrey-Guilford.

Garry has proudly called Surrey home for more than 27 years, living, working, raising his family and serving his community in the city. For the past 12 years, he has served Surrey families as a Trustee on the Surrey School Board, where he is currently Vice-Chair, representing the interests of parents, students and the broader community.

Since 2014, Garry has taken on leadership roles across the school district, chairing committees including the Learning Liaison Committee, Traditional Schools, District Principal Selection, Secondary Vice-Principal Selection, the ELL Consortium and the Budget Committee. That work has given him extensive experience in governance, policy development and accountability, and in working collaboratively with parents, educators and community stakeholders. He also sits on the External Advisory Board of Western Community College in Surrey.

Garry’s commitment to Surrey extends well beyond the School Board. He is a past President of the Rotary Club of Surrey and currently leads the BC region for the Pingalwara Society of Ontario, a charitable organization. Since 2002, he has helped raise more than $5.4 million for charitable and community causes.

Professionally, Garry brings more than 14 years of management experience and more than 13 years in sales and marketing. He is currently a full-time Realtor with Century 21 Coastal Realty in Surrey, work that has sharpened his skills in leadership, communication and relationship-building.
Pitch summary: Surrey school board vice-chair (12 years as trustee), realtor and charity fundraiser, challenging Garry Begg in a riding decided by 22 votes in 2024. He says education remains a priority but he will also tackle issues he says the NDP neglected: illicit drugs and overdoses, extortion, housing and affordability, and argues new taxes won't fix the economy.
Key priorities: education; illicit drugs and overdoses; extortion threats; housing and affordability; economy (no new taxes, grow provincial revenue)
Quote: I think we need to fix those policies. Just applying new taxes won’t solve any problem. We need to find out ways where the British Columbia government can generate more income.

Name: Garry Begg
Bio:
On your side in Surrey-Guildford.

Garry Begg knows the importance of giving families, kids, and schools the tools they need to succeed — now and later in life. Prior to being elected as the MLA for Surrey-Guildford in 2017, 2020 and 2024, he served in progressive law enforcement leadership with the RCMP for nearly 40 years where he gained a deep understanding of issues facing people living in Surrey.

Garry knows that Surrey is the fastest growing — and soon to be largest — city in BC, which comes with its own set of challenges for people who live here. It’s why he’s focused on ensuring the people of Surrey have the housing, education and health care support they need to build a good life here.

You can count on Garry Begg, David Eby and the BC NDP to look out for you and your family.
Pitch summary: Three-term MLA and former RCMP officer of nearly 40 years seeking re-election after winning by 22 votes in 2024. He says the NDP has a real plan on crime, health care and South of the Fraser transportation; his candidate page focuses on housing, education and health care for fast-growing Surrey.
Key priorities: tackle crime; improve health care; transportation for Surrey/South of the Fraser; housing; education
Quote: Garry knows that Surrey is the fastest growing — and soon to be largest — city in BC, which comes with its own set of challenges for people who live here. It’s why he’s focused on ensuring the people of Surrey have the housing, education and health care support they need to build a good life here.

Name: Harman Preet Singh
Bio:
Harman Preet Singh is a legal professional with experience in criminal defence, immigration, administrative law, public policy, governance, technology, and business. He brings a unique combination of legal expertise, governance experience, and an understanding of innovation and economic opportunity.

Harman previously served as a Student Member of the Kwantlen Polytechnic University Board of Governors, representing more than 22,000 students. In this role, he gained valuable experience in institutional governance, strategic decision-making, accountability, and advocating for the interests of a diverse community.

He is currently completing his legal articling in British Columbia and holds a J.D./BBA LL.B. His education also includes public policy studies at the London School of Economics and Political Science, entrepreneurship studies at Babson College, and an advanced diploma in computer programming. This interdisciplinary background gives him a broad perspective on law, public policy, technology, and economic development.

Harman is committed to helping build safer, healthier, and more resilient communities across British Columbia. His priorities include safer neighbourhoods, stronger responses to homelessness, addiction, and mental-health challenges, improved access to justice, greater opportunities in education and skills development, and public institutions that are accessible, transparent, and accountable.

Outside of his professional life, Harman values family, fitness, and lifelong learning. He enjoys yoga and working out and especially cherishes time with his six-year-old niece and four-year-old nephew. They keep him grounded and remind him of the importance of building a better future for the next generation.

Harman speaks English, Punjabi, and Hindi, allowing him to connect with and listen to people from diverse backgrounds across Surrey-Newton. His experience in law, public policy, technology, business, and governance gives him a broad and practical perspective on the challenges facing our community.

He is committed to bringing that experience into public service – by carefully listening to residents, understanding the issues that matter most to families and businesses, and working toward practical solutions for a stronger, safer, and more prosperous Surrey-Newton and British Columbia.
Pitch summary: Articling legal professional and former KPU Board of Governors student member. His bio lists safer neighbourhoods, stronger responses to homelessness, addiction and mental health, access to justice, education and skills, and accountable public institutions.

Name: Harj Dhaliwal
Bio:
Dr. Harj Dhaliwal is the Conservative Party of BC candidate for Surrey-Newton.

He is a business executive, educator and community leader with extensive experience in organizational leadership, governance, public transportation and community development. Over the course of his career, he has held senior executive and leadership roles in both the private and post-secondary sectors. In business, he has led complex organizations and major construction development initiatives, working with diverse teams and stakeholders across British Columbia.

Dr. Dhaliwal holds an MBA and a PhD in Organization Development and Leadership. He has taught business and management courses at the undergraduate and graduate levels. He brings significant public-sector governance experience, having served six years as a Director of TransLink and four years on the board of the BC SPCA.

Dr. Dhaliwal has been a longtime leader in youth soccer in Newton and across the region. He has served as Chair of the South Fraser District Association, Chair of the Surrey Metro Soccer Association, Board Member of the BC Coastal Soccer League, and President of the Central City Breakers Football Club in Newton.

He has lived in Surrey for 28 years, where he and his wife raised their family, and has been an active community leader throughout that time.
Pitch summary: Business executive and educator (MBA, PhD), former TransLink director and BC SPCA board member, long-time Newton youth-soccer leader. No candidate-specific pitch found beyond his bio and the party's Surrey slate message on affordability, safety (including extortion) and health care.
