Key priorities: affordability; attainable homeownership; responsible development; health care / family doctors; education; addiction and homelessness solutions; balanced evidence-based governance
Quote: Political ideology is not a solution to our problems.
Quote source: https://www.centrebc.ca/our-team/ (bio text as captured in input CSV)

Name: Lisa Phillips
Bio:
Lisa is a finance professional and business owner with an academic background in mathematics and finance. She brings a practical, analytical approach to how government spends taxpayers’ money and a firm belief that every dollar should be accounted for.

Over eight years of board governance experience, Lisa has developed a strong understanding of oversight, accountability and sound decision-making. Alongside her professional work, she has spent years volunteering in her community, working with the neighbours and organizations that make Vancouver a great place to live.

Lisa believes in financial transparency, accountability, responsible development, safe streets and strong communities, and she is ready to bring those priorities to work for the people of Vancouver-South Granville.
Pitch summary: Finance professional and business owner with board governance experience. Her bio says she believes every taxpayer dollar should be accounted for and lists financial transparency, accountability, responsible development and safe streets.
Key priorities: financial transparency; accountability for spending; responsible development; safe streets; strong communities
Quote: Lisa believes in financial transparency, accountability, responsible development, safe streets and strong communities, and she is ready to bring those priorities to work for the people of Vancouver-South Granville.

Name: Maria J. Cruz
Bio:
Maria J. Cruz (she/her) is an artist, educator, public servant, community advocate and longtime renter in Vancouver-South Granville. She grew up in Mount Pleasant and has spent the past 15 years living in South Granville, where she has seen firsthand how rising costs and housing pressures are affecting the people who make the community work.

Maria believes that people who build their lives here deserve security, dignity and access to the services they need. Her priorities include stronger renter protections, more social housing, accessible healthcare and building a climate-resilient future.

Maria currently works as an Outreach Worker in the Vancouver School Board’s Adult Education program, helping newcomers and lifelong learners build skills, confidence and pathways to new opportunities. Supporting immigrants and refugees as they find belonging through education is an important part of her community work.

She has also built a career protecting and promoting arts, culture and heritage. Maria holds a Bachelor’s degree in Theatre and Art History from the University of British Columbia and a Master of Museum Studies from the University of Toronto. As a culture and heritage planner, she has written arts policy for communities across British Columbia and, as a collections care consultant, has helped manage both public and private collections.

A member of UBCP/ACTRA for nearly 30 years, Maria has worked as an actor, writer, producer and director in film, television and theatre. She has also performed her one-woman show at the Azores International Fringe Festival.

Healthcare is also deeply personal to Maria. As a breast cancer survivor, she understands the importance of timely, reliable care and believes healthcare workers should be able to afford to live in the communities that depend on them.

Maria is running with the BC Greens to make sure Vancouver-South Granville residents are heard and that the community’s future is shaped around the people who live and work there. She wants to strengthen public services, protect renters, expand social housing and help build a greener, more resilient community for everyone.
Pitch summary: Artist, VSB adult-ed outreach worker, heritage planner and longtime renter in South Granville. Her stated priorities are stronger renter protections, more social housing, accessible health care and a climate-resilient future.
Key priorities: renter protections; social housing; accessible health care; climate resilience; arts and culture
Quote: Her priorities include stronger renter protections, more social housing, accessible healthcare and building a climate-resilient future.
Quote source: Input CSV bio (BC Greens profile text)

Name: Lara Honrado
Bio:
Lara Honrado: Building a stronger Vancouver-South Granville

Lara Honrado is focused on the issues that matter most to the people of Vancouver-South Granville - affordability, protecting services, like healthcare, that matter to people, building a strong and resilient economy.

She led community relations for Vancouver’s former mayor, where she supported a range of issues including economic development, reconciliation, and climate change while strengthening relationships with diverse local communities. As a senior leader, she was instrumental in developing the City of Vancouver’s 2020-2029 cultural plan and guiding efforts to address equity in urban planning and pandemic emergency response.

Lara works with the United Nations and the world’s leading experts on AI to help the public understand the impacts of technology on society. She is proud to be part of the BC NDP team holding big tech companies accountable for online harms.

Deeply committed to supporting arts and culture, Lara serves on the board of 221A where she helps steward BC’s first cultural land trust.

Lara is a longtime Vancouver resident and a proud parent to two children.

Lara Honrado, David Eby and the BC NDP are building a stronger province.
Pitch summary: Former community relations lead for Vancouver's ex-mayor who now works with the UN on AI impacts. Her page says she is focused on affordability, protecting services like health care and building a resilient economy, and on holding big tech accountable for online harms.
Key priorities: affordability; protect health care and services; resilient economy; big tech accountability / online harms; arts and culture
Quote: Lara Honrado is focused on the issues that matter most to the people of Vancouver-South Granville - affordability, protecting services, like healthcare, that matter to people, building a strong and resilient economy.

Name: Salvatore Vetro
Bio:
Salvatore is not a career politician. He is a neighbour who has spent decades serving this community.

For 25 years he drove a HandyDART van so people with disabilities could get to appointments, work, and family. He helped found the Kitsilano Showers Program, giving homeless neighbours a hot shower, breakfast, clean clothes, and dignity every Saturday for more than 20 years.

In 2011 he helped lead the Fight HST campaign—the first time British Columbians used a citizen vote to repeal a law and put money back in families’ pockets. He also spent 20 years building a small business that supported local artists and shops.

Now Salvatore is running with OneBC in Vancouver–South Granville to be the people’s voice: lower costs, real help for those who need it, and prosperity for all—not just those already in power.
Pitch summary: Former HandyDART driver, Kitsilano Showers Program co-founder and 2011 Fight HST campaigner. He pitches himself as a non-politician neighbour running for lower costs, real help for those in need and prosperity for all.
Key priorities: lower costs; help for those in need; prosperity for all
Quote: Now Salvatore is running with OneBC in Vancouver–South Granville to be the people’s voice: lower costs, real help for those who need it, and prosperity for all—not just those already in power.

Name: Robert Crooks
Pitch summary: No individual pitch found.

Name: Jordan McIntosh
Bio:
Jordan McIntosh is the Conservative Party of BC candidate for Vancouver-Strathcona.

Jordan was born in Vancouver and has called British Columbia home for his entire life. As a mineral exploration field worker who works in all parts of BC, Jordan knows the importance of the mining sector to the province and is dedicated to seeing British Columbia reach its full potential as a natural resource powerhouse. He is a student achieving a bachelor’s degree in Geological Engineering.

Jordan is ready to help and take the next step as an MLA to help his province accelerate economically without leaving its citizens behind.
Pitch summary: Mineral exploration field worker and geological engineering student. His bio says he wants BC to reach its potential as a natural-resource powerhouse and accelerate economically without leaving citizens behind.
Key priorities: mining and natural resources; economic growth
Quote: Jordan is ready to help and take the next step as an MLA to help his province accelerate economically without leaving its citizens behind.

Name: Tanya Webking
Bio:
Tanya Webking is Dene and German, with roots in the Tłı̨chǫ Nation in the Northwest Territories. She has spent decades working on the frontlines of housing, healthcare and community support systems in Vancouver’s Downtown Eastside.

Through that work, Tanya has seen firsthand how housing instability, stretched public services and rising costs affect workers, families and vulnerable community members. She is running to bring that frontline experience into provincial decision-making and to help build systems that respond not only to crisis, but to the conditions that create it.

Tanya believes workers are essential to keeping communities and public services functioning and that fair wages, stable housing and strong public services are key to building long-term economic security.

She also believes governments need to work more effectively across jurisdictions and political lines to address complex challenges such as housing, healthcare and affordability.

Tanya is running in Vancouver-Strathcona to bring practical experience, collaboration and a strong commitment to equity into the Legislature and to advocate for systems that work better for the people who rely on them.
Pitch summary: Dene/German frontline worker with decades in housing, health care and community support in the Downtown Eastside. She is running to bring frontline experience into decision-making, backing fair wages, stable housing and strong public services and cross-party collaboration.
Key priorities: stable housing; strong public services; fair wages for workers; health care; equity; collaboration across jurisdictions
Quote: I’m ready to fight for the changes we need to build an equitable system for all.

Name: Amanda Burrows
Bio:
Amanda Burrows: protecting the services that people count on in Vancouver-Strathcona

Amanda is a community builder who believes in the power of people to create change. As Executive Director of First United in Vancouver’s Downtown Eastside, she led a $94m redevelopment delivering Indigenous supportive housing and space for frontline services.

For decades, Amanda has worked alongside communities advancing human rights and climate justice, fighting for renters, and working on the frontlines of the homelessness and overdose crises. A trusted voice in faith and civic circles, she ran for Mayor of Vancouver on affordability, safety rooted in care, and a city where everyone belongs. She holds a master’s in museum studies from the University of Toronto and completed leadership training at the Harvard Kennedy School and London School of Economics.

Amanda is a renter in Chinatown in Vancouver-Strathcona, on the unceded territories of the Musqueam, Squamish and Tsleil-Waututh. She believes change starts with listening to and learning from the people most affected.

Amanda Burrows, David Eby and the BC NDP have a plan to stand up for our province, protect people and the things they count on, and build a stronger economy.

“Amanda is a champion for social, economic and environmental justice, a strong voice for reconciliation and for Vancouver-Strathcona neighbourhood people’s interests.

Joan loved Amanda. And I know how much Amanda loved Joan, respected her leadership and valued the work they did alongside one another. Joan fought fiercely for the people of Vancouver-Strathcona, and Amanda understands the critical need to continue to carry that work forward.

I am honoured to stand in support of Amanda Burrows. I know in my heart Joan would have wanted that.”

Grand Chief Stewart Phillip
Pitch summary: Executive director of First United in the Downtown Eastside and former Vancouver mayoral hopeful, endorsed by Grand Chief Stewart Phillip to succeed the late MLA Joan Phillip. She says she will carry on Phillip's work and credits NDP housing action with costs starting to come down, pledging to protect services.
Key priorities: affordable housing and renter protections; homelessness and overdose crisis; living wage; reconciliation; climate justice; protect services (party message)
Quote: Vancouver-Strathcona is my home, and for more than a decade I’ve worked alongside renters, workers, families and people living in poverty across this community,

Name: Dion Weisner
Bio:
Dion Weisner is the Conservative Party of BC Candidate for Vancouver-West End.

Dion has built a career in public policy and research and is currently a senior staffer in the Office of the Leader of the Official Opposition. He knows the challenges facing British Columbians, particularly when it comes to healthcare. After suffering a serious injury, Dion experienced first hand how difficult it is to navigate the urgent and primary care systems. He is passionate about fixing British Columbia’s healthcare system.

Prior to joining government, Dion worked for Harbour Air in Sales and Marketing and was an instrumental member of the game operations team for the University of Victoria Basketball team and the Victoria HarbourCats. Dion has been with his husband Robert for the past 14 years.
Pitch summary: Senior staffer in the Official Opposition leader's office who says a serious injury showed him how hard it is to get urgent and primary care. Responding to NDP attacks over Heather Maahs, he said the NDP has failed on cost of living, family doctors and West End crime and disorder, and that as a gay man his community cares about jobs, housing, doctors and safe streets.
Key priorities: fix health care / family doctors; cost of living; crime and disorder in the West End; housing affordability; good jobs; age-appropriate curriculum with anti-bullying
Quote: After nine years of NDP government, life in British Columbia costs more, the family doctor every British Columbian was promised by the end of 2025 never showed up, and West End streets have more crime and disorder every year.

Name: Donald Scott MacDonald
Bio:
Donald Scott MacDonald is a recently retired physician and longtime downtown Vancouver resident running to represent Vancouver-West End. After more than three decades in medicine, including the last twenty years practising in downtown Vancouver, Donald is bringing his experience in healthcare, addictions medicine, and patient advocacy to public service.

Donald’s medical career has taken him across Canada, from northern Manitoba and Nunavut to Toronto and Vancouver. His work has included primary care, emergency and hospital medicine, HIV/AIDS care, Hepatitis C treatment, addictions medicine, and methadone maintenance. From 2004 until his retirement in 2026, he worked as a primary care physician in Vancouver with a particular focus on addictions.

Earlier in his career, Donald served as Medical Director of Casey House Hospice in Toronto, worked with the HIV programs at St. Paul’s Hospital and the Wellesley Hospital, provided primary care in isolated northern communities, and served as a physician with the Canadian military in Halifax.

Throughout his career, Donald has advocated for patient-centred care, disability justice, and stronger supports for people affected by substance use. His professional experience has given him a firsthand understanding of the importance of accessible healthcare, safe communities, and public systems that meet people where they are.

Growing up in Nova Scotia, Donald witnessed the environmental damage caused by acid rain, an experience that helped shape his commitment to protecting the natural world. Today, he believes British Columbia has the tools to build a cleaner, safer, more inclusive, and more prosperous future.

Donald holds an Honours Bachelor of Science in Biochemistry from Mount Allison University and a medical degree from Dalhousie University. He also completed a rotating internship at the University of Ottawa. In 2025, he ran federally in Vancouver Centre for the Green Party of Canada.

Donald is running to represent Vancouver-West End with a focus on accessible healthcare, safe neighbourhoods, a strong economy, and a sustainable future for the next generation.
Pitch summary: Recently retired downtown physician with an addictions-medicine and HIV-care background; ran federally for the Greens in Vancouver Centre in 2025. He is running with a focus on accessible health care, safe neighbourhoods, a strong economy and a sustainable future.
Key priorities: accessible health care; addictions and substance-use supports; safe neighbourhoods; strong economy; sustainability / environment; disability justice
Quote: The tools exist to make British Columbia a cleaner, safer, and more inclusive province.

Name: Spencer Chandra Herbert
Bio:
A fearless voice for Vancouver-West End

Spencer Chandra Herbert has proudly represented Vancouver's West End since 2008, having been re-elected six times to the BC Legislature.

As an MLA, Spencer has stood up for renters facing illegal evictions, worked to reduce homelessness by founding Vancouver’s Rent Bank and led the successful fight to explicitly protect transgender people in BC’s Human Rights Code.

Most recently, Spencer served as Minister of Indigenous Relations and Reconciliation, working in partnership with First Nations to advance modern treaties that build a stronger BC for everyone. He has previously served as Minister of Tourism, Arts, Culture and Sport and as Deputy Speaker.

Before provincial politics, Spencer was an award-winning artist and an elected Vancouver Park Board Commissioner.

You can count on Spencer to stand up for renters, to support our seniors, to improve access to healthcare, to protect our environment, and to build strong, safe, inclusive communities.

Spencer Chandra Herbert, David Eby and the BC NDP team work hard every day to make your life more affordable, protect the services you count on and build a sustainable economy that works for everyone. You can trust that they’re on your side.
Pitch summary: West End MLA since 2008 and most recently Minister of Indigenous Relations and Reconciliation. His page pitches standing up for renters, seniors, health-care access, the environment and inclusive communities; during the campaign he led the NDP call for Doerkson to fire Conservative candidate Heather Maahs over remarks about gay people.
Key priorities: renters' rights; seniors; health-care access; environment; safe inclusive communities / LGBTQ+ rights; reconciliation and modern treaties
Quote: Conflating the gay community with pedophilia is deeply homophobic, and there should be no place for this kind of hate in a party that hopes to lead this province.

Name: Sam Chandola
Bio:
Sam Chandola is the CentreBC candidate for Vancouver-Yaletown.

Sam’s story is a Canadian one. He arrived in 2012 as a scholarship student with an idea, a lot of grit, and not much else. Over a 15-year career in Vancouver, Sam founded several technology companies, generated $100M+ in export revenue for BC, sold 3 companies, and created hundreds of green, well-paying tech jobs here in BC.

Sam’s mobile apps have been downloaded more than 30 million times, and his software is used by governments and businesses. In 2020, he founded First Fund as his way to pay forward the opportunity Canada gave him. First Fund has gone on to become Canada’s largest pre-seed fund, having invested over $35 million in BC startups and backed more than 80 first-time founders. His goal is simple: keep BC’s best talent building here, instead of watching it leave for the United States.

His work has earned him BC Business’s Top 30 Under 30, the TMX Canada’s Next 150 Award, and a place on the Vancouver Economic Commission’s list of the Top 24 People of Asian Descent to Watch. Sam holds a Bachelor’s degree in Philology from Germany on an Erasmus Mundus scholarship and speaks English, Hindi, and German.

Yaletown has been Sam’s home base for more than a decade. It’s where he has built his companies, and where he lives. Sam is running to help bring his experience to build a BC economy that is less dependent on the public sector, less dependent on the United States, and fosters private sector jobs.

Sam is socially liberal and fiscally responsible. He believes a strong economy and a fair society go hand in hand, that diversity is one of Canada’s greatest opportunities, and that governments should be judged by results, not ideology. Like many Yaletown voters, he has watched provincial politics force a choice between an NDP government that has let healthcare, housing and public safety slip, and a Conservative party consumed by culture wars and infighting. Sam is running with CentreBC to give those voters a home: a socially liberal, pro-growth, and fiscally responsible choice, focused on getting things done for Yaletown and for British Columbia.
Pitch summary: Tech founder and First Fund pre-seed investor in Yaletown. His bio pitches a socially liberal, pro-growth, fiscally responsible choice for an economy less dependent on the public sector and the U.S., criticizing both NDP results and Conservative culture wars.
Key priorities: private-sector job growth; less dependence on U.S.; keep tech talent in BC; fiscal responsibility; health care, housing and public safety
Quote: His goal is simple: keep BC’s best talent building here, instead of watching it leave for the United States.
Quote source: https://www.centrebc.ca/our-team/ (bio text as captured in input CSV)

Name: Margareta Dovgal
Bio:
Margareta Dovgal is the Conservative Party of BC candidate for Vancouver-Yaletown. She is a national economic commentator and policy analyst. She grew up below the poverty line, and built a professional career in economic development advocacy, after facing the loss of both parents in her teens.

Margareta was born and lives in Downtown Vancouver. She wants all families in Yaletown to be able to afford a home, have a government that respects every dollar they earn, and be safe in our community, rather than having to worry about needles in playgrounds or in dog parks. 

She has been an advocate for a strong economy through national columns and regular broadcast commentary. Through her expert testimony before parliamentary committees, she has been a committed voice for BC in Ottawa. She knows how to challenge the NDP’s economic mismanagement and restore accountability for public services. 

Margareta’s community work includes mental-health advocacy with the BC Schizophrenia Society and service through the Rotary Club of Vancouver Waterfront. She believes that public safety is the top priority for government, but the BC NDP has failed. She also co-founded and ran the Indigenous Partnerships Success Showcase, bringing people together to advance economic reconciliation through investment and shared prosperity. She is multilingual and has a Bachelor of Arts in Asian Area Studies from UBC and a Master of Public Administration from University College London.
Pitch summary: National economic commentator and policy analyst who grew up below the poverty line in downtown Vancouver. Her bio says she wants Yaletown families to afford a home, have a government that respects every dollar and be safe, calling public safety the government's top priority.
Key priorities: housing affordability; respect for taxpayers' money; public safety (needles in playgrounds); economic accountability; economic reconciliation
Quote: She believes that public safety is the top priority for government, but the BC NDP has failed.

Name: Priyan Samarakoone
Pitch summary: No individual pitch found.

Name: Terry Yung
Bio:
Terry Yung: Standing up for Vancouver-Yaletown

Terry Yung is a veteran of the Vancouver Police Department (VPD) and a community leader. As a police officer, he protected people, whether it was walking the beat in the Downtown Eastside, working as a Financial Crime Detective, or tackling hate crime. As the longest-serving Board Chair of SUCCESS, he helped to grow the number of affordable housing units at the organization to 1,000.

Elected as the MLA for Vancouver-Yaletown in 2024, Terry brought a focus on public safety, security and inclusion to public office. In government, he served as the Minister of State for Community Safety and Integrated services, where he worked to protect people by strengthening support for police and tackling repeat offending, retail theft and street disorder.

He also worked closely with residents, businesses and organizations across Vancouver-Yaletown to make sure their voices were heard.

Where the BC Conservatives would roll over for Trump and gut the services people rely on, Terry Yung, David Eby and the BC NDP have a plan to stand up for BC, protect people, and build an economy free from the United States. That plan is making a difference. And we can’t stop now.
Pitch summary: Former VPD officer and SUCCESS board chair, elected in 2024, who served as Minister of State for Community Safety. His page highlights his work on police support, repeat offending, retail theft and street disorder, plus the NDP message against Conservative cuts.
Key priorities: public safety (repeat offenders, retail theft, street disorder); affordable housing; inclusion; stand up to Trump (party message)
Quote: Where the BC Conservatives would roll over for Trump and gut the services people rely on, Terry Yung, David Eby and the BC NDP have a plan to stand up for BC, protect people, and build an economy free from the United States.

Name: Timothy Webster
Pitch summary: Unaffiliated candidate, electrical engineer formerly at the NYSE, Microsoft, Amazon and Meta. His website stresses democratic accountability through an independent anti-corruption commission, competitiveness, high housing costs and investigating health-care challenges.
Key priorities: independent commission against corruption; accountability and transparency; competitiveness and skills training; housing costs; health-care improvements
Quote: My mission is Peace, Order, and good Government.

Name: Kevin Acton
Bio:
Kevin Acton is the Conservative Party of BC candidate for Vernon-Lumby.

Kevin is a civic leader, entrepreneur, and registered massage therapist who has lived in the Vernon-Lumby area since 1991. He brings nearly two decades of local and regional government experience and a practical, community-first approach to public service across Vernon-Lumby.

First elected to Lumby Village Council in 2008, Kevin became Mayor in 2009 and is now serving his fifth term. For 18 years he has represented his community on the Regional District of North Okanagan, which serves municipalities and electoral areas throughout the riding and the wider region. He previously chaired the RDNO Board, currently chairs the North Okanagan/Columbia Shuswap Regional Hospital District, and has served on the board of the Economic Trust of the Southern Interior (ETSI-BC) and as the RDNO representative on the Municipal Finance Authority of British Columbia.

Kevin’s working life is rooted in the region. He has worked as a contractor and builder, served six years as a paramedic with the B.C. Ambulance Service, and for more than 25 years has been an entrepreneur and partner at Bloom Wellness Centre. He is a Registered Massage Therapist and holds an Executive Certificate in Local Government from Dalhousie University and a Level Three Certificate of Excellence in Local Government from the Local Government Leadership Academy.

A proud father and grandfather, Kevin is committed to keeping Vernon-Lumby affordable, safe, and well served.
Pitch summary: Five-term Lumby mayor who ran as an independent in 2024 and is running for mayor and MLA at the same time. He says Eby should not have called the election during local elections and pledges, if he wins both, to personally pay for a Lumby mayoral by-election, under a 'respect the taxpayer' philosophy.
Key priorities: respect the taxpayer; affordability; safety; local government experience; cover by-election cost personally
Quote: One of my philosophies has always been: respect the taxpayer,

Name: Blair Visscher
Pitch summary: No 2026 provincial pitch found. In her 2025 federal Green run she was a UBCO sustainability master's student and substitute teacher who prioritized truly affordable housing, fair taxation and wildfire preparedness.
Key priorities: (2025 federal) affordable housing; fair taxation; wildfire preparedness; jobs and environment together
Quote: I’m here to add choice for people and I’m here to spread the message that I really think we shouldn’t be voting out of fear, we should be voting out of hope.

Name: Robert Johnson
Pitch summary: No individual pitch found.

Name: Harwinder Sandhu
Bio:
An experienced local voice for Vernon and Lumby.

Harwinder Sandhu is an MLA, a community activist, and a longtime Vernon resident. Born to a farm family, and having lived in rural communities across BC, she understands the needs of those communities. As a healthcare worker for over two decades, and as a mother of three, she knows deeply what it means to have a government that is committed to investing in, and strengthening, public healthcare, housing, public and post secondary education, affordable childcare, and the other vital services BC families rely on, as well as taking action to address climate change.

Harwinder’s commitment to public service is inspired by her own personal experience of overcoming hardship. She knows how hard it can be to make ends meet and get by. After being left widowed with 2 toddlers, the experience of being a single, working mother required all her strength. She is a proud mother of three and is inspired by her children every day, both of her daughters are also working in healthcare, and making a difference by helping people in need!

On healthcare, housing, cost of living and all the issues that matter here, you can count on Harwinder Sandhu and David Eby to fight for you.
Pitch summary: Two-term MLA, health-care worker and single mother seeking a third term. She says leadership is about showing up and listening and lists opportunities for families and businesses, health care, housing, child care, water protection and a confident economy.
Key priorities: health care; housing; child care; supporting families and businesses; protecting water and communities; economy
Quote: For me, leadership is not about taking credit. It is about showing up, listening, bringing people together and getting things done with care, dedication, accessibility and integrity.

Name: Chantel Gibbs
Bio:
Born and raised in Vernon, BC, Chantel completed her primary and secondary education locally before attending Trinity Western University, where she earned a B.A. in Business Administration and a B.Sc. in Chemistry. In 2016, she obtained her professional CPA, CGA designation.

After living and working in Vancouver for a number of years, Chantel returned to Vernon in 2024, where she built a home jointly with her sister. She is pleased to be back in her hometown, where much of her extended family continues to live, and remains deeply connected to the Vernon area.

Chantel has been involved in volunteer service through her local church and Toastmasters, and currently serves as a volunteer director with the Canadian National Christian Foundation. Her family also had a longstanding connection to the Vernon community through their business and has supported local organizations, including Vernon Jubilee Hospital and Vernon Search and Rescue, through significant charitable donations.

Chantel is seeking public office as a OneBC candidate. She describes her motivation as providing voters with an alternative to the established political parties and representing truly conservative views openly and consistently throughout the campaign, regardless of the outcome.
Pitch summary: Vernon-born CPA who returned home in 2024. Her bio says she is running to give voters an alternative to the established parties and to represent truly conservative views openly and consistently.
Key priorities: alternative to established parties; conservative values
Quote: She describes her motivation as providing voters with an alternative to the established political parties and representing truly conservative views openly and consistently throughout the campaign, regardless of the outcome.

Name: Joachim Agou
Bio:
Joachim Agou is the Conservative Party of BC candidate for Victoria-Beacon Hill.

Joachim is a professional engineer and small-business owner with more than 15 years of experience in engineering research and industry. Licensed as a P.Eng. in British Columbia and in Newfoundland and Labrador, he helped deliver more than 15 gas turbine test facilities on three continents at MDS Aero in Ottawa, managing multimillion-dollar budgets and schedules, and worked on space robotics at MDA. Today he is a test and evaluation engineer in the defence sector, and he runs a Victoria engineering consulting and media company.
Pitch summary: No individual pitch found. His party bio describes a professional engineer and small-business owner working in defence-sector testing who runs a Victoria engineering consulting and media company.
Other media links: YouTube channel 'JOACHIM AGOU' has personal travel/aerial videos only, not campaign (e.g. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oJF1oHwnDHE)

Name: Rajinder Sahota
Bio:
Raj Sahota was born in Victoria, raised in Esquimalt, and formed his early political views in Saanich. He lives and works on the traditional lands of the Lekwungen and W̱SÁNEĆ peoples. A descendant of Panjabi-Sikhs who resisted British occupation and colonization in Northern India before immigrating to Canada, Raj says his family history has shaped his sense of responsibility toward his community and his decision to run for election.

Growing up in Esquimalt, Raj witnessed and experienced discrimination that inspired him to become an advocate from a young age. He has carried that commitment throughout his career, working to represent people who have been injured, harmed, or treated unfairly and challenging systems he believes contribute to inequality and discrimination.

After attending Esquimalt High School and Belmont Senior Secondary, Raj completed degrees in Commerce and Law at the University of Victoria. He began his legal career in corporate law, including positions at major law firms in Toronto and New York City. His experience working with multinational corporations gave him an inside perspective on the economic, legal, and political systems that he would later choose to challenge through his work.

Raj left corporate law to pursue a Master of Laws in International Law at the London School of Economics, where he studied international law, global economics, and war. He later returned home to Victoria to build a legal career focused on serving individuals and communities.

For nearly two decades, Raj has worked as a litigator and negotiator representing injured, harmed, and vulnerable people. For more than a decade, he has served as the Managing Partner and/or Team Principal of a law firm specializing in personal injury, human rights, and class actions. He has also served for more than a decade on the board of Pacifica Housing Advisory Association, one of B.C.’s non-profit housing and service providers.

Raj is running on priorities that include publicly funded and universally accessible healthcare, education, and transit. He also supports ending public financial support for the fossil fuel industry, multinational corporations, and wealthy individuals.

Outside of his legal and community work, Raj spends much of his time with his children and family. He coaches several youth soccer and basketball teams each week and advocates for a positive, emotionally informed, and youth-centred approach to coaching.

Raj is a proud father and son of Panjabi-Sikh descent, and says he is running in Victoria-Beacon Hill out of a sense of responsibility to the community where he was born and raised.
Pitch video title: Similarities between Trump and Eby policies? A BC Green candidate makes the case #yyj #BCpoli
Pitch summary: Victoria-born personal injury, human rights and class-action litigator and Pacifica Housing board member, running where former Green leader Furstenau lost in 2024. He backs publicly funded, universally accessible health care, education and transit, and ending public financial support for the fossil fuel industry, multinationals and the wealthy.
Key priorities: universal public health care; education; public transit; end subsidies to fossil fuels, multinationals and the wealthy; housing
Quote: Government’s primary job is to care for us, not cater to lobbyists.

Name: Grace Lore
Bio:
Grace Lore: Building a stronger Victoria-Beacon Hill

Grace Lore is a dedicated anti-violence advocate, academic instructor, and researcher focused on standing up for people and making life better for you and your family.

Elected twice to the Legislative Assembly, she has served as Parliamentary Secretary for Gender Equity, Minister of State for Childcare, and the Minister of Children and Family Development.

Grace is committed to the work that the BC NDP has done to stand up for communities and build a stronger province: building more homes, protecting affordable rentals, and hiring more healthcare workers.

Grace Lore, David Eby and the BC NDP have a plan to stand up for British Columbia, protect people and the services they count on, and build a stronger economy and a stronger province.
Pitch summary: Two-term MLA, anti-violence advocate and former Minister of Children and Family Development. Her page says she is committed to the NDP record of building more homes, protecting affordable rentals and hiring more health-care workers.
Key priorities: build more homes; protect affordable rentals; hire more health-care workers; gender equity / anti-violence; child care
Quote: Grace is committed to the work that the BC NDP has done to stand up for communities and build a stronger province: building more homes, protecting affordable rentals, and hiring more healthcare workers.

Name: Tim Taylor
Bio:
Tim Taylor brings decades of hands-on experience in commercial and residential real estate in Victoria as a licensed sales professional, property manager, and strata manager. He’s used that expertise to help create housing at every level, from affordable units to market-rate developments, directly serving the people of this community.

He’s a proven leader and community builder. Tim has chaired the Victoria Real Estate Board’s Commercial Division, served as a founding director of the British Columbia Commercial Council, and sat on the board’s political liaison and finance committees.

For the past twenty years, he’s been deeply involved in housing advocacy: chairman of the Kiwanis Housing Society for Seniors, president of the Victoria West Housing Society for Families in Need, advisor to the Kiwanis House for Women with New Babies, advisor to the Youth Empowerment Society, and a founding director of the CRD Housing Action Team.

He’s also worked alongside several First Nations councils to secure resources addressing the social, cultural, and housing crises their communities face. That work has produced real, measurable progress.

Tim knows this community. He helped build it, served it, and fought for it. He’s ready to bring that same energy to create new exciting opportunities for Victoria Swan Lake.
Pitch summary: Longtime Victoria commercial/residential realtor, property and strata manager and housing-society leader (Kiwanis seniors housing, CRD Housing Action Team). His bio frames him as a community builder who has helped create housing at every level.
Key priorities: housing at every level; community building; First Nations housing partnerships
Quote: He’s ready to bring that same energy to create new exciting opportunities for Victoria Swan Lake.

Name: Carolyn Howe
Bio:
Carolyn Howe is a longtime educator, public education advocate, labour leader, and lifelong Victorian. From her early jobs waiting tables to her career in teaching and her current role as president of the Greater Victoria Teachers’ Association, Carolyn has been driven by a commitment to connecting with people and supporting her community.

Carolyn has taught at South Park Family School since 2005, where she has led an inclusive music program and worked closely with students and families. Her years in the classroom have given her a firsthand view of the pressures many families are facing, including rising costs, food insecurity, housing instability, and the impacts of the toxic drug crisis.

Since 2024, Carolyn has served as president of the Greater Victoria Teachers’ Association, representing local teachers and advocating for strong, well-funded public education. Her work has focused on listening to educators, students, and families and ensuring that the people working directly in schools have a meaningful voice in decisions that affect them.

Carolyn believes that strong communities depend on strong public services. She is running to advocate for affordable and stable housing, accessible healthcare, thriving public schools, economic fairness, and action to protect the climate and the communities people rely on.

She holds degrees in music and education from the University of Victoria and has also built a long record of involvement in the arts. Carolyn is a choral conductor and performer who has worked with groups including the Mood Swing Chorus, Ensemble Laude, and the vocal ensemble Hexaphone.

Carolyn is stepping forward because she believes British Columbians should expect more from their government and that public policy should put the needs of people and communities at the centre of decision-making.
Pitch video title: Policy Announcement: Regulate AI (w/ Sidney Coles, David Evans, Andrew Appleton and Carolyn Howe)
Pitch summary: South Park Family School teacher and president of the Greater Victoria Teachers' Association, announced Sep 28 alongside the Green child-care plan. She says economic inequality is at crisis levels and calls for affordable housing, strong health care, thriving public schools and universal child care.
Key priorities: affordable housing; strong health care; thriving public schools; universal child care; economic fairness; climate action; AI regulation
Quote: From affordable housing to strong healthcare, thriving public schools, and universal childcare—it’s time to raise our expectations for what is possible, and create the province we want to live in.

Name: Nina Krieger
Bio:
Nina Krieger: Standing up for people in Victoria-Swan Lake

Nina Krieger has spent her life standing up for people, as a community leader dedicated to advancing education, justice, and a brighter and more equal future for everyone in British Columbia.

As Minister of Public Safety and Solicitor-General, Nina expanded training opportunities for law enforcement and innovative programs to tackle crime, break cycles of violence and support victims and vulnerable communities.

In her role as Parliamentary Secretary for Arts and Film, Nina advanced opportunities for the South Island's film sector and championed arts and culture in our province.

Before running for public office in 2024, Nina served as Executive Director of Western Canada's leading Holocaust museum, advancing anti-racism education nationally and internationally.

A proven and values-driven leader deeply committed to collaboration, Nina has forged meaningful partnerships with other levels of government and the non-profit, business and philanthropic sectors.

Where the BC Conservatives would cozy up to Donald Trump and cut the services we rely on, Nina Krieger, David Eby and the BC NDP have a plan to stand up for BC, protect the things that matter, and build up our economy.

The plan is working. And we can’t stop now.
Pitch summary: First-term MLA, former Minister of Public Safety and Solicitor General and former Holocaust museum director. Her page highlights law-enforcement training, crime and violence prevention, victim support and South Island film, plus the NDP anti-Conservative message.
Key priorities: public safety and crime prevention; victim support; arts and film sector; stand up to Trump / protect services (party message)
Quote: Where the BC Conservatives would cozy up to Donald Trump and cut the services we rely on, Nina Krieger, David Eby and the BC NDP have a plan to stand up for BC, protect the things that matter, and build up our economy.

Name: Macklin McCall
Bio:
Championing Conservative Values in West Kelowna-Peachland

Macklin McCall is honored to be the Conservative MLA for West Kelowna-Peachland Riding, driven by an unwavering commitment to conservative values and community welfare. With a deep-rooted connection to the Okanagan, Macklin’s journey reflects a lifetime dedicated to service and a profound understanding of our vibrant region.

Community Roots and Values-Driven Upbringing

Having spent his entire life in the Okanagan, with the last 15 years in West Kelowna, Macklin’s ties to the community are profound. Growing up on a family farm in OK Falls instilled in him the values of hard work and community spirit, shaping his character. Pursuing higher education in criminology, psychology, and sociology at OUC in Penticton further fueled his passion for understanding the complexities of society.

Law Enforcement Service and Commitment to Mental Health

As a former RCMP officer with 19 years of service, Macklin has closely served the West Kelowna-Peachland Riding. His experience in addressing mental health challenges firsthand, particularly in a Police and Crisis Team role, highlights the urgent need for effective solutions in British Columbia. His dedication to preserving children’s innocence and upholding parental rights underscores his commitment to community safety.

Economic Advocacy and Housing Solutions

Macklin recognizes the profound impact of economic and housing challenges on the region. Committed to advocating for policies that strengthen the economy, create job opportunities, and ensure accessible housing for all, he aims to address homelessness and support individuals through his work ethic.

Defender of Rights and Freedoms

Macklin’s reverence for the Charter of Rights and Freedoms was cultivated during his tenure in law enforcement, where he diligently protected and upheld these rights. If elected, he pledges to vigorously preserve and protect these rights, ensuring fairness and justice for all.

Deep Community Connection and Dedication to Conservative Values

Having lived in West Kelowna for over a decade and a half, Macklin’s connection to the community is deeply ingrained. His dedication to conservative values and community welfare is resolute, championing these principles faithfully as their representative for the West Kelowna-Peachland Riding.
Pitch summary: First-term MLA and 19-year RCMP veteran. His page and statements stress public safety, mental health and crime (calling BC a cartel transit hub), the economy and housing, parental rights and Charter freedoms; in April 2026 he demanded urgent action on the Trepanier Road encampment.
Key priorities: public safety and crime / catch-and-release; mental health; encampments and wildfire risk; economy and jobs; accessible housing; parental rights; Charter rights
Quote: We need solutions that prioritize safety, protect our forests, and support vulnerable people, and we need them now.

Name: George Morgan
Pitch summary: Recent UBCO mechanical engineering master's graduate and Regional Crime Stoppers director, named Oct 1. In the NDP release he says people feel the pressure of higher costs and want safe communities, pointing to affordability, health care and services.

Name: Caroline Elliott
Bio:
Caroline Elliott is a senior fellow with a leading public policy think tank, a board director of a growing organization advocating a common-sense approach to private property rights and public land use, and a well-known speaker and advocate for British Columbia. 

Caroline has consistently championed a thriving natural resource sector as part of a strong, private sector-driven economy that benefits all citizens. She holds a PhD in Political Science from Simon Fraser University, specializing in Canadian liberal democracy as it relates to Indigenous self-governance, and previously taught B.C. politics at SFU.

Earlier in her career, Caroline worked at the B.C. Legislature under the Gordon Campbell government, advising the Minister of Transportation and later the Minister of Environment. She has also built a policy consulting business serving a wide range of clients seeking to invest in B.C., from the energy and forestry sectors to major infrastructure projects. A lifelong British Columbian, Caroline grew up in Surrey with her three brothers and two sisters. She now lives in North Vancouver with her husband and their two young children.
Pitch summary: Think-tank senior fellow with an SFU political science PhD who narrowly lost the May 2026 Conservative leadership race; she replaces MLA Lynne Block in this safe right-of-centre seat. Her bio stresses a resource-driven private-sector economy and private property rights, and North Shore News says her leadership campaign focused on walking back NDP reconciliation initiatives.
Key priorities: private property rights vs Indigenous land claims; strong natural resource sector; private-sector-driven economy; party unity under Doerkson
Quote: I'm proud to run under the Conservative banner, and I'm honoured to run under Lorne Doerkson's leadership,

Name: Arwa Shurab
Bio:
Arwa Shurab is a leadership coach, community organizer, speaker, trainer and North Shore resident whose work focuses on community leadership, inclusion, engagement and helping people feel heard and represented.

She holds a Master’s degree in Global Leadership from Royal Roads University, with a focus on systems thinking, collaboration and leadership in complex environments. She is also a certified and master-certified life coach with experience in leadership development, public speaking and community engagement.

Arwa is the founder of HERVOICE, an initiative that supports women through leadership development and community-based learning. She is also a co-founder of BC Muslim & Arab Professionals and serves as a board director with the North Shore Restorative Justice Society.

Through her professional and community work, Arwa has helped build organizations, strengthen connections across communities and support people navigating complex systems. She has also worked with community and professional organizations on anti-racism, inclusion, belonging and institutional understanding.

As a mother and North Shore resident, Arwa believes leadership starts with listening. She wants public life to be more accessible, honest and responsive to the people it serves, with a focus on practical solutions and meaningful community engagement.

Arwa is running in North Vancouver-Seymour to bring her experience in leadership, community building and inclusion into public service and to help ensure local voices are heard in the decisions that affect their lives.
Pitch summary: North Shore leadership coach, HERVOICE founder and BC Muslim & Arab Professionals co-founder. Her bio says leadership starts with listening and she wants public life to be more accessible, honest and responsive, with practical solutions and real community engagement.
Key priorities: listening and community engagement; accessible, honest government; inclusion and anti-racism; practical solutions
Quote: You can’t lead people you don’t listen to.

Name: Honieh Barzegari
Bio:
Standing up for people in West Vancouver-Capilano

Honieh Barzegari is a Canadian woman of Iranian origin, physician by training, and strategic leader with more than 20 years of experience spanning medicine, healthcare, life sciences, health technology, business, public policy, government, and governance. She began her career practising medicine in rural communities in Iran, serving underserved populations and seeing firsthand the challenges people face in accessing healthcare and essential services.

After moving to Canada, Honieh built a career at the intersection of healthcare, technology, and business, gaining a practical understanding of innovation, investment, and economic opportunity. She also served as a Ministerial Advisor with the Government of British Columbia, giving her firsthand experience of how government policy affects communities and businesses.

Honieh currently serves on the Langara College Board of Governors and co-chairs KPU’s Health and Science Committee. She brings the perspective of a physician, immigrant, business and healthcare leader, and government advisor, with a commitment to accessible healthcare, innovation, economic opportunity, and practical public service.

Honieh Barzegari, David Eby and the BC NDP have a plan to build BC strong: to create jobs, to protect healthcare, and to make life more affordable.
Pitch summary: Iranian-born physician by training, former BC ministerial advisor and health/life-sciences executive (Earnscliffe). Her page pitches accessible health care, innovation and economic opportunity, with the NDP plan to create jobs, protect health care and make life affordable.
Key priorities: accessible health care; innovation and economic opportunity; jobs; affordability (party message)
Quote: Honieh Barzegari, David Eby and the BC NDP have a plan to build BC strong: to create jobs, to protect healthcare, and to make life more affordable.

Name: Naomi Chocyk
Pitch summary: No provincial pitch found. She is also running for Vancouver city council and school trustee with TrueBlue Vancouver; her municipal site pledges affordability through disciplined spending, restoring public safety, accountability and putting students and learning first.
Key priorities: (municipal campaign) affordability / disciplined spending; public safety; accountability; students and learning first; parental involvement
Quote: People should be able to look at City Hall and the School Board and know exactly who they work for: you.

Name: Dan Wood
Bio:
Dan Wood is a real estate and leasing professional with experience in public-sector housing, commercial real estate, facilities, and business continuity. He works with a government organization in British Columbia on leases, licence agreements, due diligence, property matters, and relationships with property owners, brokers, legal counsel, and government partners.

Dan’s background includes work in commercial real estate research, facilities management, occupational health and safety, and emergency planning. Dan holds an M.A. from UBC and brings a practical, policy-focused approach to communications, with an emphasis on clarity, affordability, and issues that matter to British Columbians.
Pitch summary: BC Housing property agent pitching CentreBC as the riding's middle ground. He wants regional transit and Highway 99 safety in the capital plan with firm dates, workforce and prefab housing, a staged-opening Squamish long-term care home, and DRIPA tweaked rather than repealed.
Key priorities: regional transit with deadlines; Highway 99 safety; workforce housing and prefab builds; publish public land data; Squamish long-term care home; travelling specialists and virtual care; finish treaties, amend (not repeal) DRIPA
Quote: I don’t think we split the vote on the right or on the left … we are the vote, and the other parties are the ones that are actually splitting the vote,

Name: Ayla Dumais
Bio:
Ayla Dumais was raised in Squamish, BC and is a proud member of Prophet River First Nation.

Ayla has built her career in public policy, stakeholder relations and Indigenous affairs. She currently works in the Office of the Leader of the Official Opposition as a Policy and Stakeholder Relations Advisor, where she has worked across files including Indigenous relations, property rights natural resources, the environment, economic development, youth, and more. Her work has brought her together with constituents, Indigenous leaders, businesses, industry, advocacy organizations, and community leaders across British Columbia and Canada.

Before entering the public policy field, Ayla worked in community relations with Woodfibre LNG in Squamish, where she gained firsthand experience with the opportunities that responsible resource development and strong relationships with local and Indigenous communities can bring to British Columbia.

For Ayla, this campaign is about being a voice for the next generation of British Columbians who worry about their ability to stay in this beautiful province. She will be a strong voice for West Vancouver–Sea to Sky in defense of property rights, affordability, healthcare, and education.
Pitch summary: Squamish-raised Prophet River First Nation member, Opposition leader's office policy advisor and former Woodfibre LNG community relations staffer. Her bio says the campaign is about the next generation who worry they can't afford to stay, and lists property rights, affordability, health care and education.
Key priorities: property rights; affordability; health care; education; responsible resource development
Quote: For Ayla, this campaign is about being a voice for the next generation of British Columbians who worry about their ability to stay in this beautiful province.

Name: Jeremy Valeriote
Bio:
Jeremy Valeriote was elected as the MLA for West Vancouver–Sea to Sky in 2024, and made history as the first BC Green elected on the BC mainland. With a background in environmental consulting and local government, Jeremy has spent decades advocating for sustainable communities and responsible public policy. In his public role, Jeremy has made regional transportation and the Sea to Sky’s affordability crisis key priorities, advocating for reliable, expanded transit connecting communities from Vancouver to Lil’wat, an end to fuel price gouging, non-market housing and long-term care beds, and securing Heart & Hearth program funding and Foundry centres. He has also been a strong voice against fossil fuel expansion and public subsidy , challenging the environmental impacts, public costs, and long-term risks of projects like Woodfibre LNG, in favour of cleaner, future-facing economic development.

Jeremy previously served as a Councillor for the Town of Gibsons, where he championed active transportation, public transit, natural asset management, and environmental stewardship. He holds an engineering degree and a Master’s in leadership studies from Royal Roads University.
Pitch summary: First mainland BC Green MLA (2024), former Gibsons councillor and environmental consultant. He says he has stood up for priorities government ignores (regional transit, passenger rail, highway safety, protected farmland) and also backs non-market housing, long-term care beds, ending fuel price gouging and opposing Woodfibre LNG subsidies.
Key priorities: regional transit and passenger rail; Highway 99 safety; protected farmland; non-market housing; long-term care beds; end fuel price gouging; oppose fossil fuel expansion / Woodfibre LNG subsidies
Quote: I’ve spent the last two years standing up for the priorities of the people of West Vancouver-Sea-to-Sky that the government too often ignores, including regional transit, passenger rail, highway safety, and protected farmland.

Name: Michelle Livaja
Pitch summary: Bowen Island resident who works in the Infrastructure minister's office, a former constituency assistant and union activist; she ran here for the NDP in 2017. The party lists her priorities as health care, cost of living and responding to the U.S. trade war.
Key priorities: health care; cost of living; respond to U.S. trade war / tariffs; infrastructure
Quote: These tariffs are designed to hurt us – but David Eby and the BC NDP won't back down. We're standing up for B.C., protecting families, and building the infrastructure we need to grow and diversify B.C.'s economy. We can't afford to stop now,
